I gave this game time to mature before I reviewed it, since it was early access when I bought it two years ago. It's two years later and I'm really dissapointed in how this game turned out. The level design is terrible. There are long stretches of nothing but collecting gems, and then some enemies thrown in that are way too easy. The placement of the platforms just seems slapdash. Like they were put there, not out of a necessity for your character to progress, but just for the sake of being there. The controls feel off as well. Everything is slippery and your character moves waaaaayyyy to fast. Did I mention the music? It's a horrible, ear-grating cacophony. It's possibly the worst thing about the game, and that's saying something. It's not all bad. The 2d graphics and retro aesthetic look great. That was really the only reason I bought the game in the first place. This game and DayZ were the two games that put me off of buying Early Access games for life.

A short and enjoyable dramatic adventure. I feel like I just played through an audio book with really great voice actors. This is as linear as first person game gets but it doesn't often feel like it while you're playing. The direction is blunt but soft. The music is rare but adds a necessary element when it plays. The sounds are decent and just this side of believable.
Stephen King wrote in his book "On Writing" that you don't want to tell your readers everything or give them too much. Being a little vague allows each reader to insert their own impressions which allows for a greater sense of immersion. I think, somehow, the looks and sounds and gameplay of Firewatch has adapted this quality to the game while the voice acting carries you along the way.
If you've ever been camping, used a radio, been in casual isolation, or been in or around a wildland fire this game will use those memories; I could almost taste the heat and dirt and dry blasted wind in the back of my throat when I was walking around late game.
Catch this game on a Steam sale and you won't regret it (great game to Gift someone, too). Full price (currently $20), might be a bit much at this date due to some of the dated animations and visuals. That said: 90% of this game is in the environment and story telling by the voice actors. Your experience won't be robbed by the dated visuals.

That said, it was done very, VERY well. Gameplay was solid, acting was fantastic, how it played out was excellent.
But if you were expecting something WAY dramatic, thriller, or mystery-like, keep looking. This is a far more quiet, simple story. Very down-to-earth.

Firewatch is a highly-overrated walking simulator.  It is still worth a playthough, and I am clicking on "recommended," but I wouldn't pay full price.  For one thing, there is only about 6 hours of content here, and that is doing a lot of extra exploration.  It can easily be finished in 4, and there are no alternate endings or storylines to pursue.  I doubt many people come back for round two.
If you are going to make a game in which the only gameplay is walking around and making dialog choices, the story had better be pretty good. And IMHO, this story is mediocre.
MORE ABOUT THE STORY   * MILD SPOILERS *
When the story first gets going, it seems to be leading to something big.  There seems to be a creepy government experiment going on with you as the main subject. There is a budding romance with a mysterious woman on the other end of a radio.
But in the end, be ready to be a bit disappointed.  When you solve the mystery and leave, everything seems to be a tad mundane and anti-climactic.
The game seemed to have a lot of potential, but in the end fell a bit flat.  6/10.  Buy it on sale.

This is one of the best first person shooter games I've ever played, plain and simple.
Sven Co-op is a fun and addictive goldsrc game packing a lot of fun, it begins during the Black Mesa incident, that of course if you decide to play the Half Life campaign. There are plenty of maps to play on other than the Half Life story.
Sven Co-op is at this point one of the oldest received and best games and I'm sure pretty much everyone has played it. If not, well what the hell are you doing reading this review? You need install this game straight away and play it right now.
The game is a simple first person shooter, but it does plenty things different than the regular first person shooters. You have a health bar and you have to do platforming to solve some of the puzzles. Not to mention the the graphic engine is rather old, it's still doing quite well.
For a game that came out back in 1999 it still looks amazing. Now while it does have so low res textures it still looks decent and I experienced zero problems while playing the game. This game runs really well and should run on pretty much all systems.
The game for the most part is pretty easy. I played through the game without a problem, even though some segments were tough due to the fast movement you have to pull off to avoid gunfire. Not to mention the Xen battles are incredibly intense and quite difficult.
Apart from the Sven Co-op maps, the Half Life campaign doesn't provide any replayability. There is enough user created content to keep you interested and the game is updated frequently
In the end Sven Co-op is a fantastic game. It's a must play for everyone who is a gamer. This game is a piece of history and without a doubt one of the best games I have ever played in my entire life.
9.5/10 - A must play

Although I believe magicka 2 is a fun and challenging game on its own (especially with friends) it seems to fall a little flat compared to Magicka 1.
The pros
-Better graphics, shiny, optimized
-Multiplayer is smooth, no crashes, disconnects bugs
-Hotbar for quickcasting magicks you don't want to memorize
-Casting spells on the move
-an Inventory like system that allows you to choose weapons/robes
However, I believe the game is getting quite a few negative reviews because it just lacks the content of the first game. The main issue for me personally was this artificial skill ceiling created by cooldown on your magicks. In the first game you could play for hours and hours and constantly be getting better and more skilled, able to chain complex magicks extremely fast. In Magicka 2... Usually you are capped out at casting no more than 2 at a time, the reason is there is a 2 secondish cooldown on any magicks you manually cast and that includes ALL of your magicks, and as far as i know, there isn't a way to turn that off. You could say this is a good thing, it creates more challenging play, critical thinking, and balance. However... all those are ruined by the introduction of Steam... Steam is incredibly overpowered and there are hardly any enemies resistant to it in the campaign. I played through hard in a few hours with a buddy and all we had to do was spam steam/lightning/arcane to win.
Now i'm not talking slightly overpowered... this is coming from someone who has spent hundreds of hours in magicka 2, my buddy who had only played a few hours, was literally better than me because he chose to spam the steam spells and i was trying out magicks and throwing out a variety. There is also less content, no multiplayer arena battles, the challenges are the same a bit lackluster, lack of maps, less magicks that are more (balanced) as in nothing too complex and overpowering.

Overall Coming from someone who spent over 100 hours in magicka 1, i would give the game a 6/10  It is a fun game itself but pales in comparison to the content and mastery achieved by the first game.

---Addendum---
It's been a while since I've played Magicka 2 last...and I've played it less than thirty hours...I guess I lost interest in Magicka 2 really fast. That caught me by surprise.
As it turns out, I had applauded Magicka 2 for making experimental spellcasting more enticing by removing power-combos, but in reality experimental spellcasting had actually been made less viable in Magicka 2 than it was in Magicka. Enemies are simply too aggressive; they descend on players too fast to make anything but the most efficient and effective spell combos have sufficient impact. This is especially true on anything higher than normal difficulty, when enemy health regeneration comes into effect -- they're either killed instantly or recover as the next spell is prepared.
Perhaps even more greviously, enemy variety is simply poor. A grand majority of the enemies you'll fight will be the same type you fight for the entire level. On top of that, enemy types are also recycled over several levels. Enemies are tiresome to face instead of exciting, and that's never a good sign for a game.
Combine those two together, and the game becomes a chore after one, maybe two playthroughs.
Maybe DLC is worth it, but...
I'm changing my recommendation.
---Original Review---
This game gets mixed reviews for good reason. It is, in general, a very good game, but the changes made going into Magicka 2 ended up cannibalizing some of the things that made the original Magicka so unique and popular in the first place.
For veterans of Magicka, there's two big differences between the first game and Magicka 2: Magicka 2 is faster paced, and balanced. Enemies move faster, close in from more angles, and tank more damage. Magicks have a cooldown (yes, even when using the elemental combination instead of the new quick-cast), and the power spells from Magicka don't have the oompf they had anymore. In return, we, the wizards, are also made far more mobile -- we can move while sustaining spells, and none of the magicks lock us in place for several seconds. The days of sitting in one spot and spamming awesome magicks like Lightning Bolt stay in the first Magicka.
To some people -- myself included -- this was actually a very good development. I really, really liked the spellcasting mechanics from Magicka, and I liked calling up different elements and experimenting with combinations. However, I found it discouraging that certain combinations (steam + steam + arcane + lightning + lightning) were clearly overpowered and could sweep through the entire game. The new balance in Magicka 2 makes most all spell combos powerful in one area, but near-useless in others. It rewards players who experiment frequently -- I like that.
However, the Ying-to-the-Yang here is that, a lot of the charm of Magicka was how absurdly powerful we were as wizards. Enemies did piddling damage, and died quicker and in greater numbers than we did; there were few points in the game, aside from boss battles, where AI enemies were legitimate threats. Rather, Magicka was balanced around how spells didn't discriminate between caster and target, and killing ourselves was just as easy. Heck, that was the biggest defining feature of Magicka -- the biggest threat is ourselves and our friends. That's gone; in Magicka 2, enemies don't just die helplessly in waves anymore. They're dangerous from the early chapters, and will kill us just as easily as ourselves. Some people might enjoy the extra challenge, but I'm sure as many people enjoyed the juxtaposition between ourselves and the mostly-harmless world of Magicka.
Also, yes, Magicka 2 isn't nearly as funny as the original. The land of Midgard in Magicka 2 lacks any of the special details that Magicka so lovingly put in -- tongue-in-cheek humor is replaced by straight-faced presentation, and subtle nods to pop-culture are replaced with blatant "Hay i maed a jok e" attempts at references. Top that off with how the balanced spell system prevents those crazy, outlandish moments that only a backfiring uber-spell (or a bug) can provide. The humor in Magicka 2 took a definite hit, and unlike the spell balance, there wasn't really a trade-off -- it's just lesser.
Another thing of worthwhile note, is that currently (Late November 2015), the number and range of effects from robes, staves, and weapons is minimal. This might change later with DLC, but right now, all the special stat effects are at tame, safe levels.
In the end, then, Magicka 2 comes down to the spellcasting mechanic. If you liked its potential in Magicka, you'll probably love the work done to expand spellcasting in Magicka 2. If it was rather the laugh-out-loud moments that kept you playing Magicka, either through the satirical humor or the variety of absurd baubles and booms...I would wager that, yes, you will end up being disappointed.
Myself, I do enjoy Magicka 2. Even in single-player, I found Magicka's unique spellcasting system too much fun, and the enhanced balance in Magicka 2 gives me even more reason to play around with it some more.

The short review is: Horrible music. Good mechinics from what I could tell, but the menues and controller assignments are glitchy and we couldn't even manage to play multiple with 2 xbox 360 controllers.
As it is right now, I was very disapointed with my purchase, even though i only paid 3 dollers for the game, and that says something in and of itself. The main reason for this is both the incomplete glitchyness of the game, and the music.
I have never before been detered by a games music before, but this time I honestly cannot bring myself to try the game again because of the music. Music in a game is very important to me. It helps set the pace, setting, etc, and it seems this music was going for a sort of fast pace by using a repeatative jumble of notes in all cases. However it sounds horrible. This may be highly opinionated, but I am honestly shocked I don't see comments on this music. Sure, you can set the music to your own music, but thats not really valid excuse. The majority of the time i played was muted.
I even had a firend over to try the multiplayer. We start off by plugging in reguler xbox 360 wired controllers. Should be the baseline for compatibility standards, so how could it go wrong? Well, it comes in as two different things, a gamepad AND a joypad.
After messing around, we got both players set to gamepad, but when we went to play, it switched us back to the joypad and all controls were messed up again. Then when trying to select characters, it was switching color pallets and maybe some other video settings because it was looking weird. We gave up and played a different game.
One could certainly assume that this would be better on release, but who knows when that will be. No updates in over 2 months. Early access should not be an excuse to not finish development, but its happened before. Right now just about everything is un-finished and more than a little broken.
I have been watching and waiting for this game to get out of early access for a while because I usually like action platformers like this one, but I hate this early access business. In far too many cases it leads to disapointemnt, however, I felt it worth 3 dollers at the time so I broke down and bought it. I am now even more adament about never buying early access games.

A high octane platform game that has a lot of potential to become one of the contenders of the most memorable indie games (at least in my case).
While the menu might seem confusing the first time you try it, the gameplay itself is very intuitive and easy to learn (although there's the tutorial if you need special info, because on the first time i had trouble with charging) and also it provides you with a lot of speed in combat and in platforming.
The game requires you to maneuver through the stages using your motor lance in order to achieve high scores or quick times. The combat is fun yet very exploitable one you learn how to counter attack, and the boss battles are fun, interesting and will test your skills.
The graphics are pretty much your standard 8 bit game, however this one is more focused on game boy aesthetics, but if you're bothered by that you can always choose DX mode for a more colorful experience.
The music is interesting, but I persnally have heard better songs, but you can choose your own music on the menus, which is always a +.
Overrall if you're into challenging platformers, 8 bit styled games, or high octane games, this is the game for you and I highly recommend it.

This video capture software is straightforward in its basic operation and does as advertised.
It will-
Record your entire session
Record your Mic as well as others chatting via in game com's  or over Steam calls
Record in optimal resolutions that you choose in the menu or not record the voice/com's based on your options and preferences.
Over all I am quite satisfied with the performance and overall quality of the videos that come from this software. Some games do record at a better quality than others, but the loss is so marginal that it will not hinder the overall presentation of your video. The sound is recorded in full stereo and without any noticeable volume drops or interference.
Now, there are a few small issues that I have come across. When updates come out is is possible that the location of your saved videos will revert back to your main drive (C:\) rather than the one you designated, but a simple fix.
At random times for no reason the recording will stop with no input from the user. It just stops... The recording is saved but if you did not notice it stop you will keep going thinking everything is fine and dandy. This usually happens when stating a game or switching a game when the software was running in the background.
The on screen menu/status bar seems to disappear while ingame and recording. the recording does NOT pick up the status bar but it helps the user to know if it is recording, paused or stopped. Again if you are recording and the bar disappears IT DOES RECORD and save to the folder selected.
I also  had an issue with voice quality when recording (coms/chat) being grainy and distant, but that was an audio option I found and corrected.
Over all I am quite pleased with this software and do suggest it for anything you may need it for. Watch your recordings because these files get BIG QUICK and is real easy to get carried away and have a 7 gig 1080p video now sucking up your HDD space!
Notes: I would like to see a better option menu/settings. There is a voice that tells you when you record and when you stop. But its either on or off a volume control for said voice would be perfect! I also want to see more optimized support for other games. Eg: Star Wars the Old Republic is grainy and less refined than recording Terraria. Why? Not sure just is.
Love it tho and would by again if needed.

Sniper Elite: Spooky Skeleton Army, and it's sequel, Rise of the Skeleton Lord, chronicle the true events of Adolf Hitler's rise to power over the skeleton army during the Fall of Berlin in World War II. Rebellion Developments took their time painstakingly recreating real-life locales and events in which the Bone Battles of Berlin took place. Skeleton warriors rattle and shake as they attempt to prevent the Allies from stealing all of their gold and dairy products, the sources of their skeleton powers. This hyper-realistic simulation game isn't without its flaws and inaccuracies, however. For instance, alongside the teeming skeleton hordes that haunt and spook the German villas and countrysides, you'll often encounter groups of undead Wehrmacht soldiers lumbering around. While there were indeed Nazis occupying the area at the time, any historian worth his salt will tell you that zombies weren't deployed in battle until the Korean War. They were more than likely added for gameplay reasons, as battling only skeletons would be far too difficult or frightening for any reasonable player. Overall the game is a fun, realistic, and enlightening depiction of some of the lesser-known events of World War II, and well worth the $15 price tag.

"Firewatch, a game that brings something fresh with visuals, flawless voice acting, ambience and immersion to the table. But falls short with an unsatisfying ending, repetetive gameplay and singleplayer that's way too short."
Firewatch is a game that's great for players who want to try something new, inspiring and beautiful. The controls and the graphics are stunning and I couldn't stop taking F12 screenshots (yes I love the design). The controls are solid, even on the dualshock 4 controllers. However, the voice acting is flawless and it really drives the sensation of "human" forward. It isn't an overthetop game that tries to change your life and therefore it exceeds in the way you feel connected to the protagonist and his friend.
The first half of the game is strong and sets up many ideas, the shift between immersion and ambience quickly turns into paranoia and psychologic. However, the second half is weak in many aspects and the ending is so anticlimatic that you'll end up with the question, "but why?"
If you don't pay attention to certain dialogues the ending will feel way too rushed and confusing. The story is 5 hours at max and most of the missions can be completed in minutes. Free roam does serve a real purpose except for a few easter eggs and achievements. No bugs/crashes encountered in my playthrough.
I only recommend this game for people who wants to take a break from competetive/machine-hungry/unrealistic/AAA games and just want to play a game that sets you into a beautiful game with a beautiful world  (Im a sucker for forest missions in games etc) and soundtrack. This is not a game for someone who wants an life changing story because you will feel dissapointed in the end.
This game does NOT deserve to cost 19,99 eur. I got this game during steam sale (7,99) which is an OK price.
PROS:
- No bugs, glitches, crashes
- Doesn't require a massive rig
- Voice acting is <3
- Visuals
- Soundtrack
- Immersion
- Gameplay, during the first half
CONS:
- Too short
- second half feels rushed, uninspiring and boring
- The ending anticlimatic
- After first half the gameplay becomes repetetive
- Price, should cost 7eur or 5 for a SINGLEPLAYER GAME that short
- Free Roam doesn't award you or bring anything fun in terms of gameplay, it's only there for visuals.
Verdict 7/10

Star Wars: Republic Commando is quite possibly the most fun game I have ever played...no exaggeration.
Republic Commando is a FPS that was released back in 2005 but stills holds up today as an extremely fun game. In the game, you play as RC-1138, AKA 'Boss', who is the...well...BOSS of an elite clone commando squad known as Delta Squad. You have 3 squadmates: Scorch, the munitions expert, Fixer, the computer slicer, and Sev, the sniper. The 4 of you go on many, many missions across the galaxy and basically destroy everyone in your path.
The mechanics of the game are surprisingly smooth and it's easy to get the hang of. You know how to aim at things? You're all good. This game is so worth it for the price not only because of how fun it is, but because of the length of the campaign. I think we've all bought a game and had fun with it but were left short-handed because of how small the campaign was. No worrying about that with this game. You get a blaster rifle, a sniper, shotgun, pistol, grenades, and even a grenade launcher to blow your enemies to hell all while your squad mates are bantering with each other...which is probably one of the best parts of the game.
TL;DR Here is a pros and cons list
PROS
-Good amount of content
-Smooth mechanics
-Squad banter
-Good graphics for its release date
-No extra BS. You shoot things.
CONS
-There isn't a sequel.......YET.

Magicka 2 has been updated, and people that enjoyed the original are now much more likely to enjoy it.
When Magicka 2 was first released we were greeted with a spell creation system that had been gutted in the name of balanced player versus player combat; something I, and apparently a lot of other people, don't care about in a Magicka game.  People that
care about that were probably already playing
, and not interested in another story-driven game.  That would explain all the bad reviews this game has gotten.
The developers have since fully corrected their mistake, and deserve credit for that.  Developers fixing their bad game
(as opposed to bad code) is almost unheard of in the industry.  It would be nice to see more of that.
The Good:
The spell creation system now has all the original elements, along with the new Poison element.  Most remaining differences (like being able to walk while casting) seem to be improvements.  I now enjoy the gameplay more than the original.
The voice acting and silly atmosphere is just as good as the original.
The special effects associated with spells look much better than in the original.
The Bad:
The first thing the player is greeted with after installation is the requirement to create or enter login information for a Paradox Interactive account, or be unable to play online.  I'm sure this didn't help the ratings any.  The justification, that Magicka 2 owners might receive rewards in
, was extremely weak.  I already have a Steam account that is perfectly adequate for lobby service.  I wish companies would stop thinking they are so special that they should contribute to everyone's account proliferation problems.  I really,
, don't need to have yet another username and password to remember when it's time to upgrade my computer.
The only thing I miss from the original spell creation system is the ability to push with water beams.  It would probably be most reasonable to simply add that effect to the Poison and Life Water beams.  Enemies that benefit from being poisoned (undead) are usually harmed by healing, so this shouldn't cause problems.
Difficulty is not scaled based on the number of players, and is clearly balanced with 4 skilled players in mind.  It is often frustrating in multiplayer, and is almost impossible to play solo.  The original Magicka had this problem in some of its DLC (most notably
).  Since feeling frustrated and laughing are usually mutually exclusive, this does a lot to harm the humorous atmosphere.  I play Magicka for the spell creation system and humor, not the challenge.
Magicka 2 is shorter than the original.  Perhaps DLC will improve this, but given the damage the original design did to sales, and the damage over time the bad ratings are doing to sales, I wonder if Paradox Interactive will consider it worthwhile to develop much DLC.
I don't like the soundtrack as much as the original.  It is in no way
.  I like it more than most games' soundtracks.  It just doesn't feel as memorable as the original.

Delightful game. I've never played the first one, so no comparisons with that from me. Apparently there was some grumbling over certain spell combos (water + fire = steam) not working in M2, but that's been fixed, and a new combo for poison was added to boot. The graphics are on the very pretty side of cartoony, and the whole game is clearly tongue-in-cheek. The humor didn't always have me slapping my knees, but it's very charming, from the pervasive nods to pop culture   ("A massive cold front is coming," says John Frost) to the option of giving your character a voice set called "Arnold" that sounds a lot like Will Sasso spoofing Schwarzenegger on Mad TV, and, last but certainly not least, the hilarious gibberish spoken by the NPCs. It sounds a lot more spirited than Simlish, and I'm ashamed to admit that I briefly thought it was Swedish.
The main draw here is obviously the clever and addictive experimenting with sheer endless combinations of various elements, which you can then unleash on your enemies (and on yourself, for better or for worse) in a number of different ways: as good old-fashioned rays and sprays, branching charges, weapon enchantments, area blasts, mines, and more. Want a fiery death ray that arcs to several foes at once, like lightning? You got it.
If the game has a drawback, it's that it's pretty damn hard, at least in solo mode. Magicka 2 was intended as a multiplayer experience, of course, and although the single player difficulty has been dialed down a bit in recent patches, later enemies come in such overwhelming numbers, to say nothing of certain bosses, that even the most adroit keyboard wizard will be hard put to survive without some assistance. Fortunately, it's easy to call in other aspiring mages. And even though they can do each other as much harm as the swarming monsters (friendly fire is always on), frustration is kept at bay through the sheer zaniness of the chaotic battles. It's a rather unique game, and comes at a very decent price, too—definitely a winner in my book.

Imagine you are stuck on a planet all alone. How can you possible get off that rock and back home within your lifetime... 1. Build a Rocket 2. Work Smarter Not Harder.

I recommend this game. It's fast, fun, and action-packed. It has a graphical style similar to the recently popular Shovel Knight. But after only playing thru the tutorial and 2 levels, it currently has frustrating issues which I hope get addressed before it comes out of early access:
My computer exceeds all the recommended settings with 4GB of RAM, 2.13GHz processor, and a DirectX 9 capable graphics card, yet it lags on levels outside of the tutorial. Taking the game out of fullscreen seems to help a bit, but I'm unsure why. I'm not sure if it's an instancing problem or what, but I can't understand how a pixelated retro style game can be lagging on my computer even with most of the special effects turned off.
There appears to be a graphical glich(es) where portraits don't show anything except a solid color, signs don't have any text, and doors are replaced by solid black boxes on the buildings.
Why is the jump button an input for any of the character's attacks when we have a dedicated attack button? I use a joystick on my controller, so I'm often pressing both Up and Right, or Down and Left, etc. This causes the shortcut for the Drill Uppercut move to often trigger when all I wanted was to simply jump. Which sucks since it uses up some of my Speed charges.
Speaking of Speed charges, why does the basic attack go thru a full combo with a single button press, thereby consuming all my Speed charges? Additionally, when trying to use the attacks to help platforming, using all 3 charges consecutively and flinging myself over the platform I'm trying to land on is extremely annoying. I'm fine with pressing the attack button 3 times in a row when I want 3 attacks in a row. I'm not fine attacking 3 times when I only wanted to attack once.
And lastly, outside of the tutorial level, charging up the Speed bar takes noticably longer not even accounting for the lag mentioned above. Some consistency would be nice. I was about to throw down my controller in frustration until I noticed that spamming the attack button while holding Down charges faster. Brilliant! I like it! It feels good! But why wasn't this explained in the tutorial? The only notion I got was that I needed to hold the attack button, not spam it.
This is more of a nice to have, quality of life/game feel, thing, but why can't I Uppercut in mid air? It consumes a Speed charge, so I can't do it indefinitely and abuse it to kingdom come. After many years of playing Super Smash Bros, doing an up attack move mid-air that flings the character skyward feels like the most natural thing in the gaming world. Maybe make it less effective mid-air to balance it out? Regardless, I'd really like to have this ability.

To be honest, I've never expected that much from MMORPG developers trying to make single player sandbox community-building zombie survival game. Endlessly respawning zombies, poor AI, shallow story and primitive gameplay were inevitable, but there's more to it that could've been done right.
In the end, there are two points of view: as an xbox console game, even with all of it's flaws and drawbacks, it's a masterpiece not because it's good, but because there is no better alternative. As a PC gaming product, however, it can be described with a single word: mess. Literally none of the game's systems are working good enough. It's been nearly 2 years since original release and it didn't get any better.
You can build yourself a base of your liking but there are facilities that are essential to build and those that have completely negligible effects so there is never a choice. On a first glance your people seem to be a community but after a few days you realise that they're just a bunch of drones: they don't establish friend/enemy/couple relationships, events about fights, jealousy or interpersonal dislike are completely random and random community members are 'picked' to participate, when a community member dies two random members will get a morale hit etc so both base and community building aspects are a mess too.
What there remains? Hoarding? Your base stash has only 255 slots, so eventually you'll have to waste your time clearing it out every game day or two. Spent two hours gathering supplies to train your characters next day? Too bad, they got overwritten by your facilities' daily output and you have 5 items instead of 105. Character progression? Your favourites will get killed through a wall, when all floor two zombies fall through the ceiling while you're clearing first floor and tear you apart or your car turns over near two zombie hordes because someone inside farted.
In the end I can only recommend it as a cheap and glitchy Dead Rising substitute. However you probably should play Dead Rising itself instead.
P.S. Imagine yourself a grown up person that claims to be a skilled game developer. This person spends half an hour trying to get inside a blue public restroom and finally pisses oneself just because of being unable to realise that door opens outwards, not inwards. Pathetic? Definitely. Funny? Star Wars: Republic Commando is quite possibly the most fun game I have ever played...no exaggeration.
Republic Commando is a FPS that was released back in 2005 but stills holds up today as an extremely fun game. In the game, you play as RC-1138, AKA 'Boss', who is the...well...BOSS of an elite clone commando squad known as Delta Squad. You have 3 squadmates: Scorch, the munitions expert, Fixer, the computer slicer, and Sev, the sniper. The 4 of you go on many, many missions across the galaxy and basically destroy everyone in your path.
The mechanics of the game are surprisingly smooth and it's easy to get the hang of. You know how to aim at things? You're all good. This game is so worth it for the price not only because of how fun it is, but because of the length of the campaign. I think we've all bought a game and had fun with it but were left short-handed because of how small the campaign was. No worrying about that with this game. You get a blaster rifle, a sniper, shotgun, pistol, grenades, and even a grenade launcher to blow your enemies to hell all while your squad mates are bantering with each other...which is probably one of the best parts of the game.
TL;DR Here is a pros and cons list
PROS
-Good amount of content
-Smooth mechanics
-Squad banter
-Good graphics for its release date
-No extra BS. You shoot things.
CONS
-There isn't a sequel.......YET.

I've been meaning to learn RISK for a while. It was always one of those games that I saw and heard a lot about, but never quite got around to the stage of persuading people to sit around a table and play it. With RISK: Factions on steam, this problem is eliminated. If you have no clue whatsoever on how to play the game, this will give you a nice crash course, though the rules it offers with the Factions element are a lot more simplified than the normal rules. They also make the gameplay a lot faster.
It can be fiddly working with the faster drag and release methods to speed up troop fights. You can either watch fights happen, including each painstaking dice roll, or just speed through them. Sometimes it doesn't always work when selecting and choosing – and with smaller territories they can be hard to highlight. I've had quite a few incidents where I wanted to invade a specific territory, and it took me 20 or so tries before the area finally got highlighted.
The main campaign mode is designed basically to give you the rules on this version of the game, and introduce you to five “leaders” who each have their quirks. You also get the option to have the classic RISK map without the added faction goodies, a classic RISK map with them thrown in, and a faster win method, or utilising maps that showed throughout the campaign, with their specific objectives. You can control one of five leaders: McGutterpants, Generalissmo Meow, His Excellency, Gary, Commandant SixFour, or Colonal Stiffenberg, You can either take objectives on the map for extra bonuses within game, such as an enemy city or capital, or achieve something such as taking over 5 territories in one turn -- to gain advantages over the rest. I can guarantee RNG will annoy you a lot. It can be depressing to see your 10 troops fail to take over an country with only 2 troops defending. Such is the way of the RNG Gods.
The graphics are cartoonish and comical in nature. The faction leaders are funny, with their own animations and expressions for when they attack, lose land, and gain land. The maps themselves are easy to follow, and quite bright.
The music is alright, there's nothing I would find outstanding about it – same with the voice acting tailored to the faction leaders.
There's nothing particularly special about this game, but if you want to play RISK, learn the rules, and be able to play with friends online, then this is definitely worth some of your hours.

This game is so simple, that just six minutes in I think I can give it a review.
As you can guess, the gameplay simply consists of being presented with a statement, and selecting the boolean which accurately denotes the statement's relationship to reality. After you have selected your answer, the game tells you whether you are/were right or wrong, after which you go on to the next (or not, if you make an incorrect answer in Quick Play). There's no timer; you can go at whatever pace you want. This is a welcome design choice, in my opinion, allowing it to feel like the relaxing, casual, and pleasant experience it is supposed to be. The way the correctness or incorrectness of your answer is presented doesn't come off as chiding or overly flattering; being wrong is allowed to be its own punishment, and right, its own reward. And in my opinion, it works very well; I for one found myself feeling high-and-mighty and generally smug as I got a streak of four or five right answers, only to feel promptly humbled and self-aware when I started getting long streaks of wrong answers.
The statements are indeed well-worded, and I've yet to encounter any that are physically unfeasible or unreasonable- i.e. there's no statement that Donald Trump is Cthulhu or that John Cena is the second coming of Jesus. The statements are things such as suggestions of genetic similarity between Koalas and humans, regarding known writers'/artists' hobbies or birthplaces, etc; Each presented statement could seem believable or dubious to someone unfamiliar with the subject. Additionally, so far, each of the questions is in good taste. I've yet to encounter any profanity, racism, sexual content, or anything that touches on universally sensitive material. As the summary for the game suggests, it can be fairly interesting to see which ones turn out to be right or wrong- and of course there is the simple, universal gratification of when you see confirmed what you know well.
The presentation is pleasant and endearing. The game greets you upon startup with a simple menu with a little line that says "You are awesome, [username]". Automated though the message is, I somehow found it oddly warming and pleasant. The imagery is indeed endearing. The main menu overlays a simple image of a quaint beach and shoreline in the background. The animals, of which at least one is almost always visible, are cute, none of which drawn to play on any grotesque or vulgar material (no bathroom humor, etc.). And the animal is changed with each question. Granted, there's not much variety, but their simple art style, combined with the fact that the game's designers had the decency to position them in such a way as to be relatively easy to ignore once you get into the game, has made it so that I, for one, have yet to tire of their presence.
For a fairly casual experience to test one's trivia and to perhaps learn a few things, I do recommend the game. I honestly wouldn't if they were asking for money for it, but as a Free-to-Play game I think it's worth at least a few minutes. I for one have found it nice for just winding down when I'm tired enough to want to lull myself, but awake enough that I want to do something besides lie down, and a bit too restless to look into one of my books. This game also works nicely simply as a "time-waster", if that's what you want, and
There are two complaints I have with the game, though. The first is that there seems to be no defined score for Campaign mode. I do not know whether it's supposed to just be limitless play, if there's a hidden quota of questions we have to meet, etc. I rather wish they'd clarify whether "Campaign" mode has a goal, and if so, what it is.
The second is that when you submit an answer, it only tells you if you were right or not. I for one rather wish that with each question, there would be a little blurb going into detail, even if only slightly, about the statement presented. For example, if/when the statement is in regards to the existence of a specific place or the occurence of a specific event which turns out to be true, I rather wish the place or event in question would be named (if it has a name), its approximate location and/or time of occurence given, and its backstory/history, purpose, significance, and/or details of its witnessing and recording slightly explained.
In short: As a relaxing, simple, pressure-free experience, I recommend giving the game a couple of minutes. It's Free, so you don't stand to lose much.

This game, from what I have played so far, is rather good. I got it very cheap in a bundle, but after playing it, I feel like it will be well worth the price they're asking for it. I dont know exactly how much content is currently in the game, but the developer promises a large number of levels and multiplayer modes, and considering how active said developer has been, Im inclined to believe that. That said, my opinion is primarily based on the gameplay and mechanics thus far, how they feel, as well as the art style and music. The game is very combat focused, taking a lot of cues from both fighting games and modern hack and slash/spectacle fighting games. The control scheme is simple, but responsive, and the way your various abilities interact creates a variety of mobility and combat options. The combat thus far is fairly challenging and shows a huge potential for depth, much in the same way that games like Devil May Cry, Ninja Gaiden, and Bayonetta do. The similarities to these types of games seem to be the primary criticism most are leveraging against this game, that Joylancer's combat ultimately boils down to frantic buttonmashing, as many also say about the games I mentioned. You certainly COULD get by with mindless mashing, but there is a lot more to it if you try to learn how everything works. The art style, in my opinion, captures the retro feel while not feeling like a duplicate of any particular game. However, since it does carry the sort of 8-bit/early handheld graphical style, many may form their opinion on that alone, and you probably know whether you like it or not. The music is pretty damn good as well, and fits the high-speed, aggressive nature of the game. If you're interested, I'd definitely reccomend picking it up in a sale or a bundle. If you're not too sure, as with any early access game, wait for the full release.

Solid 9/10
Graphics were okay, gameplay was simple yet fun, but plot is the highlight of this game.
You start as a retired member of the Manhattan Fact Checkers, a gang dedicated to making sure everyone knew what was true and what was false. Years later, after a big breakup of the gang, you are at home with your husband and two kids, Jack and James. Suddenly, an old friend, One-Eye Moe, shows up at your door, telling you that another retired member, Handsome Henry, has started spreading false facts around New York. One-Eye Moe convinces you to come back to the fact-checking game, and before you know it, you're in high speed car chases to the library or shootouts over the spelling of "necessary". Plenty of story arcs and character development. You'll fall in love with the colourful cast, such as Dumb Donny, a stupid yet kind-hearted man who just wants to know how long bees sleep on average, or an old love interest Scarlet Encyclopdia.
Warning, spoilers!:
The best thing about the plot is the emotion. There is nothing more happy then when you finally figure out how long bees sleep on average for Donny, nothing as angering as when Scarlet Encyclopedia betrays you, or nothing as tear-jerking as the end, when you manage to correct every existing Wikipedia page, only to find out One-Eye Moe has gone to your house and killed your family. The final chapter is the best, when you track down Moe and have a one-on-one truth duel for vengeance.
An overall amazing game, ladies and gentlemen.

True or False is exactly what it says it is. Read the question and decide whether or not it is true or false. Simple concept, True or False is a casual game that was made in Unity free edition. Choose Campaign or Quick Play game modes to test your mind, and don't worry, you'll complete the game long before it becomes boring. I do have complaints, however.
I finished the campaign very quickly and noticed out of the
questions, at least 30 (or less) were false. There needs to be a better balance between true and false. After you complete the campaign and want to do it again, it gives you the same questions in the same order as the first time. Indeed True or False is a simple game in itself, but the effort to not make it ask different questions in different order is redundant. Lastly, you can look up the answers on Google. There should be a countdown timer for each question.
I'll recommend it. True or False is worth its achievements and that's it. The game takes an hour or less to complete, maybe even less if you only seek the achievements.
In short..
- Free
- Casual
- Fast to achieve all achievements for a perfect game
- No true balance between true or false questions which limits difficulty (way more than half of the questions are true)
- Grammar errors. Not everywhere but in some questions..
- No countdown timer that will limit searching for the correct answer on Google.
5/10

- Multiplayer unbalanced maps: This problem still remains in Battlefield 3/4 as well. The map are too unbalanced. Which means on some maps, 8/10 times you etheir win hard or lose hard. There is no between. This cannot be blamed on the teams. It is a map issue.
- There is hardly any rest time in multiplayer. When you lose a base in rush. It takes you 10 seconds and then the enemy are nearby the next objective. Very intense and I disslike it. Personal opinion
- During the story line you run a lot. On Battlefield 3/4 they leave you with much more action, less running. I put it as a negative thing however it is a personal preference.
- Story line bugs. There are a lot of them. CPU that won't die. Terrain bugs. etc. It is not something that RUIN the story but everytime it happens. It will remind you that it exist.
I won't compare this game to Battlefield 3/4 so I say as a game in general 8/10

Quick thoughts. I only played the original campaign as of now and my review is based on that experience. With that in mind, lets go.
Alien Swarm Reactive Drop is a free game (no microtransactions or DLC) made by modding community based on the Alien Swarm which was a good game, but too short, but despite this it was free. This game is just an expansion of the original game and gives you new campaigns (nine compared to one), weapons, enemies, more achievements and 8-player co-op. Sure it might have some flaws, but since it's free you don't lose anything.
+Source-made games usually look good and this one is no exception.
+Gameplay is surprisingly fantastic. You have different classes and weapons to choose from.
+Basic level system, which unlocks more items the more you level up.
+The key to success is cooperation and that's always a good thing and mandatory for co-op games.
+A lot of maps and workshop offers even more.
+Doesn't seem to have a lot bugs (as of yet, in my experience).
+Achievements and workshop offer some replay value.
*It's not that fun without friends. Talking with someone and making up strategies is honestly the best part in this game. Get some friend and play. The experience is much more fun when doing that.
*Can be a bit sketchy for new players and requires some excercise when playing more maps. Though it's the same thing with every game.
*More characters and skins would be been nice, though not necessary to enjoy this game.
-Some network issues occur here and there
-Server browser usually don't show the real player amount or just shows it too later
As a free game it's pretty close to 10/10 because of that reason. Developers clearly made this version of Alien Swarm as a fan project and offering more missions and workshop was indeed something that Alien Swarm required.

In the game, you can drive vehicles plowing through hordes, gather resources, rescue survivors, change home base locations to better suit your needs and build and upgrade your base as well for other purposes. Another problem which is debatable, is that time passes by without you actually being game, even though it's an offline game. It's not fair to review a less-than-half-done game, but given the quality of these entitled forum posts disguised as reviews, here goes:
Paint the Town Red is an early-access, first person Voxel based Brawler with a solid base experience which it is currently gaining fame for in all the right ways. The basic concept of organic cuboid gore and the wide variety of tools at the player's disposal from release have made the existing product a good example of an early access game.
So far the only given objective is to kill everyone, in the spirit of notable stylistic cousin Hotline Miami.
The Hotline comparisons are thick on the floor, save for the damage model and backstory. You can take multiple hits, as can foes, depending on what you hit them with and where. Reactions to those injuries are lacking somewhat, and multiple times  found myself wondering how the thug I'd just disfigured was continuing his assault unflinching with a face full of broken glass and chair splinters. The story is 'missing' - nothing is told to us, yet the title screen suggests we're either reliving memories or outright time traveling to sort history out one beatdown at a time, a far cry from Hotline's well buried and confusing world. (Not that all games need War and Peace for a backdrop of course)
The technical flaws it has so far are fairly usual for a Unity game in early development; framerate inconsistency, laptop processors having trouble, occasional clipping errors and a lack of in-depth settings currently sit on the game's shoulders, and are never shy about asking for your chips. At times,(usually when re-enacting the elevator scene from 'Driver') Voxel bloodspurts are so voluminous that the framerate chokes on those too.
The AI feign ignorance at times, but they always know where you are, and it can lead to a 'Conga of death' where half the level's population will seek you out and swarm you for an unseen bathroom murder.
Oh, one other thing, you can rebind the controls, but the main menu isn't the place to do it for some reason. You must currently be in a level to get the option to adjust control methods.
PVE multiplayer has been hinted by the Developers as on the horizon, and it would be welcomed, as will the mass of patches that will undoubtedly invalidate this review.

Well, this game is rather simple; as its name says, it's all about true or false questions. Still, it contains some very interesting facts; some of which I had to search about after playing the game. It'd be a nice addition if the game provided some sources regarding the "true" facts; however, you can always Google them later on (which I've seen another review suggest).
The background music is simple, but it fits nicely, and I love the "cute" style they went with, having different animals bring the questions and such. It's silly, sure, but in a fun way. Also, the game has a "campaign" mode, which consists of all the available questions, and at the end it tells you how many correct answers you had.
Still, given the nature of this game, it doesn't offer a lot of replayability. It's still good to learn about some interesting facts, and also to see how good your intuition is, as some questions (unless you happen to know about them through another source) clearly defy your expectations. So, I recommend it for a free evening!

Battlefield Bad Company 2 (BBC2) is a normal shooter military game. I had to play a shooter for years because of my strategy game taste and I decided to see where things had come. Well, the game is good. I think the multiplayer part, these games were designed for, is even better.
Electronic Arts as always has made pretty good job on the graphics sector. The guns are pretty good. The soldiers' figures, the environment like trees, rocks, grass or whatever. The sounds are very normal in comparison with reality. Explosions, gun sounds, soldiers' voices, helicopter and plane sounds, all of them great.
The story mode is weird. You continue to fight against the foes to find a secret weapon. A plane with cloak ability containing a great EMP pulse weapon of some sort. One gets another like a team when someone tries to go away from the cause saying that all finished. It's not bad , but NOT real anyway... lol
Let's go to the point... GUNS and GUN fights. You'll have much gun play here. You'll find the one suited to your needs. Weapons with different aiming, precision, firepower, ammo, and reload times. I personally liked the heavy machine guns with the precision scopes even if without the scopes were more natural. Have you ever seen a very precised machine gun? NOoooooo. Can you carry an MG-3 with 200 rounds or an M60 with 500 rounds. They both weight about 10 kg WITHOUT the rounds. And you can use them almost as snipers do. Or you can move along with a scope in your eye.... LOL.. Totally fake. Or maybe you are a SUPER soldier.... Anyway.. It's fun because it's a game. Another point you won't like is RPG's or missile launchers.They are totally inaccurate and a tank needs 2 or more to die. This is an issue because you'll find yourself completely pinned down and you will be unable to do anything sometimes. With those weapons you fight tanks and helicopters, yeah you read right, helicopters. There is even a level that you have to do with two helies at the same time. You have some missile launchers at the borders of a base, but as they have guided missiles, the helies can avoid them. And at the same time you have infantry on your back, GREAT or HELL? The ONLY way to get down those helies was running among the ruins for cover and shoot with my OWN missile launcher. And everyone of them needs 2-3 shots to die, totally unnatural. The only weapon that fullfills its promise is the great sniper weapon. But this one fires Km far away. So, GOOD gun play but totally fake game.
As much for the environment. Feeling like you are in a battlefield is NOT an easy case. So EA made everything destructable. Almost everything can be destroyed. You walk among the ruins and there are gas barrels or FULL tanks of trucks in the level. If you shoot at them they blow up. If you shoot at anything with heavy weapons it will be destroyed, buildings too.ONLY rocks and terrains is inpenetrable and undestructable. Another thing a player likes but it's totally unreal is that the same soldies can drive trucks, helies, ATVs, to be a gunner on them, drive a TANK with BOTH AT shells and against personnel. I mean OK, you HAVE to be a SUPER soldier. Am I playing Battlefield or Return to Castle Wolfenstein, Duke Nukem or Crysis? Has anyone of you played Super Trench Attack? If NOT search some walkthrough videos till the training and with it. You'll laugh so MUCH... You are the guy! The ONLY hero we have!
So, after so .... much reality in this game and with great explosions and gun play I have to say it's JUST a great experience. That's ALL!

A case study in self-imposed constraints leading to polished, refined design, Joylancer's chunky pixels and limited palette mesh well with its responsive, fluid gameplay. Definitely play with a gamepad.

I made a video preview to show off some of the features and gameplay of this game!
I hope you enjoy!
Martyr

This game gets straight to the point: the satisfaction of busting through enemies is one of the biggest draws for action/platformer games, and Joylancer nails it. Not only is it rewarding to plow through enemies, but there is enough depth to the combat and movement systems to let you plow through them the way YOU want to. Even more than that, just being able to fly across levels with the few actions available to you is just a hell of a lot of fun. Boss battles, though? That's where the game may catch you by surprise. No spoilers, but you'll want to use every tool at your disposal when facing them...
The A/V experience is a bit harder to gush about; you may need to spend a few minutes messing with the colour presets to find something that you will enjoy playing with, although the basic preset is decent. The nice thing is that if you ever DO get bored with one selection, you can just go fiddle with it until you find something more appealing. Also worth mentioning is the music, because your mileage will likely vary: the harsh soundtrack can at times be distracting, but it can also fit the action quite nicely. It appears that there will soon be a feature to choose which track plays during gameplay, but it isn't there yet, so be wary/look forward to that. Personally I enjoy most of the soundtrack, so that'll just be a bonus for me when it comes out.
There's actually a fair amount of content not in the game yet, so if you prefer your games to be made of whole cloth you may want to hold off for a few more patches— but the feel of the game is definitely enough to warrant a purchase right now. If you're looking for in-depth combat mechanics in a simple-looking game, Joylancer has it. If you're looking for a satisfying score/time attack action game, Joylancer is quickly becoming that game. If you're looking for frenetic and fun multiplayer, Joylancer has got your back.

Although it is naturally really fun and always entertaining, I have a huge gripe with it ....
When I first played SC many years ago, you had to have Half-Life and its expansions to get the full experience. It had a dedicated and mostly mature community. Sure, it was then free and still is, but let me get back to you on that.
As the F2P community spreads throughout previously dead servers, one such as myself who had only months ago struggled to find a populated server is pleased. Yet this newly popular mod's availability on Steam is an excellent exemplification of "bittersweetness."
With any game that the public hasn't seen/is ignorant too (mostly), you'll have the immature idiots who would waste seasoned players' and their own time messing about (blocking doors, spamming mics, getting into arguments over whether it's a game or mod, etc). It is just truly saddening to see that negativity spread to SC.
So, I have some advice (let's just say I know a thing or two about running sh*t). --
1. Disallow players who don't own Half-Life (and/or its expansions) to enjoy all of SC. Yeah, deal with it.
2. Maybe ask what, 5 dollars (?) for people to download the mod? I'd pay 50 dollars to enjoy the SC I know and love as it should be if it means paying that much.
3. Just, idk. Maybe putting SC on Steam was good for publicity and public awareness regarding an honestly dying mod. But maybe not. I mean, people refuse to accept the fact that it's originally and basically a mod for a wrinkling game on the GoldSource engine. Is the engine or Half-Life bad? Hell no! But you need to be up and front about what these people think. You have the Steam store; a marketplace filled with good and bad people all looking for their own method of entertainment and must be more than just "It's free and you don't need anything to play it" about it. You need to start demanding some prerequesites. Take my words into consideration. Whatever my *steam* hours may be on the steam version you could likely multiply by 10000 in actual time played.

Pretty disappointed to say I feel I would not recommend this game. It's a walking sim essentially which is fine if the story is worth getting absorbed in, but it wasn't. It slams you with all these emotions in the first 5 minutes or so and then it sort of incoherently rambles from one plot to another until it ends with no real payoff.
You ever play through a game and get to an ending so disappointing that you start googling alternate endings wondering if you somehow got the bad ending? I did that right after beating this. There's also no mapping of your choices like in telltale games or OXENFREE to give you some sense of what the game was trying to do. It feels like the game was supposed to revolve around your radio relationship with the primary NPC. Maybe go on some kind of emotional journey, but you don't. I seemed to me the writers ran out of gas trying to do that and instead threw in a bunch of distracting and hohum subplots. Also the exploration felt incomplete. I felt like I probably had the option to explore, but there were too many invisible walls that kept me from bothering.
I wish steam had options other that a simple YAY or NAY, because I don't feel ripped off and the game was competently done. It's not something I feel was worth recommending. If you aren't the type that gives a lot of slack when it comes to walking sims I can't recommend this one.

So! Let's talk Joylancer, shall we?
While the game just recently hit Early Access and is obviously not finished, for what its worth, it actually plays pretty damn well all things considered. The multiple color schemes, the feel, and the looks all scream Game Boy and Game Boy Color, and on that note, they have so far excelled in bringing in the nostalgia train for this gamer. The controls take a short amount of time and practice to get used to, and the uppercut lance technique seems to be particularly tricky (at least, to me, that is).
Combat is frantic and furious, with things exploding and being knocked all over the place. Expect a serious amount of carnage for such a promising game in the future. Oh, did I mention I tested this game out with an Xbox 360 controller, and works wonderfully? They even got the pad to vibrate when your lance is fully rev-ed up. Nice touch.

Probably the best zombie survival game out there. It has an open world feel in a town setting which helps immensely in making the town feel real. It was a surreal feeling as i was starting to learn the roads and ways to get back home recognising signs and houses as i drove by them while mowing down zombie hordes.
Cars really make a difference making missions play out faster and a little safer though still quite dangerous especially when your vehicle has no driver side door allowing a zombie to pull you out of your car to make a flesh dinner out of you if you dont toss em off somehow. Having a car makes mowing down zombies which have formed a horde much more easier to tackle compared to the much more terrifying on foot melee combat. You will have many different types of vehicles at your disposal which feel great to drive and have a nice collision model with some good visuals showing car damage until eventually you have to abandon it as it begins to smoke eventually catching on fire. You can though with the proper base upgrades repair vehicles before they get too banged up.
Of course you can always walk it which makes things much more dangerous as you have to bring food to keep your stamina up and medicine to deal with any possible injuries while evading any large gathering of zombies as the day fades into the night. You can defend yourself with melee weapons for close up combat and guns for long range attacks. You will be limited by what you can carry especially with supply stockpiles you come across but this can be remedied by using a vehicle for supply runs which allows you to load up multiple stockpiles to take back to the base where your friends and other survivors are.
Going through houses and commercial buildings for supplies and survivors is creepy as you never know if there is just that one zombie you see slowly moving past a first floor window or if the place is infested by zombies in other parts of the house. With some stealthy movement you can scout the outside of the house looking into windows to get a possible idea of what awaits inside. That is unless a zombie sneaks up behind you as you struggle with it attracting the zombies in the house. Next thing you know the stealthy silence is shattered by an explosion of zombie moans and growls raging with crazed cannibalistic hunger for your warm raw flesh.
Gathering supplies is needed to build your base and upgrade it over time allowing it to have more survivors living there while better dealing with the psychotic murderous zombies roaming the country side. Gathering supplies which are used daily, completing missions, bringing new survivors, keeping things peaceful between fellow survivors, cooking a nice big meal, brewing up a pot of delicious hot coffee among many other things helps to keep morale up at your home base. You will also gain influence points and fame which allows you to choose better equipment from the supply store and influence others to help you.
You will be playing more then one character as you do missions you will become tired over time and need to rest. This is when another survivor can be asked to take the place of your current character out on the field while they rest up. As your characters grow and develop you will find yourself getting attached to them. When my characters died i was surprised just how it effected me and actually missed them afterwards feeling the loss along with people back at the base talking about their death.
They also died in some incredibly blood thirsty gruesome ways which shocked even a gore hound such as myself. It felt strangely sad as another survivor i was playing came across my previous now dead character's backpack full of supplies as they picked it up to take back to base.
The excellent journal log keeps tracks of all these events and effect it has on everyone. It is also used to give orders for things like base upgrades, seeing what quests are available and things like how other survivors are getting along with each other and the morale of the base.
Weapons and vehicles can be repaired when the proper base upgrades are built. This is usually over night so it pays to use more then one type while the other is being repaired.
Music is done very well setting the tone of a once normal world transformed into a unbelievable living nightmare which blends well with the home town family surroundings all around you constantly assaulting your mind with contrasting atrocities of flesh eating zombies feasting on the living.
Graphics are interesting in the fact that they are not the greatest yet get the point across like a sledgehammer as you are suddenly witnessed to a brutal death and even more shockingly so if its your own.

Star Wars Republic Commando is a significant deviation from the previous Star Wars games I’ve played (Dark Forces/Jedi Knight) and definitely a more modern take on the franchise. If you thought it was weird how storm/clone troopers fought their enemies in battle lines like Civil War era musket infantry, you’ll appreciate the “special forces” feel of Republic Commando.
The game starts near the end of the second Star Wars prequel movie “Attack of the Clones” where the massive clone army is landing on the Separatist planet Geonosis. While the Jedi Knights and Grand Army of the Republic (clone troopers) are fighting on the surface, a four man group of clone commandos is performing covert actions in the underground Geonosian tunnels and even infiltrating the CIS command ships parked on the ground. You play Delta 38, the leader of Delta Squad, a team of “enhanced” clones who take on special assignments. It’s hinted in the opening animation that even though most clones are genetically identical, the commandos have some sort of physical superiority. You definitely have better firepower.
Republic Commando is a first person shooter with heavy squad based gameplay. With a single contextual “use” button, you issue orders to the other three commandos on your team such as door breach, focus target, hack consoles, etc. You can also order team members to use various fighting positions that appear on your hud. This includes sniping positions, grenade positions, and heavy weapon positions. Your computer controlled team has exactly the same weapons that you have, but most of the time they only use the special weapons when assigned to the special positions in the field. There aren’t that many weapons to choose from actually, but there’s plenty of ammo all over the place. This is good because most of the guns can be ineffective depending on who you’re fighting. If everyone has to die right now though, start throwing your grenades.
Pros:
+A lot of teamwork involved in the single player campaign. In the sections where you’re fighting by yourself you will notice just how much harder the game is without your brothers backing you up. Most importantly, you won’t be revived if you get knocked out, which will happen A LOT.
+The game runs parallel to the movie storylines (though movie characters don’t really show up) so if you’re familiar with the Star Wars prequel movies you’ll have a good idea what’s going on. There are three game campaigns: Geonosis, RAS Prosecutor (a spooky abandoned ship), and Kashyyyk (the Wookie home world). This isn’t Call of Duty where your team is a bunch of people you don’t care about. Your Delta Squad brothers are with you from beginning to end.
+There’s quite a mix up of enemies to fight and usually you have a bunch of different ways to go about clearing a room. The easiest is usually busting out one of your 4 different types of grenades, but the heavy anti-armor gun is always fun too. You don’t get to control any vehicles like in the Battlefront games, but you can man a few different stationary gun turrets (or order your men to do it).
Cons:
-The difficulty of the game seems to vary wildly, especially when dealing with enemies who use melee weapons. Sometimes they just seem to cut you down in one shot. This isn’t a big deal most of the time because your team members can quickly revive you, but during the second campaign, those scavenger droids are a nightmare. I get the feeling they’re just supposed to be an annoyance, but they can absolutely wreck you.
-I mentioned before that the weapons seem weak, but they might just be more suited for fighting certain types of enemies.  Your blaster rifle is decent against the weak droids and Geonosians but seems to be terrible against everything else. There are a few different guns that you can pick up from fallen enemies as well, but with the exception of a couple rare ones, they’re not so hot either. Get used to emptying an entire clip to kill one enemy.
-No co-op multiplayer! A game like this would be amazing if you could go through the game with a team of friends since the computer is already controlling the small team. Unfortunately the multiplayer seems to be restricted to basic PvP.
Overall Republic Commando is probably my favorite Star Wars game (so far). It’s action packed with a strong story and it’s not so old that I’m embarrassed to run it on a modern computer. Definitely give the game a try if you can get your hands on it.

Star Wars meets Rainbow Six in this tactical FPS, where you lead a group of strangely unique clones against the enemies of the Republic in three different campaigns. It may not be on the levels of Battlefront or the actual Rainbow Six titles, but Republic Commando is still a great game to play.
Star Wars has a really successful and long relationship with the FPS genre, and Republic Commando is no exception. It may be nothing but a Rainbow Six clone in Star Wars costume, but this is hidden behind excellent game design.
The story takes place during the Clone Wars, where the player takes the role of a special commando, leading his own squad straight into the heart of enemy lines. (The game is not tied to the animated series.)
The settings are a bit clichéd: the battle of Geonosis, a (seemingly) desolate space ship, and Kashyyyk (because there always have to be wookies)… Luckily the writers knew these predictable settings need something to keep interest, so they spoil us with some good dialogues and fast-paced mission structure.
The gameplay itself is simplistic squadron-based tactical combat where a single button replaces the command menu. It may be a significant limitation, but the system works as intended. All events are scripted, but you still need to continuously assess the situation and order your squad accordingly.
Republic Commando may not reach early Halo levels with the AI, but it has nothing to be ashamed of. Just don’t expect your squad to win the game for you; team management is a very crucial point, especially in hold the line situations.
The game didn’t age well from a technical standpoint; modern systems may have a bit of a problem running it properly. But when they do, you are offered one of the best Star Wars games to date to play with.

Joseph Stalin or Iosif Vissarionovich Stalin (Russian: Ио́сиф Виссарио́нович Ста́лин, pronounced [ˈjɵsʲɪf vʲɪsɐˈrʲɵnəvʲɪtɕ ˈstalʲɪn]; born Ioseb Besarionis Dze Jugashvili, Georgian: იოსებ ბესარიონის ძე ჯუღაშვილი, pronounced [iɔsɛb bɛsɑriɔnis dzɛ dʒuɣɑʃvili]; 18 December 1878[1] – 5 March 1953) was the leader of the Soviet Union from the mid-1920s until his death in 1953.
Among the Bolshevik revolutionaries who took part in the Russian Revolution of 1917, Stalin was appointed general secretary of the party's Central Committee in 1922. He subsequently managed to consolidate power following the 1924 death of Vladimir Lenin through suppressing Lenin's criticisms (in the postscript of his testament) and expanding the functions of his role, all the while eliminating any opposition. He remained general secretary until the post was abolished in 1952, concurrently serving as the Premier of the Soviet Union from 1941 onward.
Under Stalin's rule, the concept of "socialism in one country" became a central tenet of Soviet society. He replaced the New Economic Policy introduced by Lenin in the early 1920s with a highly centralised command economy, launching a period of industrialization and collectivization that resulted in the rapid transformation of the USSR from an agrarian society into an industrial power.[2] However, the economic changes coincided with the imprisonment of millions of people in correctional labour camps.[3] The initial upheaval in agriculture disrupted food production and contributed to the catastrophic Soviet famine of 1932–1933, known as the Holodomor in Ukraine. Between 1934 and 1939 he organized and led a massive purge (known as "Great Purge") of the party, government, armed forces and intelligentsia, in which millions of so-called "enemies of the Soviet people" were imprisoned, exiled or executed. In a period that lasted from 1936 to 1939, Stalin instituted a campaign against enemies within his regime. Major figures in the Communist Party, such as the old Bolsheviks, Leon Trotsky, and most of the Red Army generals, were killed after being convicted of plotting to overthrow the government and Stalin.[4]
In August 1939, after failed attempts to conclude anti-Hitler pacts with other major European powers, Stalin entered into a non-aggression pact with Nazi Germany that divided their influence and territory within Eastern Europe, resulting in their invasion of Poland in September of that year, but Germany later violated the agreement and launched a massive invasion of the Soviet Union in June 1941. Despite heavy human and territorial losses, Soviet forces managed to halt the Nazi incursion after the decisive Battles of Moscow and Stalingrad. After defeating the Axis powers on the Eastern Front, the Red Army captured Berlin in May 1945, effectively ending the war in Europe for the Allies.[5][6] The Soviet Union subsequently emerged as one of two recognized world superpowers, the other being the United States.[7] The Yalta and Potsdam conferences established communist governments loyal to the Soviet Union in the Eastern Bloc countries as buffer states. He also fostered close relations with Mao Zedong in China and Kim Il-sung in North Korea.
Stalin led the Soviet Union through its post-war reconstruction phase, which saw a significant rise in tension with the Western world that would later be known as the Cold War. During this period, the USSR became the second country in the world to successfully develop a nuclear weapon, as well as launching the Great Plan for the Transformation of Nature in response to another widespread famine and the Great Construction Projects of Communism.
In the years following his death, Stalin and his regime have been condemned on numerous occasions, most notably in 1956 when his successor Nikita Khrushchev denounced his legacy and initiated a process of de-Stalinization. He remains a controversial figure today, with many regarding him as a tyrant.[8] However, popular opinion within the Russian Federation is mixed.[9][10][11] Stalin is attributed to 20,000,000–40,000,000 deaths as a result of his regime's actions.[12][13]

Unbalanced and inconsistent. To start off, I'm not great at shooters but I enjoy them for the competiton. This game though, the multiplayer makes me upset. Most servers advertise "No spawn camping" and "Don't use X weapon if team size less than Y". Sure it may sound good but when you spend a total of 3.5 seconds alive and the remainder waiting to respawn, you tend to get salty. Another thing that I don't like, but I understand why it's in place, is limits of how many of each class be in a match. It makes it really unfair when the defenders can camp buildings all as snipers but attackers aren't allowed to have any snipers at all! It feels like everyones weapon is stronger than yours when it takes a clip an a half of consistent hits to kill them but they just need 2. The cover system is aesthetic considering most covers can be shot through and the ones that can't can either be destroyed or are too short to actually serve as cover. The only populated servers are repatative. You gain better equipment as you rank up, so higher ranking players will be more accurate, deal and take more damage and have, overall, a better chance at being sucessful.
Overall, this game can be fun, provided you get into a good server and the other players are a somewhat similar rank to you and you learn every nook of each map. If you like shooters for campers and dying, you'll like this. If you like shooters for gameplay that's based mostly on skill, maybe not so much.
