I rate this software as recommended because I personally enjoyed this simulator, as a person interested in aviation. This simulator may NOT be enjoyable for everyone. Here, I list the pros and cons of this software and further down below, a list of the traits and circumstances one may have in order to enjoy this simulation.
PROs:
+Somewhat realistic flight characteristics (for aircrafts with accurate flight models)
+A global-scaled scenery covering the entire planet Earth
+Accurate weather/atmospheric pressure simulations (with the ability to download up-to-date real-world weather data)
+Simulation on areas outside of the earth (you can fly spacecrafts in and out of space)
+Highly complex and realistic aircrafts that can be bought at online stores
+A huge amount of downloadable contents on the internet (
is a good place to start)
+The package includes a plane-make that allows you to create your own aircraft (with some difficulty)
+Realistic navigation (waypoint/ILS/NDB/VOR) simulation and positioning
+Includes many flight operations (for example, flap, bleed air, electrics, engine operation)
+Interesting situations provided (including landing on a aircraft carrier, flying a X-15 from a B-52, space shuttle re-entry, ect...)
CONs:
-Sceneries have low resolution
-Some Terminals and some cities are not included on Sceneries (Fan-made scenery enhancement may somewhat relief this problem)
-Default aircrafts are mediocre
-Accurately simulated aircrafts are often costly (a well-made aircraft normally cost $30 to $85 without discount, which are more expensive than X-Plane itself)
-Joystick and rudder hardware are required for an accurate simulation (a nice set costs around $300 to $500)
-No crash simulation
-Complex aircrafts consumes quite a bit of FPS (my 5 year old MacBook AIr is having trouble with some complex airliners)
-Consumes a large amount of disk space
-Lacking tutorials to fully explain flight operations and menu options
-Menu is difficult to use, with unclear labels and bad categorizing
If you fit most of these circumstances below, I believe you may enjoy this simulation:
1.*You have a interest in aviation and piloting
2.*You're willing to spend time and effort to explore this simulator
3. You had success on other flight simulators/flight simulation games/real world piloting (don't tell me that flying in GTA V counts as flight simulation)
4. You have, and is willing to spend a formidable (for a software) amount of money on this flight simulator
5. You can accept low resolution world textures and not-so-good visual effects
6. Your computer is more powerful than a 5 years old MacBook Air

A true sand-box flight-sim, X-Plane 10 offers a huge variety of options for virtual pilots.
that X-Plane 11 now exists, so you may wish to check that first, if you want the latest version. But version 10 is still a solid offering.
X-Plane 10 is a first rate flight sim. It is
the latest in the series, as X-Pane 11 has now been released. However I've really enjoyed using X-Plane 10 and this sim deserves a positive review. X-Plane 10 may also still be preferred for older machines.
There is a modest selection of aircraft that come with it by default, some of which have high-levels of detail. However, it is the 3rd-party add-ons which are superb and which really add to it. There are hundreds of these (and thousands of community-built ones). If you are a serious simmer, you are probably already aware of this sort of thing, but for the novice, you should consider this as buying the "sim engine", rather than what you'll end up flying. That said, some of the default aircraft are still pretty neat. Many implement good flight models and superb avionics. The level of detail in some of the add-ons is breath-taking. Aircraft available range from the early days of aviation, through the war birds, early commercial airlines, small general aviation, spacecraft, modern fighter-jets, gliders, seaplanes and event remote-control models.
The world is pretty much everything. Apart from the polar regions (over 80 deg latitude) every other continent is rendered. Compared to combat flight sims, the availability of nearly the entire planet is really quite something. Landscapes are pretty good, but there are loads of options for downloading open-source scenery packs, ranging from photo-rendered land-tiles to high-quality airports, complete with ground traffic, etc.
From a multiplayer perspective, sites like VATSIM, IVAO, PilotEdge, etc. provide a way to fly with others online, including human air-traffic controllers. There are some single-player missions available for download, but for the most part, it should be treated as a simulator, not a game or mission. Also, as a flight sim, you would be advised to use a joystick. Even a basic one would give you a great start in learning to control the aircraft. In principle you can do it with the mouse, but it really is not so good.
X-Plane 10 also comes with a utility called Plane Maker. This allows you to build or modify your own aircraft. As a result, there are literally thousands of community contributions. Some are a bit rough, but some are very professional, matching the quality of the paid add-ons. Additionally, there is a well defined network interface, making it possible to link other software to the sim or to add in your own hardware and controllers.
So, in conclusion, if you are interested in flight, you will find X-Plane a great simulator environment. My only caveat is that now that X-Plane 11 is available, you should check that first!

There are quite a few things I would say are positive about this game.
Controls are tight and responsive.
Music is catchy. I wouldn't say that I've been humming it to myself yet, but it fits the theme of the game well.
Spite work and character art is good. Art is subjective, but I found the portraits of Shantae that appear while she talks to be nice to look at as well as amusing.
The writing is good, I find it impressive that they've managed to keep up with continuity since their first game. Everything fits together and you get a feel for who the characters are and why they are the way they are. Humor is also well done, as certain parts made me break out laughing.
If there were one thing that I would critique negatively, it would be some of the level design towards the end. They throw you into these segments where you either get through in one go or die to insta-kill spikes. I don't mind insta-kills when used in moderation, but that's practically all you get towards the end and it's very frustrating. It's not a game breaker, but it's not much fun to fail instantaneously and repeatedly to these traps.
Overall though, I liked the game. Been playing them in reverse order it seems, so I've got high hopes for the next Shantae game I play.

In short, no other game has had such a powerful effect on me as this one. Not even many movies, or books. The story is deep and involving. There is more than one story going on, and all reflect a common theme we can all relate to and which felt like it was talking directly to me. The voice acting is really the best. The visuals are beautiful, and really unique with a blend of realism and graphic art that I have never seen anywhere else. The soundtrack is beautiful. Personally, I loved the balance of interactivity/decision making and linearity, although I still wish there was so much more of it.
Above all though, Firewatch is incredibly brave. It tackles some subject matters which I would have thought were totally unworkable in a game, and yet it works so perfectly, all the while refusing to give in to neatly tied up conclusions and happy endings. If you are familiar with the the Japanese concept of Mono no aware, Firewatch is absolutely this. I wish I could go back and experience this game from the beginning all over again. I hope I will play something as good as this again some day, although it wouldn't surprise me if I don't.

Firewatch very much falls comfortably in the "Walking Simulator" genre. A genre which sounds boring, but can easily let you escape into another world when its done right, and this game does it right.

The game has a few more negatives. Actual gameplay is as simplistic as it comes, and there was some glitching on the landscape (getting stuck) which can break immersion. It didnt happen too often at least, and I never had to restart, just wriggle about a bit to get free. Its a real pity because these dings against the game mean I cannot shout to anyone who would care to listen to buy this gem!

Starr Mazer: DSP is a beautifully crafted prequel to Starr Mazer. (an upcoming point-and-click SHMUP coming out in 2017) Everything is wonderfully balanced, gorgeously presented, and amazingly crafted.
STORY:
The G'ell fleet have invaded, and it's your job to destroy them using pilots you buy over time. As you progressively kill more G'ell, you will collect carbomite, which you can collect with SK:ORE, the game's currency, to buy more pilots once all your current ships have been destroyed. (carbomite can also refill your special meter so you can use more powerful attacks) As time goes on, you'll be collecting more carbomite for each run, which you can use to get better ships, and eventually end the G'ell fleet as you know it.
GAMEPLAY:
The game, at it's core, is a light bullet-hell SHMUP. But, where this game sets itself apart from the rest, aside from the pilot mechanic mentioned earlier, is the balance between it all. Between you shooting enemies, collecting carbomite, and avoiding bullets, it'll almost flow like water how smooth it all works simultaneously. You can let the stray carbomite roam around the screen, which may form into other carbomite, equaling bigger pieces which earn you more SK:ORE. So it has a risk-and-reward type formula going on, should you get the smaller carbomite pieces before you die or wait to get more SK:ORE in the end? It'll definitely be a tense moment throughout your playthroughs, and it's ingenious how it's all executed.
DIFFICULTY:
From my experience, I would say it's pretty fairly balanced difficulty-wise, and definitely shows the classic "Nintenhard" it tries to replicate in it's design. It all naturally gets harder and doesn't have any insane difficulty spikes with bosses. However, in Act 1, I did come across some enemies in the last section that had almost impossible reaction time to properly avoid its attacks. Which brings up the only gripe I have with the game, I think a button to temporarily slow down your ship would help alot. There's a couple bullet-hell sections that require slow, precise movements to properly avoid the bullets, but the sensitivity of the ship gets too slippery and you'll slam right into the hazard. As of this review, there's no way to alter the speed of each ship, so any way to get through those sections would be great. But, I digress, *almost* all of your deaths in Starr Mazer: DSP will definitely fall on your fault alone, and the game does a good job of using audio and visual cues to show when bullets and/or enemies are appearing.
CONCLUSION:
So, to sum it all up, Starr Mazer: DSP is a greatly made SHMUP that adds that classic retro difficulty and a very smart "upgrade" system that sets itself apart from the rest. If you love games like R-Type or Gradius, this is a MUST HAVE, and shows there can be well thought out games for Early Access.
-NOTE-
Although I am a backer of the original Starr Mazer when it was released on Kickstarter back in 2015, and got a discount on this game, I made sure to stay honest and un-biased in this review.

FULL DISCLOSURE: I am a kickstarter backer for Starr Mazer, of which this is a sub game for, and due to being a backer have gotten to know the Imagos Softworks staff fairly well, though just through the internet, I do not know any of them beyond that level (though I'd like to, they are the most open kickstarter runner people I've ever seen and just cool people) - however also as a backer I was able to get this game at 50% off. Starr Mazer: DSP is a crazy high action SHMUP, and god do I suck at it - but it's still really, really fun! I've yet to beat Act I (good enough for now, act II is still in testing), but I've gotten relatively close.
What I like about this game is that it's fair - I never felt any of my deaths were insurmountable, there was always a better way through the enemies and bullets that I just didn't process fast enough - there's also a good bit of strategy involved in what pilots you use, they're proceeduraly generated (with a few notable exceptions such as the three gold pilots named after imagos softworks staff), so there's a bit of chance involved, though this too can be mitigated by buying more expensive 'packs' that give better odds for the pilots you can buy.
Oh, and yes, this games not just a shmup, as you may have guessed from above it's also a bit of a roguelike with death being permanent for your generated pilot - the mission goes on, with newly hired pilots, but when you die, that pilot is gone - and when you run out of pilots in your squad, you get to start over.
Honestly, my only gripe is just that, no matter how many phases my squadrons can take me, I have to restart Act I to phase 1 (the act contains several phases within) when they all die up - as stated I am not particularly good at SHMUPs, and not being able to progress past this has been a bit of a problem for me. I doubt this will be a problem for any skiled SHMUP player though.
The graphics and sound are also just fantastic, very much befitting the arcadey feel of the game - I'd love to go into more detail but unlike gameplay these are easily visable from the screenshots or from the trailer in the case of the audio. But yeah, the presentation is fantastic.
If you love SHMUPs, even if you're like me and suck at them but enjoy them, do your cat admiral proud and get this game.

EDIT: A year later they seem to have gone. Either a fix or other changes in my PC got rid of them - for me, at least.
There are many negative reviews from people who actually like this game, just expected something more from this new release of their old favorite. To them: please remember that Steam users might decide on purchasing the game based on your reviews. Your review should be about the game, not the maker's way doing business. This game is solid. Some say this is the best single-player zombie apocalypse survival game in the Steam market. I agree with them.
SoD:YOSE won't bring much for the owners of the original game though. These new features are:
- High-res menu items and icons
- Better lighting
- One new car type (SUV)
- Varied car paintings
- One new hero
- Many cool new weapons
- Some new combat moves
- Some new textures and 3D models (don't expect a lot!)
- You can re-case ammo in the original campaign and 'Breakdown' too, not just in 'Lifeline'
- You can find and use the military vehicle from 'Lifeline' in the original campaign and 'Breakdown' too
- Some new bugs, hopefully to be fixed soon (nothing game breaking to me)
About the game:
SoD is a third person open-world zombie apocalypse survival game, unfortunately only single-player, where you can manage a small survivor community, build and upgrade base structures, and research new items for your ongoing combat against an unlimited zombie horde. The game has perma-death, some RPG elements, a wide variety of weapons and you can use the environment to fight the hordes too.
The main campaign provides a mediocre story with a good atmosphere, and introduces you to the gameplay.
'Breakdown' is a sandbox version of the main story - you play on the same map, without the storyline. You start in a random location, find and join a community, and then take on its management. When all resources were used up, or you are just bored, there is a broken RV you can fix and use to take a few key members of your community to another area. It will be the same map, with all resources respawned randomly, where you will start in a random point (from your broken down RV) and have to build up everything again. As you repeat the previous steps, the horde gets stronger and stronger, and you will receive new, stronger survivors to reinforce your team. This is my favorite game mode.
'Lifeline' takes place on a new map, is more military-oriented and as such provides a different experience. It is a mixture of the previous two: there is some story, but you can decide to stay and continue saving people at an increased difficulty - with a global leaderboard.
Would I recommend this game?
- If you don't own the original, but like what you have read here, definitely.
- If you own the original and like it, maybe. You won't get much extra, so decide based on what I wrote earlier. Or wait for a sale.

Disclaimer: I'm reviewing this game as its own thing. IMO if you already own State of Decay and its associated DLC this is nothing more than a 1080p graphical update and is not worth the upgrade.
PC Specs (just in case):
AMD FX6300
NVidia GTX760
8GB of RAM
Played on a Microsoft Xbox 360 controller
What can I say about State of Decay other than it is the best zombie survival game in the market. It does a number of things really well:
1) Make every character feel unique
While you will always start with the 3 same characters, the community members you can acquire and how you build your characters can differ tremendously playthrough to playthrough. My first go at this game (in the 720p version) is completely different than my just finished 15 hours of playthough (on the Vanilla campaign). This game rewards smart play, some characters are more suited to melee and some for gunplay and building your characters around these strengths can help greatly or you can take the added risk of building evenly on every character. By the end of the campaign, I had three characters suited for gunplay, three for melee and two all-rounders and tasked each group to specific mission types. Everyone had a backstory and I tried to incorporate this into my decision making as I roleplayed them for what I thought each character would do in real-life. Each character also suffers permadeath and nothing is more heart-breaking than watching a character you build get destroyed by a silly move in a routine scavenging mission although after one or two deaths, you'll usually know when to pick your fights.
2) Simulate a zombie apocalypse.
Resources are scarce and while there are ways to end up not having to worry about resource A or B more often than not you'll run short on Resource C or D (there are five in total Food, Medicine, Ammo, Materials and Fuel). These resources are also consumed as the game is turned off meaning that you'll have to log in to check on the health of your community and to scavenge what you need. Which segues well into my next point. This game requires resource management. While you may be overflowing with food, not having enough medicine to stave off the flu or materials to maintain your defenses can and will spell certain doom. Adding to that is the fact that you can and will run out of resources, so it is a battle against time to stockpile resources and find a way out. Additionally, you will need to balance your time out as well. You will need to decide whether you want to clear the path around you or pursue story or community missions or scavenge for resources. You can roleplay as the hero of the community or the leader of your own isolated community depending on what you choose.
3) Combat is kinda awesome
There is nothing more awesome IMO that kneeing a zombie's skull open, or taking an oar and beating the crap out of multiple zombies. Melee combat in this game is great! You have your attack, dodge or (as I call it) space making moves that allow you to dictate melee fights with zombies. However, get overrun and surrounded and you will die. On the controller the Left Bumper (forgot the keyboard equivalent) allows you to add more power to your attacks, dodge further and finish grounded enemies all with the added cost of more stamina meaning that you can't just spam the attack button all the time.
Gunplay is tight as guns react as you'd expect forcing you to choose the range of engagements depending on the weapon you choose. Pistol's can't one tap enemies from as far as a rifle can, but rifles don't have the rate of fire as pistols do. Assault weapons are a happy medium but ammo for them is scarce and automatic firing will burn through ammo. There are plenty more weapons and I enjoyed using all of them, none of them felt particularly overpowered (though any weapon that can take a silencer should be top priority picks) and filled each niche appropriately.
4) Story
The story was in my opinion strongly average, there are some bits where you have to fill it in with your imagination but the game's narrative is relatively realistic with well-written dialogue. Needlessly to say, this is the most subjective part and I'll leave you to make this decision on your own.
In short, this is in my opinion the best zombie game out there and you should buy it if you are new to the series. Hordes of zombies can be either terrifying or exhilarating to fight against depending on how prepared you are to face them. In between all the fighting there's managing your community, resources and characters. Sprinkled on top of all this is a great melee combat system and great gunplay. The story is what you make of it honestly, I found it adequate to keep my playing and motivated to finish the game but it isn't going to win awards. Some technical stuff below.
Technical stuff
Graphics: Decent looking. I had everything on the Max preset (there's the Ultra preset after Max) and the game looked beautiful at times. What really detracted from the experience was the game slowdowns as you moved from area to area. It almost felt like the game kept reloading assets of the upcoming parts of the map leading to some noticeable stutter.
Sound: I liked how everything in this game sounded. Zombies whether aggressive or not sounded suitably dead and menacing. The guns sounded great, melee weapon effects were also pretty good. The ambiance came together very well for me.

For new players interested in SOD, yes I would reccomend this to you. For the vet players who own the original SOD and are debating about buying this one, think about if the new additions are worth the price tag to you. The game itself is basicly the same except with a few tweaks, visual improvements, new characters in breakdown and some of the breakdown challenges changed.
For new players:
State of Decay is a sandboxish zombie survival RPG. You switch between different survivors that have their own perks and personalities and try to gather supplies to help your group survive. There are lots of different weapons to use and there is a small RPGlike skill system. For example, if you spec a survivor in using blunt weapons then when that skill levels up enough you can pick 1 of 2 attacks for the survivor to learn. With firearms depending on what type the survivor specs in you can get better firerate, longer distance lockons, etc. The game also features perma-death so if your survivor dies, they are gone for good which adds a bit of tension when your trying to escape a horde or dealing with one of the "freaks".
There are 3 modes in the game that you can play and they are:
Storymode:
The one you want to start with as it explains how you play the game. You follow the story of 3 survivors and without any spoilers, basicly work on surviving and expanding your base as you help other survivors out and start learning about whats going on in the world.
Breakdown:
The main survival part of the game. You start out with a random survivor, pick an enclave group to join, then get to work surviving. The main goal is to find an RV and fix it up. Once you do that you pick which survivors you want to take with you to the next level and repeat. With each level resources become more scarce and zombies become more populated. There are also challenges that when you complete them, unlock hero characters which have their own special perks and bonuses. Theres a small escort quest to bring them to your base and from then on if you restart breakdown you can then choose that hero to start with instead of a random survivor.
Lifeline:
This mode is unique because you take on the role of the army inside a city crawling with the infected. Your job is to simply scavenge supplies while extracting key VIP targets and any civilians you find. The key difference in this mode is that after a period of time you have to fight of a siege of the infected which gets steadily more difficult as you move on.
To sum it up, State of Decay ( or SOD ) is one of the best zombie games out there at least in my opinion. If you've never owned the original SOD and were interested in grabbing it, then yes I would reccomend this to you 100%. As for vet players though, I know alot of them are angry about the support being dropped for the original and they do have a right to be. Its purely up to them if they want to buy this version for only a few new features.
For new players this is perfect for you. For the old vets, again just think if spending the money is worth for the extra features that they threw in.

The default aircraft aren't amazing, and only a few thousand (only :P) have 3D scenery. There is a wealth of free aircraft and scenery avaliable at the
forums and the
Store (

), probably the most generous community I've ever seen for a game. But if you want a detailed simulation, be prepared to pay money, this isn't a cheap hobby. I've probably spent well over $1000AUD on addons, hardware and software, as well as all of the free utilities and things that would usually come at a premium at a P3D or FSX forum. I would personally recommend against getting X-Plane 10 from steam, and instead get X-Plane 11 from Laminar's website, as X-Plane 10 is included free with it. The actual engine in X-Plane is fantastic. I can't really compare it to real life as I've never flown in real life, but certainly compared to FSX it's a huge improvement. You can really feel the air under your wings, as appossed to the "flying on rails" feel you get with FSX and P3D. The only real downside to X-Plane 10 is that it can only use a few of your cores, due to limitations with the OpenGL engine. This can lead to low framerates when you're using several high-fidelity aircarft and custom scenery. Even still, low framerates is far superior to random CTD's you get with FSX and P3D due to memory limitations.
TL;DR:
This is not a game. It's a simulation. Expect to have to pay big money for extreme-fidelity aircraft, but still less than P3D or FSX. It's a solid engine, runs well and consistantly. Have a high single-thread clock and a decent GPU if you want to get the best performance. The best addons are at

First of all,
I've read many negative reviews about Magicka 2 and I partly agree with some of them, but overall I'll think that Magicka 2 deserves to be a "good game".
Here comes why.
I am going to compare Magicka 2 with Magicka 1 right here because it's the point why the most people complain about Magicka 2.
To see why Magicka 2 differs so much from Magicka 1 we have to look at the spellcasting system and gameplay.
Those are the most differences between Magicka 1 and Magicka 2 refering on spellcasting and gameplay (those, that many are complaining about).
I think the other differences are almost visible so I'll gotta tell you, why I prefer Magicka 2 over Magicka 1.
People who played Magicka 1 as long as me do have the most problems with getting into the new System of Magicka 2.
Most of your old spell combinations don't work anymore or feel weak. Everything just felt weak when I've started playing Magicka 2.
That was, mostly, because I didn't knew what I was doing because I was playing like I played Magicka 1.
That is a fault. And I would recommend every new Magicka 2 player who comes from Magicka 1 to test new spells and combinations because some (*caugh* Spam QSR *caugh*) are more powerful than they were in Magicka 1.
It is something you have to get into. It takes time, but also makes more fun to play than in Magicka 1.
That comes because it is now harder to survive and you need more knowledge (weakness of several enemies) and reaction (or friends who revive you) in order to be effective.
But it also feels better if you made it through a level just by *knowing what you're doing*.
Also I prefer the new graphics and music, there is still some good humor in the game and its more long-time-motivating because of artifacts and things you can unlock by playing on higher difficulties (also playing on higher difficulties itself is challenging but fun, too).
So, my statement overall is:

BROWNIE LAYER:
3/4 cup (1 1/2 sticks) unsalted butter
1 1/2 cups bittersweet chocolate chips
1 cup granulated white sugar
1/2 cup packed light brown sugar
4 large eggs
1 teaspoon vanilla extract
1/2 teaspoon salt
1 cup all-purpose flour
COOKIE DOUGH:
3/4 cup (1 1/2 sticks) unsalted butter, room temperature or almost melted
3/4 cup granulated white sugar
3/4 cup packed light brown sugar
1/4 teaspoon salt
2 tablespoons milk or cream
1 1/2 teaspoons vanilla extract or vanilla bean paste
1 cup all-purpose flour
1 cup miniature chocolate chips
additional miniature chocolate chips, if desired (to garnish the top)
Directions:
Prepare the brownie layer-
1. Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F. Spray a 9x9-inch pan with nonstick spray, then line with a strip of parchment paper so that it covers the bottom and comes up two sides of the pan. Spray the parchment with nonstick spray too.
2. In a microwave safe bowl (or in the top of a double boiler or pan set on top of a pan of simmering water), microwave in 30 second bursts to melt butter and chocolate chips together until all is melted and smooth. Whisk in the sugars, then whisk in the eggs, vanilla and salt. Sift flour into the bowl and stir that in too. Scrape the brownie batter into the prepared pan. Bake for 25 to 30 minutes, or until the brownie layer is cooked through (toothpick inserted into the center comes out clean). Place the pan of brownies in the refrigerator to speed up the cooling process (or cool at room temperature and add the cookie dough layer later).
Prepare the cookie dough layer:
3. In a large bowl, use an electric mixer to combine the butter, sugars and salt until soft and creamy (1 to 2 minutes). Mix in the milk and vanilla. Sprinkle in the flour and mix in until combined. Stir in the 1 cup of chocolate chips. Scoop the cookie dough onto the top of the brownies and spread onto the brownie layer. I find that it's easiest to do this if the brownie layer is chilled and firm. Wet your hands or spray them with nonstick spray and pat the cookie dough on top in a even layer. Sprinkle additional chocolate chips on top to create a nicer, visual appearance. For easy, clean cutting, chill the brownies (wrap the brownies with plastic wrap and chill until firm- 1 to 2 hours or up to 2 days).
4. Cut the brownies: Run a knife along the sides of the brownie pan and then use the parchment paper to lift the brownies from the pan and onto a cutting board. Slice the brownies with a sharp knife, wiping the knife with a paper towel between cuts. If you'd like all of your slices of brownies to look clean-cut without edges, use the knife to cut the sides of the brownies off before cutting pieces. Keep brownies slices covered and chilled until ready to serve.

I had this game years ago, but always had a problem getting it to run on my PC because of the ultra-realisitc graphics and 3D models of 1999.  I know: it's just NOT possible for graphics to ever get any more advanced that this.  Am I right?  Because my computer just could not handle the 32 MB of RAM needed to play this beast, I was only ever able to play it on Dreamcast, but is among my favourite games of all time, ranking just below the original Fallout.  That's just how good it is!
It's a game that features David Bowie, his music, and his wife is a playable character.  What more is needed?  Nothing, I tell you.  After all these years now I'm able to play the game on PC without problems.  I dusted off my strategy guide (because I still have the strategy guide for this game) and entered heaven once more.
I remeber the game being much more difficult when I was younger, but this game is not about struggling to advance further in the game, it is to experience the narrative.  Made by QuanticDream, the company known for its Hollywood-esque cinematic games like Deus Ex, Fahrenheit (or Indigo Prophecy), and Heavy Rain, just to name a few.  However, unlike Heavy Rain and Fahrenheit, you do actually get to play this game instead of going through quick-time events and occasionally getting to walk.  Nomad Soul (or Omikron: The Nomad Soul) requires strategy, it has timed events, gun combat, hand-to-hand combat reminiscent of Virtua Fighter, action events.  Basically this game is cross-genre hybrid of gaming types and it tries to balance them the best it can, though because of the tank controls (Yes, tank controls), things that require precision timing can be unfair.
The game is fully-immersive.  You play as multiple characters throughout the game and each one has different strengths and weaknesses.  You, the player, are thrust into this world where you can go to the store to buy things, hang out at the bar, listen to some music, visit your apartment flat, do side missions, or just go through the plot.  The game has a similar feel to Shenmue where you can completely live in this game and ignore the main plot and go have fun in all the different locations.  The game really feels like a city.  There is obvious draw from Blade Runner in the game's design.
The game offers some of the old-school-iest things in gaming that you just don't see anymore.  You have limited saves and checkpoints.  The game will require you to find rings to get more saves.  There does come to a point where you will have, like, 30 rings so as long as you play a good chunk of the game each session, you will not use up all your rings.  This really is not for the person who likes to save their game around every corner.  Be prepared to reload just so you don't waste all your rings.  These rings also act as continues, so again, reloading your last save is sometimes better than wasting all your rings.

Squadron (itself based on the melodramatic 80s manga/anime Area 88). The roguelike "individual pilots/ships=lives mechanics" should makes the game feel forgiving/fair while still incentivizing going for a one-credit clear (1cc) and score-chasing -- since the game is challenging and rewards hi-scoring, while simultaneously not allowing credit feeding, the usual complaints about shmups by mainstream media-outlets don't apply here [i.e., that they're hard yet you can credit feed, thus making playtime for someone just looking to see the ending short and frustrating - these complaints usually miss the point about score, which Starr Mazer actively compels you to achieve higher and higher with the "buying-lives-on-subsequent-playthroughs-with-accumulated-score mechanic]. And, if a players doesn't like a particular weapon/subweapon/ship, another one is waiting after the next life or run, it sounds like the already great variety is only going to get better. Also, while gorgeous and backed by a ♥♥♥♥♥en' synth-fueled soundtrack, it still runs on a toaster like my eight year-old laptop (bravo devs). Finally, one of the subweapons is the
, which is a nice metonym for this game on the whole: stylish, fast-paced, and action packed -- a fever-dream-of what a child of the eighties would have imagined video games would look like in a neon-and-chrome synthesizer future. Brilliant.

In this game, you play as Commando Delta 38 (Boss/Leader).
The game follows the story of three missions throughout Delta Squad's career in the Separatist Crisis.
From fighting alongside wookies to getting your face drilled by a scavenger droid, you lead your squad to complete objectives your normal, mass produced, counterparts could/cannot.
The game and story is nice, I loved it and maybe you will too. This is from the soldier's perspective as to the usual jedi perspective. The game plays pretty damn smooth on PC. I haven't had any real game-breaking problems. The game is old enough to even play on lower-end laptops. You get to actually order your squad to do things (ex.When you issue the Search and Destroy order, they become aggressive and move ahead even if you're looking around, You can order them to set demolition charges on objectives to progress or you could order them to secure the area and plant the demolition charge yourself. You can even send them to sniper/anti-armor positions as well as turrets.)
If you lose all your health, you get downed and the game doesn't end until your entire squad is downed. So while you're downed you could either tell them to maintain current orders (ex. search and destroy) or order the closest squad member to revive you. There's also the option to load the last save while you're downed. There's also quicksaves, I hotkeyed mine to F1 and F3 because I can screw things up a lot.
I don't think you can really get through this game without ordering your squad around. You take quite a bit of damage, even on medium difficulty. Just for future reference, don't run infront of your squad while they're firing a sniper or a anti-armor grenade. Bad things happen. . .
All in all this game was great for it's time and pretty short if you know what you're doing. I just REALLY wish there was a sequal just because of the ending. . .
One of the only good things to come out of the prequels.

Republic Commando is a FANTASTIC game, one of the greatest Star Wars games ever made and unquestionably the best Star Wars first-person shooter ever made (I do not count Jedi Outcast or Jedi Academy, because the lightsabers kind of radically change those games to the point where they no longer really qualify). The squad AI is still incredibly good by today's standards, the characters are compelling and smartly-written, and the environments and story are original and creative.
But I cannot openly recommend getting this on Steam without some qualifying statements.
Republic Commando is an old game. A very old game. And it does not play nicely with newer computers. Problems with bumpmapping in the graphics can result in crashes, and trying to get it to run on a 64-bit Windows OS is a horrific struggle. If you have Windows 7 or 8 64-bit, Republic Commando may need to be sadly relegated to the history books. Hopefully your memories, if you got a chance to play it back in the day. You will likely not get another.
EDIT: Ever since I upgraded to Windows 10, it's worked perfectly. I don't know what changed, but I hereby retract the preceding paragraph. In the interests of transparency, I will leave it up, but the compatibility issues probably won't affect you anymore.

In many of the negative reviews of X-plane there seems to be a mismatch between the reviewers expectations and what X-plane is. If you're looking for aerial combat you'll be far better served by DCS World. Flight simulation whether you go FSX, P3D or X-plane is more hobby than a computer game. If you were going to get into model railways you may start with a small basic train set. If the bug bites, you soon want to add switches, scenery and new locomotives and stock. That's what x-plane is; a flight simulator starter set.
You get a couple of basic aircraft, a sky and a barren planet (inhabited by only deer and birds). X-plane does itself a disservice with most of the included aircraft as they are far from representative of quality of aircraft that are available. X-plane's clouds are stonefish ugly.
All the main simulators have pro's and con's. X-plane's smaller community is very committed and self reliant and there is a smorgasbord of freely available utilities and addon scenery. Some of which are pretty damn awesome considering they are free. You can get a very decent simulator experience with freeware alone. For sure, you will not minutely scratch the surface unless you're prepared to research and learn.
Personally I'd recommend budgeting for an addon aircraft in addition to X-plane. I'd suggest a Carenado HD aircraft, not because there aren't other worthy aircraft, just that if you are starting into X-plane, Carenado are consistently high quality and you're less likely buy something disappointing. If you want to go a bit further, Skymaxx Pro will fix X-plane's underwhelming skies.
Flight simulators may bore your socks off but they may also change your life. X-plane is a starting point for a hobby that may be with you for years.

Longtime FSX user and wanted to upgrade to a more recent flightsim. Thought I would try X-Plane out. Picked it up on a steam sale and was blown away with the land and water textures. Flying at night is so awesome in X-Plane.
I noticed some things that really disappointed me.
I was let down by the selection of aircraft packed in with the sim. Some are unfinished with no VC or cockpit. Also the default aircraft all have a tendency to roll to the left. I've tried calibrating my joystick, adjusting the settings in the sim. Nothing, I can't get the Cessna 172 to not roll to the left. And yes, I'm a private pilot. I know all about the left turning tendency, torque and MORE RIGHT PEDAL. I got all that from my CFI. But try and fly that sucker straight and level in X-Plane. Let go of the yoke and left turn...every time. That's an immersion breaker. Unless you turn on the auto pilot.
Adjusting the controls is a nightmare. You have to set up control schemes for each aircraft. Why? Flaps, gear, lights and views should not change depending on what airplane I happen to be flying in.
The ATC.... SO BAD. Disappointed by the primitive ATC in this game. Trying to fly IFR with the ATC is impossible in this sim. Just don't even use the ATC. Your ears will thank you.
Lack of freeware aircraft. The selection of freeware is disappointing considering this is the tenth version of this game. And the payware seems to be very pricey with sales few and far between.
Your local airfield will probably not have any buildings or hangars. Why? This is 2017. This is unacceptable in a flight sim that is active and still receiving updates in 2017. This breaks immersion and makes me feel like I have an incomplete product.
Im sure there are people who say, "Just download this AddOn to fix the ATC", or "You can download a program to re-create your airfield". Why? Why should I have jump through all those hoops and spend time fixing a game that was sold to me as a complete product?

This is actually a nice little gem of a game.
It's a parkour simulator in an open world environment, with a possibility to shift between 1st and 3rd person perspective AND a good "rewind" mechanic like in the Prince of Persia series.
It's colorful, it's simple, it's fast. It's fun.
I like it. A lot. If you're into Mirror's Edge or Cloudbuilt (or like skipping around the city like in Saints Row 4 or Prototype), give it a try.
There's not much of a plot - there's an evil tyrant, there's the resistance made up of gamers, that's about it, at least, as far as I've played it. The game doesn't take itself seriously at all, which is a good thing and fits perfectly with the cartoony overall style.
Run, jump, collect, break, explore, play ball, race, do whatever you like. There is a multiplayer and a friends-only option, but soloing the game is fun in itself.
There's not a lot of player customization options, mostly just size and palate swaps. You can, however, upgrade their stats by placing chips acquired from the game into the character's slots, and thus changing your game style. The problem with that is that you can't see the inventory (which is in TEAM) and the equipped menu (CHARACTER) at the same time. You can remove a chip and then select from the inventory, but sometimes this destroys the equipped chip, so this gets pretty annoying. Maybe I'm doing it wrong.
There are no enemies per say, just the robo-drones that chase you and "traitors" and spu-drones that you chase. There are no weapons, you just ram your target.
There are HUNDREDS of secrets and things to do (even in solo mode), and, if you're a completionist, this might turn into the best game of your life or a living nightmare. Maybe that's just me, but I can't distinguish between a sign that I've already broken and a previously untouched one, or posters previously sprayed and those that are new. In a big city with, like, a 100 of each of those, finding the last ones on the list is problematic.
The soundtrack is nice, but it does get repetitive fast - there's just not a lot of tunes available, maybe 4 or 5 in the first section of the game.
This is not exactly a casual gaming experience, it's quite challenging, it requires skill to advance the story, beating races and playing that basketball-ish game. They're not that hard, they just need time and effort, and if you're not going to invest in that, well, you won't be able to move the plot along.
There are a few bugs in the game, like whenever I choose "Try Again", my character teleports back to the beginning of the race, but immediately falls through the floor and out off the map entirely. I have to time a jump so that I stay on the same level as the quest giver. And some textures in the Sewer level vanish, revealing a black emptiness. But otherwise it's a pretty solid experience, nothing game-breaking or serious.
If you like messing around in a busy neony open world for some time, jumping off walls and basically goofing off, sure, by all means, get it.

Let's start off with my first encounter with One Thousand Lies.
At first glance, I thought this game was a pretty short and simple VN, like any other. With it's not so great backgrounds, well for my taste that is. I immediately felt like it wasn't even worth playing, specially after seeing such few reviews. But still, I installed it, for the sake of recording it for the YouTube Channel. I thought, "Hey, maybe it's still worth recording", but I didn't... I opened the game, to check if everything's working properly. I read a bit of the start, to find out if it's worth continuing. In the end, I wasn't satisfied. I never bothered recording, instead I played it, since it's already installed...
About 30 mins in, I can feel myself sighing in regret. I can understand if the dev's are trying to make it philosophically deep, but at times, it get's pretty tedious to read. The fact that it's mostly just deep words with simple meaning. It made it less enjoyable. I ended up skimming some lines, mostly because they're just pointless to read, and a bit repetitive. But after time, I got used to it, just shrugging it off.
Hours already passed, i'm starting to enjoy it. The sense of humor and cliches kept me going, mostly the humor. I didn't expect much from the story, as it's the typical "Teen protag-kun undergoing a mysterious problem" scenario. There wasn't much to it, specially the fact that I've seen most of this kind of scenarios in anime... Then it hit me, the whole VN felt like an anime. One of those comdedic Slice of Life animes that ends up serious about mid season of the series. But the thing with One Thousand Lies, was the fact that it took so much time and compiled all the tension, executing it near end. In short, it felt rushed. It didn't have a proper flow...
I've reached the end... A bit overwhelmed, my brain connecting the pieces of the story, figuring out what the heck just happened. It all felt too much in a short span of time, guess they wanted to give a big impact on the players. Well, it worked. I felt satisfied reaching the end, a bit sad and still confused, so much questions unanswered.
...
Now, from what I've said so far, they all mostly sound negative. But don't let that decieve you. The game has it's quirks that makes it good in it's own way. One of such is the humor, in which I loved. It really felt like reading a Slice of Life anime, about teens doing stupid stuff. Another one are the characters, their personality makes them likeable and enjoyable to be around (specially Ausse). I may have not been able to relate with the Protagonist in a deeper level, nevertheless I was happy with it. It wasn't my story after all, it was his. Also, the story isn't that bad, nor too cliche. I'm not going to explain why, as I'd like to avoid any spoilers, and it's better for you to find out on your own. I'd ruin the fun if I told hints.
In the end of the day, it wasn't the best nor was the worst. It was good. I'd rate it 7.5/10 (.5 for the humor).

For the first time since an arcade, I have played a side scrolling SHMUP game. I found this game through some hype on Twitch and thought it looked pretty interesting in it's pre-release stages, so I continued to follow as Imagos and Pixel Jam worked out the kinks and brought the title to Steam. Boy was it a fun ride!
Your first go into the world of Starr Mazer DSP is three randomly generated pilots smashing through a building to stop the oncoming Ge'll invasion. Recieving your orders from Cat Admiral similarly to what you would get from games like Star Fox back in the day, you fight your way through a horde of enemies all vying for the right to shoot you down. Cat Admiral reminds you fairly quickly how to use your weapons, just in case you forgot in flight school, then the waves really start coming. By collecting the "carbomite" that gets left behind from your kills, you power up your weapons and take the fight to them!
The enemies are varied, the waves are tough but fair once you learn a few tricks, but expect to die and die often. It will happen, and you will enjoy it. Seriously. I spent the first two hours of gameplay trying to get off of Act 1 Stage 2 before finally figuring it out. I don't think there was a time I thought the game was trying to cheat me, and I kept on buying new squads to try different tactics.
Speaking of tactics, this is a SHMUP so you just hold fire and dodge right? Nope! There are several different offensive weapons that you can choose from (some you "unlock" by buying new pilots) so there are a plethora of combinations and squad styles to choose from. The only limit is your SKORE, which is what you racked up in the first (or thirtieth) run through. Buy new pilots and send them out for more! Better pilots mean you should do better against the waves, you just have to decide what weapon is right for you!
Now, down to the gritty of this review.
Visuals are astounding. They remind you of the old school 8 bit games, but are cut so clean and colored so well, this is a place on even the highest definition monitor. Absolutely 10/10
Music is pretty special. There will be those that aren't into it, and thats fine, just turn the music off. But I don't know why you would. Again, we're going back to the 80s with old electronica sounds, but each track is thoughtfully put assembled and sounds crisp and smooth in your ears. 10/10
SFX are spot on. I wouldn't mind hearing some more variation in the weapons sounds for when you have a higher carbomite count and are doing more damage, but all in all, I'm quite happy with the sound. 9/10
Gameplay is smooth as butter. Different ships have different speed ratings, and you can definitely feel the difference in each one. Sliding from left to right attacking or dodging is crisp and responsive even to an old Logitech controller. If you're more in tune with playing via keyboard, thats definitely an option, however I haven't tried it. It just feels to good playing with a set of sticks than WASD, since thats what the Dev's aimed for. 10/10
Game length depends on your own personal skill level. You COULD beat the current stages in about an hour, if you're an excellent SHMUP player and only use the first three pilots you randomly get. If you can do that, I'd like to see it, please link me to the youtube or twitch channel. As it stands, I've got around 7 hours of play time in to the current build and I've yet to beat Act 2. And I'm really in no hurry to beat it either. Launch the title, play for a bit and if you make it, you make it. If not, come back for more tomorrow. You'll enjoy it each time.
Overall: 9.8/10 If it weren't for my minor quibble about more diverse audio, it'd be a perfect 10.
Disclaimer: I recieved this title for free, as I (along with several others) volunteered to test it before release.

For $19.99 I got a handful of minor new features, worse (IMO) graphics with more glitches, and a host of new bugs. All of the bugs I was hoping would be fixed are not.

If you have played the original game, you may be wondering if the remastered version is worth buying. There are no significant improvements to the game, it's still the same game with a few nice changes. These changes do make the game more enjoyable but are probably not worth the full price. Improvements include:
-Enhanced graphics and draw distance, and new textures. The graphics aren't significantly better, but the difference is noticable.
-Improved effects, with dust, fog, and fire effects...
-More animations have been added. Zed's move differently, and they changed the unarmed combat.
-Cleaner looking interface.
-Some of the features in Lifeline have now been added to the main game and Breakdown.
-A new mission type, with new special weapons.
-Grenade launcher attachement and incendiary shotguns.
-More vehicles and some new skins.
-One new character is included (if you bought the original game).
-You can now play as Hawkes, Kilo, Vince and Sasquatch. (More dialogue was recorded for Breakdown).
-More music in game.
-Increased number of Zeds.
There are still some problems with the game. Zed's can pass through doors, and there are pathing problems (Surviors can get stuck when trying to enter vehicles).  Unfortunately there is still no support for 4k or 2k monitors. I have a 1440p monitor and I find it dissapointing (and I'm sure I'm not the only one) that I have to play the game at 1080p.
It may be better to wait for a discount, before considering to buy this game. Having glanced at some of the negative reviews, I agree that this game is not a major improvement, and there are still the same bugs. I suggest you buy this game if you haven't bought the original (or you bought the base game but not the DLC). For others, I suggest you wait for a discount. I still like this game and the improvements (particularly the new mission type), but graphically I expected it to be better.

TL;DR: If you watch a playthrough on YouTube you will get exactly the same experience as playing the game.
It is, in fact, highly misleading to call this a game. This is a movie which requires you to click sometimes to advance the plot. "Game" implies that something the player does influences the experience. While you do control your character's movements, there is no decision-making process involved here: you go where the game tells you to go, look at what it tells you to look at, repeat until done. It feels like there is a game out there missing its tutorial; I kept waiting for MY turn to decide where the game should go.
That said, the setting is nice, the plot is actually kind of decent, and the script and voice acting are believable. If you want an immersive movie, this is not a bad one to buy.
But don't expect any sort of gaming experience from this; you won't find it here.

This is incredibly disappointing sequel.  I feel sorry that I have convinced my friends to buy this game, hoping we'll have as good time as we had in Magicka 1.
I was in love with Magicka 1, I've played it over 10 times. I also played Wizard Wars since alpha, for quite long time. Magicka 2 is like an inbred baby of these two, dropped to it's head in infancy and raised by alcoholics. It took cons from both these games, added a handful of bad solutions of it's own, and almost completely ignored everything good these games had.
Let's count the great things that already were in Magicka 1 that didn't made it into the sequel:
Steam and Ice are no longer individual elements, meaning you can't combine them with lighting element. This reduces amount of possible combos, and there is nothing to fill the void - developers has removed a feature and haven't added anything here.
Cool weapons - I admit I haven't played the game till it's end (and I'm not sure I will), but almost everything that was found in Magicka 1 felt awesome and gameplay changing. Thor's hammer, staff that regenerates health, staves with spells, machine gun, masters' sword, knife of counter-striking - everything was awesome. Here? After playing for 3 hours everything I found was boring stats weapons and staves. Weapon that adds little element dmg, stave that increases certain element dmg... Yawn.
I understand why these weapons would be in WW, since it's a PvP, but why ruin creative freedom of coop game?
Balance - granted, Magicka 1 was a bit easy at times, but it was completely possible for solo players. More than that, I've finished it multiple times even before the resurecting fairy update, it was challenging, but fun as hell. Here playing solo is difficult, repetitive and boring. Foes are numerous, fast, and often have one-shot-kill attacks. Great, huh?
Enchanted melee - I was disappointed when I learned that you can enchant melee weapons in WW, and was looking forward to it in Magicka 2. And it is here.. but it doesn't feels like it. It's week, range is laughable, and there is absolutely no reason to do it for offence.
Push - Magicka 1 featured a push spell. Simple, niche, but cool looking and effective where it was needed. Here? It's tier 1 magick with cooldown and long animation. It's a downgrade.
Awesomeness of magicks - Once again, I haven't seems them all, but what I've seen saddens me. Haste lasts for couple of seconds, napalm kills only weakest of foes, and there is COOLDOWN. A ♥♥♥♥ING COOLDOWN. In Magicka 1 you could spam spells. It was not always profitable and challenging, which is why it felt rewarding when you did that to a great effect. Here? Magicks looks like party tricks, not as powerful spells.
Story mode - it was silly in Magicka, but there was a story it was interesting to look at. In Magicka 2 story is much more nonsensical in a bad way, just being a sad excuse to throw some enemies at you, I've stoped paying attention to what's going on at chapter 3.
Seems plenty to me. Plenty of reasons not to buy this game.

A lukewarm recommendation.  It's a good, solid game...kind of a throwback even.  It feels more like a game released in 2007 instead of 2013, which isn't all bad.  But it's worth playing enough to see if the game draws you in.  But note that it sets up a sequel that may never be released.
PROS:
- good story
- good length; a fair amount of content
- glitch-free
- good Noir ambiance; you feel like you're in the era
- fully voiced
- I liked the "insights" system where you'd have to combine two facts you've picked up to draw a conclusion
- You can't screw something up so badly that you have to reload a save
- Trading cards
NEITHER PRO nor CON
- I didn't think the [English] voice acting was so bad...the protagonist in particular was sharp.
- Extremely linear.  Some will consider this a con, but it doesn't bother me.
- Mostly good puzzling; some were pretty obtuse or required real pixel hunting, but what do you expect from a point-and-click?  :)
CONS
- Feels old/dated: slow walking, low-resolution, awkward 3D elements
- Several times I knew exactly what I wanted to do, and tried doing it in what seemed like a perfectly reasonable way, but it wanted me to do it slightly differently.
- There were times where you needed information from something (e.g., by reading a newspaper), so you'd read it, but it wouldn't register unless you "looked at" (clicked) the area of interest.
- The story is incomplete (makes a reference to Face Noir II) but this game may never be made.  I was getting a little worried about where the plot was going anyway, so maybe it's just as well.
Anyway-- give it a try, with the caveats listed above!

Yeah, I can understand why this novel will receive some mixed reviews. It is however an intelligent piece of writing. It's also a grown up love story, yes, with some flaws, but serious and dramatic with a lot of hidden meanings and themes.
Why do you need to check it out? Well, some hi-lites include: various secrets, the haunting piano and jazz soundtrack, some funny and deeply damaged characters with almost upronounceable names and surnames, strip poker and (a very questionable) joyride and a team death match with guns, in a school.
I don't think this was originally written in English, and it felt if some things were lost in translation. At some points there is no distinction between characters words and dialogue, as if they are speaking from the same mouth and similar. Also, perhaps due to the translation, the story does tend to carry on about insignificant story details in the search of making it an epic. However, hang in there, in the end it all gets tied together.
It took me just over 7 hours to complete, and yes, I would have loved some game choices to spruce things up, but as the story went on, I realised I should have rather played chapter to chapter, saved regularly, take a break, think about the game, come back later refreshed and take it all in again, slowly.
Pros - A novel of this high quality free, including dlc soundtrack, is unbeleivable. A lot of hard work went into this, and it shows. Great and easy to read in game menus. Magnificent backgrounds and animation. Also some nice music from the moonlight piano, to something reminding me a lot of Charles Schultz's 'Peanuts', I thorougly enjoyd the classic and sometimes jazzy, soundtrack. Some beautiful themes about life and endings, and pain. A story within a story.
Cons - I didn't like the start of the game, it felt wrong, however ride (or read) it out, it gets better. With novel games the font, size and color is extremely important to me, and this game has a lot of backgrounds with brownish colours, and the font background is translucent, this caused some problems for me. There are also quite a few loose ends in the story for example what was up with the policman/barman/waiter/spy character and why the racial overtone? No in game choices, it's a movie in other words, even if your choices where liniar and cosmetic, this would have been apreciated.
Prepare some popcorn, and watch this on autoplay, no choices needed just save when you get tired and come back later, it will take some time, but if you stick with it you'll find a lot of heart and some genuinely haunting themes. 7/10

(I may or may not be crying as i'm typing this). I'm in disbelief. this game was not as long as "If My Heart Had Wings(Aerodynamics: the Visual Novel)", or as advanced, yet it has overtaken it as my number one favorite. what this game lacks in graphically superior cutscenes, it excels in almost every other aspect. right off the back we get characters with compelling motives and personalities, as well as a relatable protagonist. the plot's premise was familiar and cliche but this game takes it and rewrites its entire goddamn existence and purpose. a group of high school seniors learn a LOT of valuable lessons and information about each other as graduation approaches(play to figure out their relationships, history, and dynamics for yourself, heh). a completely separate score accompanies each background and scenario to establish and differentiate themselves. chapters are a reasonable length and the plot flows smoothly. the humor relies on sarcasm, lack of seriousness and sincerity, and so many references(to the outside world and to itself), that you'd think Deadpool hijacked the script. it all culminates, resembling a more realistic take on something so common. the introduction isn't overflowing with pointless exposition, the middle was admittedly the most enjoyable and settles you comfortably into the novel, and the ending is climatic as ♥♥♥♥. the incorporation of inarguably the most important lesson as the novel's foundation(title gives you a very insubtle hint), makes a lot of ♥♥♥♥ing sense and left my mouth visibly opened by how drastically my view of the main characters changed. not to mention, unless you closely follow the story, the twist is HUUUUUGE, yet phenomenal. this visual novel didn't need to be flashy or overdeveloped to deliver. the amount of substance from this free-to-play game shocks me immensely. with as many meaningful games as i've played, i won't lie(wink wink), it was almost impossible to think that i could even determine a favorite. I've made so many connections, and have been exposed to so many concepts, methods, styles, etc. i think i can appreciate and continue to play these games, despite what happens to my emotional state. a little prematurely optimistic, especially after my last review was deserveably a negative one. hey, i dropped reading actual books for a reason, ok. who knew that all it took to reinvigorate my interest in reading was to combine it with my favorite passion. everyone has a reason for doing something, y'know?

For this reason it requires quite a lot of patience and close attention from the reader. As it's a kinetic novel (no choices), those less patient, or those who won't get sucked-in by the story can easily get bored or confused. It also has quite a lot of symbolism and philosophical talk that some might find pretencious or overbearing.
Thankfully, I think the quality of the writing and the pay-off the ending offers are totally worth the effort. The dialogues and characters' thoughts are for the most part very well written and the author shows serious talent with some of the conversations and the fairy tail-style stories written by the protagonist. The English translation (the game was originally in Spanish) also feel pretty much perfect. From purely literary point of view, this was the best western-made VN I've read so far, even if people might question some storytelling choices in it or parts of the author's style.
Characters, although their actions and attitudes might feel strange at first, have a lot of charisma and charm, and you get to understand them much better when the plot gets resolved. As in many stories of this kind, the protagonist seems like the least appealing member of the cast, but he isn't just a jerk, he has his seriously considerate moments and once more, his behaviour becomes much more understandable after you finish reading.
Backgrounds are mostly photos with filter added to them, but they're servicable. Same goes to music, which wasn't very memorable for me, but never got in the way.
I have to agree with some of the criticisms in other reviews - the story felt a bit overstreched and the humour, while good, didn't mix that well with the heavy themes in the core story. Also, I think some parts of the mystery were never explained clearly enough and I had to read through some forum posts to fully understand it.

The art is pretty gorgeous, and I have to commend the devs for incorporating "Claire de Lune." Overall, the quality is great for a free game, but the story might leave you a bit confused until you actually think about it. If being actively engaged in reading and reflecting on content is what you like doing, this is the game for you.

Few things i like and things i dont like.
Likes: Good change of pace from usual racing. Good idea of race tracks. Gives off a new kind of high.
Dislikes: Needs to improve on building tracks (like the tutorial needs to teach players how to finish tracks, I couldn't finish nor save any tracks), there needs to be different types of racing vehicles, It felt like a mix between FWD and AWD, but turning mechanics was awkward. I would enter a corner like a FWD, but exit like an AWD. Also, I wanted to know whether or not the wings had any effect on turning, wind resistance, drag coefficients, and downforce. There should be a menu on types of vehicles to choose and characteristics, like different style wings (concentrating more on mid air speed, turning speed, road speed, etc) mainly for individual racing benefits and disadvantages, this would make players think twice before choosing the best type of settings for the race. Building race tracks need more improvement for versatility, I ended up with bunch of turns that I didn't want, instead i wanted loops, jumps, etc. This would be excellent if it could incorporate building tracks like "Trackmania," it gives more control over how a track can be created, deleted, modified. Also, I felt some major lag while turning. Like, as the game went on, the memory started to stack upwards, then the turning would delay, maybe because it had to save, and build up memory while racing. I played this on highest graphic settings. I would love to see updates to improve on this. Also, I would like to see "key bindings" in options, because it took me a while to find out what "C" button did. Also, sound settings need improvement, like sound vs. bgm music. I turned off sound but i kept hearing acceleration sounds, beeping sounds, etc. If the game allowed drifting, even in midair. I bet this game would hit at least, top 5 games of 2014-15.

Possibly one of my favorite game ever. Star Wars Republic Commando lets you lead Delta Squad.

If you're looking into this game, you should really get it.
It's a fantastic game, it has a pretty good story, unique weapons, and you play with your squad for most of the game.
The biggest part of the game is your squad. They're really amazing, you've scorch, sev, and fixer. They all have their specialties, and it's not super noticeable, but they do better than the others in their area. (Scorch- demolitions, fixer-computers/slicing, sev- weapons expert{sniping, anti-armor posts, turrets, etc.}) They listen to your orders, you can set them to do different things. You can have one guy sniping, one guy disabling the droid dispenser and still have the last one fighting head on with you. You can have them on the full offensive, you can have them staying in formation, you can have them moving carefully, ready to blow ammo into anything that moves.
Plus there's the Humour. Really there's some funny jokes in there. Gotta love scorch XD
There's a really unique weapon setup in the game, you can have 3 guns. There's your standardized pistol (infinite ammo, energy recharge), the standardized rifle (with sniping and explosives attachments), and then you can have a single enemy weapon. That could be anything an enemy drops, like a geonosian beam rifle (pretty much shoots a powerful beam of energy) or a trandoshan shotgun, or even a wookie bowcaster. There's also heavy weapons you can get, like the ACP Heavy Repeater or the Wookie Rocket Launcher. Personally, by the end of the game I really only used the pistol, and the rifle attachments if I really need to.
It also has a fair ammount of extra fun one time kind of stuff. Most of them come as a surprise, so I don't really wanna spoil it for you.
When you play, keep in mind how useful cover can really be. You have an energy shield, which recharges, and a pistol with infinite ammo. If you can find some good cover, you can use those two together and take out just about anything with relative ease.

Just played through this game again.
Being a little older, more experienced, not to mention with some time in the military now, I am happy to say that I am still blown away this game, now MORE than ever.
For those of you fellow nerds who grew up liking geeky stuff like Star Wars and Lord of the Rings, but ran away to the Army (or your respective service) to proove that you were a real man afterall: let me say that I feel like this game was made for us . . . both back then, and now.
And even if you weren't the biggest Stars Wars fan, let me break the theme of this game down for you: You are an elite clone soldier fighting for an intergalactic democracy trained by Mandolorian warriors, i.e. space Vikings, who raise you into an ancient warrior ethos and the skills necessary to royaly thrash every army of robots, space bugs and space lizards who even dare look at you side-ways. Still not interested?! Well, maybe you should move to France.
This game is a MATURE military/sci-fi tactical shooter. This is not your typical PG sci-fi game where you dress up as a "Thpace Troopfer" with a "totally rad lazer gun" to shoot at  "goober monsters from Mars". No. The content, the characters, the dialogue, the mechanics, EVERYTHING in this game tells me that the devs actually talked with military consultants to make this game right and quasi-realistic.
Let's talk about Delta Squad and their behavior. Not only do these guys use real communication with each otherand and you while in combat, but the&quot♥♥♥♥♥♥talk" banter these dudes mofos belt out makes me laugh out loud everytime I play through this game. They WILL call you out when you screw up . . . just like any type-A doorkicker would do to you in real life.
Playing this game, I don't feel the necessity to hide away in a dark room with the door locked to enjoy my nostalgia without being judged. This game is freaking badass! For example, my woman walks over while I'm playing and asks "what are you up to?", and I reply "knifing lizards in the face." Then she looks at my screen where trandoshan blood literally COVERS my helmet visor after I bury a blade into that unlucky SOB, and then order my squaddies to cap his buddies with their rifles. What other Star Wars game do you see blood? I think none. Not only was I not judged for playing a Star Wars game, but she thought it was cool.
Alright, I'll wrap this up by saying that if you are a gunfighter or service member or LEO or any other avergage joe who loves a good tactical shooter, but also wants to get in some Star Wars nostaliga, look no further than Republic Commando.

Most people think this is a quick cash-in, for developers to get some money fast by just adding zombies to any ♥♥♥♥ing existing game. It's not realy true.
The game has 5 levels, and is recommended to be played in co-op. I played it alone, and still liked it. You walk around from A to B destorying every zombie you see, with the lovely killcam we all love. You have all weapons that ever existed for Sniper Elite V2, no matter if you have DLC's or not. You can also find new weapons on your way, like shotguns, which is cool.
Despite being only 5 levels long (compared to SEV2, which has 10), the playtime is even longer, because the missions often last over 1 hour (!). This might get you kinda bored, because after the first ~40 minutes i was like "Please, let this level end, i do't want to die".
Despite the game being a shooter, its scary. There are programmed few zombies that have to jump out of a corner right at you, also on level four, sounds of little, really spooky (2spooky4me) girls assist you through the level.
The game has a good atmosphere of being really empty - since you are the last living soul in Berlin - despite having a lot of enemies.
Pros:
- Playtime equal or longer than the regular game
- Good atmosphere
- All and more weapons
- Scary
- Is not a DLC - Sniper Elite V2 not needed to play.
Cons:
- Levels sometimes too long
- The Sniper Rifle is somtimes useless because you ahve to waste one precious bulet for 1-3 zombies, while your secondary weapon and pistol have much more ammo.
- Too green >_<
Would definately recommend.

Some advice to beginners:
- This is not your common FPS; do not run everywhere, it will only confuse your team-partners and they will be afraid to shoot you. Take a position and stand it, dodge with small movements. Do not cross fire unless your partner clearly understood your intentions. Otherwise, stay behind him.
- Do not panic. Panicking is your worst enemy in this game and it will kill you. If you are overwhelmed, find a wall and shot at the aliens from there. Avoid staying in the middle of a room unless your team-partners cover your flanks.
- Know your weapon. Each weapon has strong points and weaknesses. For example, the Tech-prototype rifle has auto-targeting, very good for shooting the buzzers (the flying insectoids). The heavy-gun bullets pass through the aliens, good for taking out large waves.
- Parasites and eggs are your worse nightmare, they are always the highest priority, at all times, if you see one. Once infected, the medic is the only one who can save your life. Or maybe an electrified armor if you have one.
- The medic is one of the most important jobs, make sure to know how it works when you pick this class or it will greatly bother your team-partners if they die because of your lack of competence.

Hover is a very colorful, enjoyable and relaxing Open-Worl Multiplayer Freeruning Game.
The freerunning mechanics are deep enough to be enjoyable for a long time without being super complex (a bit simpler than Mirror's Edge). Running, jumping and sliding around in the colorful and weird sci-fi city doesn't get old fast.
The biggest downside is the rpg element of the game: You can collect and equip chips of different types and quality, which give you various stat boosts. While this gives you a feeling of progression and also allows you to customize your character, it also means that the balancing is gets way off depending of the situation. If you go back to earlier races after leveling up your character, challenges become trivial. If you progress too far without having strong enough chips, challenges will be impossible to beat.
Even worse: For the multiplayer part of the game, it means that players can have a significant advantage over others, which can make races very one-sided.
The multiplayer in general feels tagged on and not well fleshed out: People can join missions you start. You don't necessarily want this to happen, though. If you do a race for yourself, you just have to beat a certain time-limit to complete the mission, collect the reward and progress in the story. If you play against other players, you have to win the race AND beat the time-limit. If you go second, you fail the mission. This discourages you from playing with others.
Contrary to that there are ball-game missions where you have to throw balls in to containers to score points. If other players join in those missions, they will actually play with you and they are usually way more competent than your AI allies. While this is a good addition to the game, I've been told, that ball-game missions in the later part of the game become so hard, that they are basically unwinnable with AI teammates.
Everything else in the game is awesome. The music, the art, the freerunning...it's just a lot of fun to traverse the city, find collectables and complete missions.
I recommend the game as a fun, relaxing chill-out game to play while listenening to music, watching videos or talking to friends.
It definitely holds some challenges for players who want to master the controls as well but other games like Mirror's Edge or Cloudbuilt do it better.

This is half of a good game. There is a large and pretty city, but because you can only run, and never walk, it feels like a playground and never like a real place. The parkour controls are very responsive but movement is very floaty. You can't make short jumps, only medium and long jumps.
