The level design is a poor fit for the floatiness, with some areas requiring precision that the controls can't provide.
The main problem is the lack of aim. I have no idea who my character is or what they hope to achieve. Other characters talk at me, never with me, as my character never gets to speak. There is no map (that I found) so it's hard to get a sense of place. A character told me to meet her "above the city", with no more details. Nothing in the game tells me where to find her. There is a bunch of items, upgrades, and character traits that are never explained; I literally have no idea what they do.
This feels more like a tech demo than a finished game. As a demo it's impressive; as a game it's aimless, awkward and unfulfilling.

Face Noir is a 2.5D detective point and click adventure with a grim sepia filter and serious atmosphere. You will play as a private eye – Jack Del Nero, who somehow lives from day to day like most people after the collapse of the New York Stock Exchange. His only pleasure are cigarettes and whiskey, which he generally can’t afford and his job as a private detective doesn’t earn much. But one day he answers the call from his old colleague, who was involved in a pretty tangled cobweb of underworld.
The story begins at the end to entice you, then of course you will play retrospectively to find out why it happened. Because I don’t want to spoil the whole story, let’s continue with parameters, which can be reviewed without interfering with the plot.
3D characters have slightly more sophisticated Max Payne’s graphic. The textures are visibly more balanced. Well, there’s a difference of 12 years so it’s not an objective comparison, but I mentioned it only as a metaphor. Character’s facial expressions are horrible, but you honestly can’t expect more here (it’s technically impossible). I personally really didn’t mind the lack of facial expressions, even though it has lowered the seriousness and emotionalism of the situations. However the whole graphic is in the well chosen sepia tone, which underlines the depressive undertone of the game.
As every adventure game this one has mini games and tasks too. Does Face Noir have some atypical elements? I can think of one mechanism – you collect thoughts by examining various subjects and obtaining information, which you can lately match together in order to get new conversation topics or it can lead you to a crucial track of the investigation. Otherwise, the mini-games are not significantly different from other adventure games.
As a player you don’t have any freedom. The game is exactly scripted and if you don’t complete everything in the correct order, there’s no way to get further in the story, even if you know what to do. This game simply doesn’t care that you as an experienced point-and-click player know, what is expected of you, here the game decides what’s next. E.g. You know that you need to go into that locked dark alley, but Jack won’t go there, because it doesn’t make sense to him. So you have to convince him that he actually wants to go there. Sounds interesting, right? Sometimes I had the feeling that Face Noir is pulling my leg, because I somehow always missed the right point and found it after I walked around all possible locations, I made a circle and returned to the same location, but this time I was successful. Anyway, I appreciate the opportunity to speed up the character movement with a double-click.
If you are handy and easily progress through the game, you will soon realize that it’s pretty dynamic. You won’t play as Jack the whole time and you will find out that what seemed to be realism turned out to actually be a magical realism.
My Italian vocabulary of four words – grande, italiano, grazie and arrivederci have expanded by another word - dannazione! Jack will use it so many times that you will never forget it. I don’t blame him, I would be cynical and negative too if I were him. But what I definitely don’t find negative is the English voice acting. I think that the voices fit to the characters and the music is also appropriately chosen.
I rank Face Noir among the games that didn’t really impress me, but didn’t really disappoint me in the same time. But what really did upset me is the end. I don’t mind the open end, but I mind that at the end I was acquainted with a sequel - Face Noir 2, which I wanted to play because I obviously am interested in how the story turns out. But instead I found out that Face Noir 2 was never released. I don’t know what happened, maybe the development team broke up, anyway, I as a player feel cheated. Of course, this fact doesn’t affect the evaluation of Face Noir, on the contrary, my disappointment is a compliment, because I'm interested in the sequel.
Score: 57/100

I remember when I was a small wee child, back when I was shorter than most grown adults. I remember the smell and feel of grease in the air, the hotness off the deep fry vats, the diversity in culture and strangers met at the local fish and chip shop. Most iconic-ly what I remember from those days, The Arcade Machine.
Imagos Softworks who has now Teamed up with PixelJam Studios who never fail to deliver in retro or nostalgia bring us this new game ‘Starr Mazer : DSP’ to fit in the retro and nostalgic lines. Bringing nostalgia of the games I played back then, where you flew around as a jet blowing up UFO's and such picking up weapons and generally trying to avoid bullets, Starr Mazer remains it's own unique features and play style to the star fighter shoot'em'up genre. With a weapon power and upgrade system the makes you think about how You use your resources and try to skillfully manoeuvre around the screen to try and combine said resources for the BIG points this is one that will have arcade fans sitting at their computers for some hours as they b last through hoards of the alien scum known as the G'ell.
The geniuses at pixel jam also thought of a way in which you can ‘pay’ by using the score you accumulate to buy more lives, much to the liking of inserting all your spare change in to the much loved to this day arcade machines. This fantastic feature is not only addicting to use but wont leave your pockets penniless.
True to arcade nature there is only one difficulty and that's hard mode. Can't say i'm to upset about missing difficulty slider the games extensive content of 2 ACTS is meant to be enjoyed in a challenging and fun experience.
But wait don't go anywhere i have more to say! Adding on to the nostalgic experience are many quotes and movie references from iconic games/movies such as “Duke Nukem” and “FireFly(Serenity)”
9.9/10 from me, would like to have seen remap-able key options but hey guess I'm fussy. In the end it's a good game worthy of much praise and lived up to all my expectations after watching the shorts for it. Great work Imagos and PixelJam!

Really enjoyed the game when I first started it. There seemed to be a good background story, excellent voice-acting by the two main characters, great environment to explore - atmospheric lighting and mist/smoke and ambient sounds and event/location-triggered music.
As time went by, game-play became a little repetitive and on the verge of being boring. But occasionally something unexpected would happen, or you'd discover a hidden 'treat', which would get you going for a while.
Much is hinted at in the way the plot unravels depending on the answers you give in radio conversations with your boss, Delilah - but I found this only seemed to affect subsequent conversation rather than the plot itself.
Having played it through three times (and once you know where the locations are, you can zip through the game in under 2 hours or so) -and taking different attitudes towards Delilah and my character's 'estranged' wife in the attempt to manipulate a different ending, or series of events, I couldn't. I think this is a trick lost by the authors, it would have made the game so much more interesting and made for very much better 'replayability'.
For example, travel throughout the forest and mountains could have been made more interesting with small surprises to break your walk - eg, glimpses of wildlife, interacting with other rangers or perhaps tourists.
And the tension could have been increased with even simple distant glimpses of shadowy figures, reflections off their binoculars in the trees... just something that made you feel you weren't simply yomping from one event or trigger-point to the next.
No harm of any kind (other than hard-scripted into the story) can come to your character - why not add a risk element that might hamper the character's search, or even put him in harm's way which might even end the game or level?
In the end, it played like an animated graphic novel, rather than a video game. Well written, well acted and actually quite poignant and moving. I enjoyed it admired many of the production values, but was left feeling it could have been just a little bit more. Having gone through it three times, I won't play it again.

rom Keinart Lobre comes One Thousand Lies, a free to play, visual anime game. Released in 2016, you follow the story of Ciaran Ednyein who lives a pretty simple life. One day, he gets a mysterious email and must find out who sent it, and send him on an adventure to learn about love and life.
I was recommended this by the Steam Store and it was apparently similar to other games I had played, like Trick and Treat and Elisa: The Innkeeper Prequel. I had enjoyed both of these games and decided to get this to give it a try and see what it was like. This was not like either of the games Steam said it was.
This is purely a book. There's no play features about it. You read the text and the speech and progress through the game purely to see what happens. I was bored within minutes. There's no choices, there's nothing for the player to actually do, other than skim the text.
Eventually, I just put autoskip on to complete the game and get the achievement because I didn't even care enough about the characters to even sit and read it all through, and sat writing reviews whilst the game completed itself. Ultimately, it took 12 minutes, and the Store page says it takes 5-10 hours? I think not.
I don't think that has anything substantial to hold itself as game. I'm surprised the rating for it is so high. Luckily, the achievement is easy enough to grab so if you want to collect another completed game, maybe just grab this and skip everything for the achievement.
The achievement being easy is the only decent thing about this game.

One of the most beloved American films, this captivating wartime adventure of romance and intrigue from director Michael Curtiz defies standard categorization. Simply put, it is the story of Rick Blaine (Humphrey Bogart), a world-weary ex-freedom fighter who runs a nightclub in Casablanca during the early part of WWII. Despite pressure from the local authorities, notably the crafty Capt. Renault (Claude Rains), Rick's cafÃ (C) has become a haven for refugees looking to purchase illicit letters of transit which will allow them to escape to America. One day, to Rick's great surprise, he is approached by the famed rebel Victor Laszlo (Paul Henreid) and his wife, Ilsa (Ingrid Bergman), Rick's true love who deserted him when the Nazis invaded Paris. She still wants Victor to escape to America, but now that she's renewed her love for Rick, she wants to stay behind in Casablanca. "You must do the thinking for both of us," she says to Rick. He does, and his plan brings the story to its satisfyingly logical, if not entirely happy, conclusion.

In light of the bad reviews I've seen for this game, let me give a positive one.
Disclaimer: I've only had a chance to play breakdown thus far, so I have no comments on the main game quest or on lifeline, but I expect like everything else they will be like the original.
Summary:  If you enjoyed the original game, this version gives improved graphics and perhaps a tiny bit more gameplay stuff.  If you expected anything different than that, I don't know what to tell you.
The game plays like the original game, because *gasp* it is the original game.  All that was promised was improved graphics and a few little tidbits to make the game more fun.  It's basically a textures overhaul mod you'd expect to see for Skyrim, except its official.
I've heard complaints about the bugs, and all I can say is that they were neither better nor worse than the original game.  I'm guessing they were bugs that are driven by intricacies of the Cryengine version used be SOD, but that's just conjecture (it's all physics related and a few random crashes that honestly shouldn't happen, but I couldn't care less.)
As for the improved graphics, I noticed a huge improvement.  Everything was far less dingy, and undead labs seriously toned up the lighting.  While I can sort of get the realism of not being able to see at night, I'm glad they fixed it because for me the game was virtually unplayable during 'night'; if you want to be unable to see for 50% of the game I would then of course recommend the original.
They probably added new character traits, and definitely added new shirts and pants and hats.  This mixes up what sort of characters you will see and increases playability.  Similarly the vehicles were diversified and given new textures, which again makes for more replayability since there are more than 6 distinct cars in the valley.
I did in fact notice the higher res textures.  The original was grainy as heck.  The menu and maps have been cleaned up significantly, which is really good.  I'm so glad they kept the physical journal interface (the game menus look like pages in a notebook) ====== very cool UI.  Plus you can now tell which item you have selected!
In closing, the Year One edition is worth it if you liked the original game (or if you never played it, I suppose).  If you go in expecting a vastly different setting and feeling and a bug free game, then you'll be disappointed.
Good luck, it's a brutal game.

Face Noir captures anyone easily in its world of noir tropes, but to enjoy that, you have to deal with the typical point ‘n’ click logic, the slow controls, subpar voice acting, and that… interesting ending.
The title of Face Noir is very apt: it takes every noir detective story cliché known to mankind and pushes it right into the player’s face at full force.
We are talking about clichés such as a mysterious phone call, a murder that the police is trying to pin on the alcoholic ex-cop private detective protagonist, and of course a case where the threads lead to the highest circles of the city — everything would fit a Philippe Marlow novel except the motive (which would go well with Indiana Jones instead). And, of course, I have to mention that anyone buying the game has to live with the fact that it ends with a cliffhanger, and the chances for a sequel are… slim.
The presentation is a little difficult to rate. The exposition dump dialogues are part of the noir setting, and the writing is mostly acceptable. The voice acting isn’t bad, not at all, but it sounds more like some amateurs and family members doing their best to try to act than actual actors playing roles. (The audio quality is terrible though.)
Game mechanics are painfully simplistic: look at items, pick up items, and use items. For the most part, progress is logical, albeit suffers from the ancient adventure game design problem that doesn’t want to finally die: every single action requires several trips to different spots of the city, even to do simple tasks as making a phone call.
There is one addition that brings some novelty, the deduction parts, where the player has to select two previously acquired facts out of many to reach a conclusion. They are a welcomed change of pace, even if their contribution to the 9-11 hour game time is negligible compared to the constant travelling.

The short review is that the game is fantastic. It's priced at $10 as of the writing of this review, and it's worth it, but getting on sale would be better!
Except for one point, the story was excellent, the feel of the game was great and very immersive in 1930s New York, the soundtrack kicked butt, the puzzles were intelligible (I knew exactly what to do most of the time, but there was just the right amount of difficulty in getting it done), and I thought the humor of the protagonist was fantastic, but I like dry humor. The connect-the-dots mechanic was pretty inventive, I thought and added a good detective story even better, IMHO. The mannequins were probably the worst part of the game because they sometimes looked or did things that weren't right, but almost all point and click adventure puzzles suffer from this. My second complaint would be all the Dannazionis that were liberally peppered throughout the game. It was a bit overused.
To address some complaints about the story being too linear or limiting in that I can't grab an object or do something now, but can later on when the story advances, I actually thought it made sense and, once again, is something most point and click adventure games do. I actually didn't mind because I viewed it as a story-focused game and that stream-lined it so that I could enjoy the story instead of getting caught up in picking up a bunch of useless stuff that I didn't need and wouldn't use.
SPOILER ALERT AHEAD!
The one thing I didn't like about the story was the paranormal element that was thrown in regarding the girl. While she is basically the MacGuffin for Face Noir, there is this allusion to her being able to control time and dreams and that she is going to do something supernatural in the sequel. This kind of threw me out of the immersiveness that the rest of the game established so well. The supernatural really has no place in a good noir story. Read any of the hard-boiled detective writers like Raymond Chandler, Dashell Hammett, and Mickey Spillane that typified the detective/Noir writing and none of them ever got caught up in that stuff. I also thought that its introduction in the last 1/3 of the game kind of blindsided me after being so true to the hard-boiled detective genre for the first 2/3 of the game.
I do look forward to Face Noir II, though. Great job!

I love this game. I really do, but it does have some issues with it that can be frustrating at times. Republic Commando was originally released back in 2005 alongside a Star Wars novel title "Hard Contact." The game has the Star Wars music and sound effects you would expect from a Star Wars game and recreates the weapons that the commandos use in the book and subsequent ones that followed. (The books are pretty good BTW and if you're itching for more of Delta squad I highly recommend you check them out.) However, the AI at times can be frustrating as well as some enemies/situations that you will die on multiple times before you manage to beat them. The game is also pretty short in my opinion and I wish we would have been able to see more of the Star Wars universe. Overall though I would give it a 7.5 out of 10 and I would by it at it's current cost.

Republic Commando is a high action look into the Star Wars universe through the eyes of a special clone commando unit. This is a great shooter where you control your squad to kill droids and complete missions that took place during the clone wars.
Each new area you visit is unique and presents a challenge as you lead your very own clone squad on special missions. Telling them to take up positions and stratigising adds a fun layer to the already excellent combat.
Solid gameplay with no unresonable dificulty jumps, weapons for every occasion, and well crafted enviroments. Also, it is fun to listen to the commandos in your unit talk trash to the droids and make funny remarks.
A well made shooter, all in all. I say its worth getting.

This game shows a grittier and more tactical side of the Star Wars universe. In the beginning you are dropped into the infamous battle of Geonosis, where small squads of battle droids dot the path ahead. Soon enough you meet your squadmates, one by one, along the battlefield. Eventually you will find yourself and your squad fighting through all hell in droid supercomplexes, racing through to the bridge in an attempt to keep yourself from blowing up. You often find yourself stacked against impossible odds, whether laying out the red carpet for the biggest invasion in Star Wars history, or investigating a Republic ghost ship, left abandoned in a remote sector, haunted by a deadly secret.
Republic Commando is definately a good game for fans of the harder 'nothing like a blaster at your side' side of Star Wars. There aren't Jedi plagueing battlefields like bantha fodder. An ever widening arsenal from different styles and speices is what gets you through. But you can't rely on only your own weapons to keep you breathing. Your three squadmates will do almost anything you ask, though the pathfinding has some issues, they rarely cost you much. The four characters interact beautifully with each other, often Sev and Scorch take shots at each other, but you can tell that they are the best of friends. Sometimes some enemies seem way overpowered, and unreasonable fight scenarios dot the game.
Personally this game is one of my favorites. It is a great stress reliever and adds some different perspectives to my favorite fictional universe. Weapons are balanced well, although enemies can be unreasonably strong. A few pathfinding bugs dot the game, but don't really ruin the game. Characters and enemies often have one-liners that offer comic-relief, yet don't destroy the serious tone that this game was built around.
TL;DR:
Good Game
Few Bugs
10/10

Growing up as a gamer, this is without a doubt in my mind one of the games I owned that rocked me to my core. This game redefined the fps genre for me, instead of being shoot everything until they are dead as some faceless nigh-invincible killing machine you had to craft your squad of surprizingly intelligent elite commandos into a perfect killing machine. Star Wars or not, to this day this is the best executed squad-based single player fps that I have ever seen. It even had elements that modern games took on years later like reviving incapicitated teammates with a bacta gun, both Battlefield and Killzone have this to very similar degrees. Though this game shows its age at this point in that it feels like a classic fps rather than a modern one, it is still an incredibly unique experience for any lover of Star Wars, sci-fi games, or fps's in general. The characters are likable and humorous, the environments are really cool, and the game has such a great sense of lighting and mood. Star Wars Republic Commando is one of my favorite and most nostaligic games. Its my Golden Eye, but it's actually still fun. Very. Very. Very fun. It should be up there with greatest Star Wars games along with the Jedi Knight series, and it will always have a special place in my heart. Okay that was a little too gooey. Umm... it kicks♥♥♥♥♥and you should give it a try. The mulitplayer servers are still running too, I think, so you know its got to be good if people are still playing it. Anyway, this game is worth the try. Period. Thanks for reading.

It is been 4 years since the first game in this franchise took the world by storm. Its gem you ask? The unique spellcasting mechanic that is. In Magicka you could combine 8 elements to create unique spells to fight with. Together with 4 ways to cast them. Death or Life turns every spell into a beam, add shield to create bombs, or use shield without it to create a wall.
Magicka 2 redesigned this system with what they have learned from this games multiplayer counterpart Magicka: Wizard Wars. They have tried to get rid of the redundancy of spells present in preceding titles. They did a sufficient job, Death used to removes lightning unique feature of hopping from enemy to enemy. Magicks are available to cast directly instead of having to sequence the elements, although the option is still available and reduces the cool down timer significantly. while having to  It is all wrapped in a new story which feels much more alive than before. And yes it is still packed with popular references and memes.
However the game is still packed with unused mechanics, quite a shame. The game never forces you to think of new spells. Enemies have nothing more than a weakness or strength. This, together with the short tutorial forcing player to remember everything in one go. Results in some unsatisfying gameplay, repeating one spell over and over again. Sadly  people never use complex combination like ice or steam because a simple spell does the job just as well. The same goes for the different ways to cast a spell, cast around you and cast weapon are completely abandoned as soon as the tutorial finishes.
This is all not to say that I didn't enjoy the game! The game is fantastic and with a group of friends turns in one of the most hectic games to date. The game stand firm in line of the Magicka series and deserves a strong recommendation. I just hope the developers figure out a way to reduce redundancy even more, may there ever be another game.

It's a free visual novel that takes 7-8 hours to read.
There are themes of drama, romance, humor, and philosophy. The story is told in the first person perspective and there are no branching paths or choices to make.
I felt that the artwork and music were well done. However, the actual story itself is not going to appeal to everyone, so I'll briefly cover the good and bad:
THE BAD:
On the surface it's a tale about some juvenile delinquents and their interpersonal relationships. The kids do quite a few illegal things (breaking and entering, constant truancy, carjacking, ect) but they are seldom caught, and even when they are caught they are seldom actually punished.
This was a sore point for me because I was constantly thinking to myself, "If I had done that in high school I would have been expelled immediately!" In short, it hurt my suspension of disbelief and nearly caused me to give up reading the novel several times. This issue is actually addressed at the end of the novel, but I feel by that time any reader who had been wavering on this issue would have put the book down long ago.
Also, the novel starts slowly and takes a while to really get moving which was unfortunate.
THE GOOD
On the bright side the novel has some great character development. The characters are mostly interesting and they all grow and change over the course of the story. There are no superflous characters that clutter up the narrative which is a good thing. Some of the humor was pretty funny too.
I noticed no major spelling or grammar issues.
Please note that the story is not actually done when you finish the final chapter. Instead there is an epilogue which can be accessed from the main screen. Completing the epilogue will award you the game's single Steam achievement.
If you like visual novels this might be worth checking out!

A sequel should add to the experience, not take away. There are so many things that Magicka 2 lacks compared to the first one which makes it not very enjoyable to someone who loved the craziness of Magicka. The changes in Magicka 2 seem to be appealing to a people who are use to MOBAs or more casual gameplay. I've found three main things that makes Magicka 2 feel this way to me: Cooldowns, Non-combining elements, and Streamlined feel. I'm sure I'm missing some things, but these are the main issues I had with Magicka 2.
Cooldowns: Remember spamming Conflageration to deal massive damage to crowds? How about raising an army of zombies and elemental guardians? With Cooldowns on the spells, these can no longer happen. This makes the game artificially more difficult rather than naturally. In Magicka 1, learning how to execute spells quickly and accurately allowed you to be much more successful while feeling like a true wizard. Cooldowns and having a hotbar for instantly casting them takes away from the challenge of memorizing spells so you can cast the right spell as quick as possible. I think ifthe developer made it so you could have up to 7 elements on your hotbar, it would allow for a lot more interesting element combinations as setting up for some really strong spells for those who are capable of executing them.
Non-Combining Elements: WIth elements like frost/water or fire/water not becoming ice or steam in the casting bar not only makes spells shorter and simpler, it can be confusing for new players to the series. When casting a spell that requires making steam, having a visual icon show up when the right elements combine lets the player know they have it set up. When casting complex spells, that icon also helps to show you you've cast the elements in the right order. It was an unnecessary change that really impacts the gameplay.
Streamlined Feel: They made this game feel sort of like an RPG with the addition of a progression system.The progression system lets players unlock items like robes and weapons as they play. It lets players unlock more items without paying money. I'm not saying this is a bad thing, in fact it's one of the things I like about Magicka 2. My issue is with what they took out of the customization along with how the menus feel. Something seemed off about it when I first saw the menu, and it reminded me of games some critics review which are actually ports. After a while I realized it reminded me heavily of a mobile port due to the giant buttons and fonts.I was a little worried, but I continued on to the single player anyway. My favorite part of Magicka was the variety of robes and colors for them, and I was excited to see how Magicka 2 did the customization. When I got to the wizard customizer, at first it looked great, but then I clicked on the colors. There are only around 6 different colors to choose from compared to the great number in Magicka 1. They also won't let you change your name once you've picked one for your wizard. (Oh well I guess). The lack of robes and weapons I could understand since it just came out.
It's not all terrible. The movement system is a little more dynamic now since you can move and cast spells at the same time. The progression system is nice as well. There's just so many other things that make the sequel feel lacking compared to the first. It's a shame a great classic has such a lacking sequel.

While the new controls took me a bit to get used to coming from the first game, still a fun game with all the quirky nerd-humor of the first.  There are some spell changes that are a bit irksome (the lack of steam deathbeam comes readily to mind), but most of these come across as a means to tone down certain fairly overpowered spell combinations; nerfing them wouldve been preferable but it is by no means game breaking.

Oof... This game is one of these cases when I really wish there was a neutral recommendation button. I don't want to give the devs a negative one as they clearly devoted a lot of time and effort to deliver a well made final product, but at the same time I do want to say a few words about it and I cannot say I would personally recommend it.
What was my fault was, I didn't notice it was a kinetic novel while downloading it. I saw tons of good reviews and a "Visual Novel" tag - and, since it was free at the same time, that was all I needed to install the game. I'm a fan of making choices and influencing the story, and in case of kinetic novels, I'd much prefer if they were made into comics, or books/short written stories. A lot of the scenes seemed much too long for me, and, with the repetitive, unchanging backgrounds, it almost felt like a chore to read through them - but, since I started, I wanted to know what the ending will be.
As someone pointed out in another review, all of the story comes to a conclusion within the last minutes of the whole game - that's when it actually gets interesting - but the previous hours, they do feel pretty bland. It was all needed for the ending, all right, but I really wish the narration was, if not sped up, made a bit more... dynamic? Captivating? I don't really know; I'd experiment with the form, possibly adding more full pictures on the way and changing the backgrounds within a single scene - maybe zooming or panning them accordingly to what's going on?
I cannot say, however, that I didn't like any of the story preceeding the ending. The humor was pretty good  - I liked the class clowns therater, the food ordering competition and the Baldy ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ - even if he was a totally random character, not needed for the story itself; he made a nice 'LOL'-evoking addition.
As for the art - the character art was really great, looking at the sprites was really pleasant. I didn't like the full art pages as much, but they were good, too. What I didn't like were backgrounds being photos with some filter thrown onto them; having created a vn-like project myself, I know drawing backgrounds can be a real pain, but at the same time, they really make a difference. I can't say much about the music, as I had it muted down most of the time; the other times I didn't really notice it. I recall one or two tracks I really liked appearing somewhere near the ending.
I had that feeling One Thousand Lies tried to tackle a more philosophical theme using a normal, laid-back story, only getting more serious at the ending and few times throughout the play that felt too long and out of place for me; there was also main character's story. Personally I'd prefer if the whole thing was kept in the serious tone and was made shorter without beating around the bush so much, but I understand what the creator wanted to achieve. If you like kinetic novels and don't mind the slow pace, I'm sure you'll like it; if you prefer concentrated essence of your tale, stronger emotions or the ability to influence the story at all, you'll probably not be much interested in it.

Yes I gave it a thumbs up, because the game itself is fun and enjoyable. However,  lot of the negative reviews addressing the ridiculous F2P grab from publishing company Trion are warranted and should be expected from any Trion game. As a player who enjoys most of their games I can usually say it is easy to overlook marketplace items. However in the case of Devilian, paying to unlock a skill set...has everyone at Trion lost their friggin minds? Are Austin's utilities that bad to the point we are charging what should be base game mechanics as luxury items. I have seen you do some horrible things with past games and compensations for players who actually purchased game copies, but this is way below the belt.
Here we have Devilian, a very fun Diablo/Torchlight/Dungeon Siege clone MMO. Decent graphics, can be played on lower than spec equipment, IE I have tested this game on a ASUS Transformer Tablet and an older Dell Inspiron 9400 C2D w Nvidia 7800gs Go. And both run excellently, given the fact that th resolutions are lowered a bit. Storyline is a bit standard but quests and side quests are bountiful and keep a player from needing to endlessly & mindlessly grind to reach their next level.

The gameplay itself is very fast and fluid like a MMOARPG should be. Almost reminding me of Dekaron (still the best example of MMOARPG mechanics, Dekaron
). And a few of the ideas standout and are more attuned to MMOARPG players than classic MMORPG players. I just hope those of you at Trion can take cues from better publishers/hosting companies and learn how to run a marketplace without hugely impacting core gameplay.

The  original State of Decay was a combination of everything i wanted from a zombie survival game. Building a community, scavenging resources and improving your living conditions during an apocalypse. It had it's own charm and all the annoying things about it (especially the bugs) were tolerable when you considered how small a developer Undead Labs was.
Yet i can not recommend this version of the game to anyone, not even people who haven't played the "non-remastered" version.
The original version got rid of a lot of bugs through patching but most of those are back in the YOSE edition with the addition of way more annoying new ones (car hit detection where you drive through a whole zombie horde without hurting a single one). A lot of obvious design flaws were not corrected (like adding a simple sorting function to your base inventory) and the visual improvements are nice in comparison but not that noticeable. And for a "polished" version, the framerate is horrendous, even on a decent system.
I ended up reinstalling the original SoD, since it has fewer bugs and a lot of awesome mods available, that make the game more enjoyable (and from which the developers should have drawn inspiration on how to improve their game).
If Undead Labs will patch it to a playable state and add a little mod support, i'll give it another whirl. Until then, this prime example of a money grab stays off my hard drive.
#Update 31.10.2015
Apart from a small hotfix right after release, the developer did not address any issues for a full six months.
Thankfully modders have not been idle and there are some nice additions and fixes out there that makes it feel like i didn't totally waste my money on this purchase.
Now only recommended if you don't own the original and don't mind searching for and installing mods and community made fixes by yourself.

As a returning player who loved the original State of Decay, let me be honest here, this is a completely unnecessary, controversial re-release that brings nothing of real value that would be so significant compared to the original that it would deserve its own release and the price, even with 33% discount is still way TOO much in terms of value for returning players.
YOSE keeps crashing to desktop and overall feels as a slower, less optimized and just more bugged version compared to the original. People who purchase this game as newcomers to SoD "franchise" as well as the returning players deserve smooth and flawless gameplay for the money these developers ask for this game, unfortunately if you think that you're getting flawless game for your hard earned money, I have to disappoint you by saying you better forget it.
As for the "remaster" aspect of this re-release, promise of the high quality textures is one of the biggest lies and not only you can see it for yourself in the parts of the game where textures are just ugly and you can't quite recognize what are you even looking at, but also according to developers themselves, PC release is smaller than Xbox One release because in PC release they didn't need to upgrade as many textures to higher quality as they needed to upgrade for Xbox One. This is interesting. Now I don't really own Xbox One, but I wonder if the Xbox One players really have the same ugly textures that show here in my PC version and while the fact that they did not upgrade as many textures for PC as they upgraded for Xbox One should naturally mean significantly lower price on PC, the price is the same even though the value added compared to original is clearly not that significant at all.
Smaller difference in the quality compared to original equals smaller reason for anyone on PC to upgrade to YOSE, but wait. Can you really stay away of this re-release and just enjoy the original? According to some players, the original game won't launch for them anymore and as a matter of fact, the original game and its dlcs are replaced with YOSE, so there is no way to purchase the original anymore and no way for original owners to get the support unless they purchase YOSE! So much for optional purchase for the original owners...
Let us put that aside and let me say what most of us think anyway, but nobody had the guts to say it out loud:
Real fans of SoD expected more from the SoD "franchise" than just a re-release of the same thing they already have and losing the support for the original is a legitimate reason for fans of the original SoD to be mad as they are basically forced to upgrade to YOSE and pay for the same thing again if they don't want to lose support.
In other words, for original fans it feels like being stabbed in our backs and I'm pretty sure that we all will remember this and keep it in mind from now on every time these developers bring a new game of any name.
EDIT:
To be completely fair, I love the little things they added exclusively for original owners and those who pre-order this game (new character who is already one leveled-up badass with unique weapons for original owners and special prepper pack for those who pre-ordered the game) and I also love CLEO items, but it still isn't that significant change that would justify the re-release and especially the price and just like many already said, not only bugs aren't fixed at all, but they somehow managed to introduce new bugs and crashes to desktop that basically render this overpriced re-release unplayable, isn't a "definitive edition" supposed to be clean of all the bugs present in the standard one?
Speaking of bugs, here is a little peek...
As an owner of the original release, I would be willing to pay for all the new stuff in form of a regular DLC as an optional "update" even if the price was slightly higher than a regular DLC, but the current price is a ripoff even with 33% discount.

Alright, so, though I have barely scratched the surface of this game (literally I just ran around exploring during the time that I've played this far) I felt like writing a review of this game. To start, a friend recommend it to me based on my love of the classic Xbox game, Jet Set Radio. Let me say that this was nothing what I expected, it smashed my expectations to pieces. It has very basic character customization, semi easy controls, and a story that really doesn't make much sense at first. Usually, lack of these things turn me away from games but, I persevered and I'm glad I did. This game is simply amazing, I love open worlds that allow you to explore and do whatever, and after the initial tutorial, that's exactly what this game does, it hands you the reins and says "go crazy". Sure, at first it may feel like you don't have anything to do, you can look around for missions, or, do what I did and just run, jump, climb and explore the city. The races are fun, especially with friends, and help you learn more ways to get around Hover City. The controls are simple to learn but, pretty hard to master, but once you master them, the things you can do will make your jaw drop. You'll feel like you can fly all over the place, especially with all of the upgrades you find. Long story short, if your a fan of open world exploration, futuristic environments, and crazy parkour abilities, then I can not recommend this game more to you. Give it a try, and I promise you wont be disappointed!

One Thousand Lies is a rambling story with a cast of characters who have random adventures featuring a B-grade weirdo. First I have to say it i's hard to describe the general story of One Thousand Lies. With that in mind, it's basically a RomCom, except that there is nothing funny about it (although the characters can be a bit silly), and it's more creepy than romantic. Unfortunately, this is another Visual Novel struck down by the curse of a jerk protagonist and vapid female supporting characters, although OTL goes a long way to do something with that in the random story events. The story meanders and goes on random adventures and I guess that's nice but I wasn't interested much. There is a psychological twist to the story but it didn't work for me.
Ignore me, One Thousand Lies is a good visual novel, possibly even great if you like this sort of story.  It's free, go ahead and play One Thousand Lies if you want to read something light hearted.

Best free to play visual novel by far. Multiple points across the story all resurface at the ending to bring about a very impactful ending. The initial story may be a little bland and lacking as it was all set up for the end.

I honestly love OTL. I went into it not expecting much, since OELVNs (OSLVN for this one in particular) are usually pretty hit or miss. This is definitely my favorite non-Japanese visual novel that I've read. The characters are great, and I loved reading the banter between everyone. Even though not a lot was "happening", I still found myself enjoying the story and dialogue between the characters.

I really liked the original magicka. But the changes in magicka 2 are not for me.
I find the new movement system interesting. Being able to cast spells on the move makes you more mobile as a wizard. The problem is that the ranges of cone and AOE spells are decreased. Also the damage of al spells is decreased. As a result you feel weak in comparison to the first Magicka.
I also do not like the new spell formula. I can understand why some people would like to cast spells with fewer amount of button clicks. I rely liked the old way. The most powerful spells demanded up to 10 clicks. With the new system you can’t cast spell with more than 5 basic elements. Fire and water do not become steam in one slot. It is the same with water and ice.
A minor problem for me is that the game seems to have been made with consoles in mind. The new spell casting system would fit controllers better than mouse and keyboard.
I really wanted to like this game. But sadly it was not to my liking. If anyone want more magicka, buy the DLC to the first game.

Much simpler maps, which all look about the same, unlike Magicka 1's INTERESTING and diverse maps and bosses (this game has no actual bosses except the end boss).
The magic mechanics are simplified in this game; no combining elements within the casting bar such as steam being a single icon.
It's like they saw how uninterested the community was in Wizard Wars and decided to scrap together some maps and call it Magicka 2.
I also got kicked from singleplayer for my internet connection going out. Do not buy.

As a fan of Visual Novels, I was pretty excited to hear about this short (not to mention free) game. A friend of mine also recommended it with a lot of good things to vouch for.
The first thing I noticed was the art style. It's fairly cute, and while there aren't many poses/expressions for each character, they ARE at least drawn well.
The soundtrack for the game is cute as well, but it's insanely repetitive. There were 2 or 3 songs that I enjoyed but after hearing them over and over, you just get sick of them.
As far as the story goes, I have to say I was extremely disappointed. It was unfortunate because the beginning sets you up with a lot of vague phrases and stories that draw you in, and the entire rest of the game is practically unrelated. It's not until the very end (like the last 10 minutes of the game) that they decide to connect everything and you're able to make sense of the plot. The characters also did not feel very relateable to me. While I did enjoy them and their characteristics, I still found them strange and had trouble understanding some of their reasons and motives so acting certain ways or saying certain things. All in all I had high hopes for this game but was ultimately disappointed. My experience will not be the same as others, but if you have less patience and enjoy relateable characters/story, then I would skip out on this one.

Don't get me wrong, I love the characters and their personality in their own way but the story was perplexing. More so, I don't really recommend this because of course, no options to choose your path and another is that the story was just a bit too jumbled. I know the ambiguity was what this game was aiming for but the plot of the story didn't really have consistency other than lies being the main point and wrapping everything up. The other thing was that it felt like there were fillers inside the story where it had nothing to do with the story. I get that it might've been used for seeing their lives but it just felt like forever before we could progress on with the story.  As for the side story that Ciar wrote; I think it would've been better to put those at the end of the chapters instead of midway of each chapter. Just my opinion, you can hate on it if you want but I just felt like a visual novel like this had so much more potential.

is the first VN written by Spanish independent developer named Keinart Lobre. The story has written in Spanish and translated to English.
This VN tells the tale of Ciarán Endyein, a liar writing the fable of a wolf longing to reach the sun. One day, Ciarán starts receiving enigmatic emails from a mysterious sender, turning his everyday life into a mess of a romantic comedy with psychological themes mixed in. What lies beyond the mystery he's been presented with? In the words of Harry H.: "If you want to know the truth, go find it".
Let's go to the good points. The art is good. The characters personalities were well-made and lively; they were attractive (both physically and spiritually), and realistic. The soundtrack seems decent, with a good variety and didn't get repetitive. As for writing, it's eloquent and well-made, with almost no grammatical errors. However, the translation of Spanish to English isn't 100% faithful, the own creator says that, but I'm sure he did the best within the possible.
Then comes the main part of a visual novel, the dialogue. Repetitive, boring, agonizing. Overall, this game it's just a novel, it bored me and made me angry. They're all talking about the same things, time after time, one character after another. The story is very, very long and very annoying. I appreciate Keinart's effort, seriously, but for me, definitely not.
This game has only one achievement: 'Only the truth'. This achievement can be obtained by completing the whole story, which has not any choices you have to make, and then click on a 'hidden' text which finishes the story. So to start click on the yellow tab with a plus sign on it to start. It's quite a long story and if you don't like reading it all I recommend using a macro to go through the story really fast. Once you finished the story go back to the main menu and click on the text which says: 'One hidden truth'. Easy game for an achievement hunter.

Pain gives this game an eh/10. All the technical aspects of the game have worked fine for me with the exception of alt+tab crashing it. the story line is also nice, it made me laugh a few times, but it wasnt bad. But game play wise, it just doesn't feel as fun as it should be. Spell casting should be the most fun part of this game, but tbh it feels clunky, dumbed down and the spells themselves dont feel like they have much weight behind them, specifically charge spells and the earth element.  Most of the time while actually using the earth element i found myself not being sure if the charge was done before i got fire it. Which brings me to another point, charge times for spells are ridiculously long. This also goes for the AOE spells, as even fully powered up the area they affect doesn't grow, it just stays the same and does a little bit more damage than a smaller spell would have. The only magick that has a decent AOE range is lightning, but thats just because it jumps from target to target. Ice and water combo spells also felt pretty useless for most of the game, as when you freeze an enemy, you cant damage them, making it feel like a waste of time to use. On a more positive note, healing is REALLY useful now, as you can move and heal yourself at the same time.  And a personal gripe, the lightning beam and the push from the first game are gone and it makes me sad. Also with the charge push element being gone and being made into a spell, getting large groups of enemys away from you is MUCH harder, if not near impossible without the use of water aoe, as the knockdown from the earth element aoe isnt as strong as it once was, and is pretty much useless. Also the Artifacts are a bit of a letdown. They dont really change much about the game aside from making it harder or changing how the faeries work.
TL;DR: FEELS LIKE THEY TRIED TO MAKE A DIABLO STYLE GAME FROM A MOBA AND DIDNT TAKE INTO ACCOUNT THE DIFFERENCES

For those of us in the Linux userland, there isn't much choice when it comes to Flight sims, so XPlane10 was pretty much the only choice out there. But even when pitted against others sim, the realism of XPlane really shines. I am a hardcore simmer, with 3-monitor 5760x1080 resolution on GTX 1080, 32GB of RAM and Core i7-6700k. I get about 30-90 FPS depending where I am at, it is definitely a resource hog and can use some improvements.
Flight model is quite realistic and it forces you to rethink your controls (think right rudder). However, some flight forces are exegerrated and can lead to uncomfortable rights. I still get right-tendencies even in level flight. There are problems with ground shaking and abrupt FPS changes, but hopefully thoes will be fixed with XPlane11.
Most importantly, I got all my hardware (All the saitek radio panel, multi-panel, rudder, yoke..etc) working without any issues. Even TrackIR works great with XPlane on Linux. It is highly recommended for any serious simmer out there.

An amazing piece of art. Firewatch is an amazing and artistic game full of wonders. It's amazing in terms of art style and even though I have to run the game on low quality due to my potato computer, it's still beautiful either way. One thing I liked about the game was the elements of the game. The realistic deal of Henry being a distressed man trying to deal with the fact his wife has dementia, needing to get away and take a break, the element of suspense that kicks up later in the game with this strange events occurring here and there, and obviously the art. They just all fit together well and this game did a good job of representing that. Another thing I liked about this game is how realistic Henry and Delilah's personalities are; they sound like typical humans. Cursing, and cracking jokes, they don't have the same "perfect" video game personalities, but rather unique and realistic ones. Aside from that though this game is very relaxing and a good pass time if you have nothing else to play or want to take your mind off of stress. While this game does have its cons and definitely isn't the "AMAZING! BEST GAME EVER" type of game, I urge anyone with the time and money to give this game a try!

Now to my suggestion... Should you buy it or not?
Well let me answer that with another question, do you have the original game or not?
If you do not have this game already, get it. Get it now and don't think about any other game. This game is absolutely amazing, and in this pack, you get all of the DLC's. I love Jet Set Radio/Future, but this game simply is not finished. It has so many little flaws that keep it from being great. And trust me, the greatness is there, it's just covered by a terrible user interface that reminds me of Everquest Online mixed with System Shock 2.
The font choices, colors, menus, controller optimization etc. are VERY rough. The game just doesn't have any soul to it.
Jet Set Radio starts and it's like BAM, you're a member of this youth gang that wants to stop corrupt police and politicians, you immediately feel a connection to these characters.
But in Hover, you're... a human covered in winter attire and everyone that talks to you is so overly enthusiastic and looks like they're about to drop acid and go to a rave. There are typos in the dialogue and, I'm not kidding, a male character actually used the emote "^^" to signal that he's happy.
The characters don't have any background or development, they're just overly excitable faceless cyberpunk people that you can tell the devs wrote while thinking "Let's make them super nice, that will make new players feel welcome!!!"
All the reviews are saying "I dislike X, Y, and Z, but the game overall is really good/promising!" But I'll just tell you right now that, while the game has definite potential and the style is cool in a "newbie's first 3D game" kind of way, this isn't worth 20 dollars. The soundtrack is generic even with Hideki Naganuma's involvement. A lot of songs sound kind of ambient and quiet repetitive with some dance/techno influences. Considering that JSR's main draw was both the fun gameplay and the great music, and this game has neither, I would call this game a failed spiritual successor.
I get it: a lot of the hype for this game is for people itching to have a new Jet Set Radio game and they'll take whatever they can get. If this game gets improved and maybe has a more functional single player experience, I'll change my review. But for the time being, I'm seeing people who enjoy the *FRAMEWORK* of the game and the promise it has if the devs choose to patch it and keep expanding it, but that's different from what's here: an unpolished game being sold for 20 bucks, which granted, is fairly reasonable.
Many reviews for this game want it to be good to validate your belief that there's still a market for this kind of game, and trust me, there most definitely IS a market for new Jet Set Radio games. This just isn't it.
Not yet, anyway.

Hover: Revolt Of Gamers is a fast paced, first/third person, open world parkour game, reminiscent of Jet Set Radio's colourful art style and music with Mirror's Edge as the parkour aspect. (To be honest, when I learned that it was a Kickstarter project, I didn't believe it at the time). It is set in the city ECP-17 where the mayor, who looks like he's got bean cans glued to his shoulders, outlawed entertainment. Maybe because he has to run a city while all the noncorporeal clones just stand around, maybe having parties, so if he has no fun, then noone has fun. I GUESS, anyway. Also, I think that's how the devs got out of making a bunch of different NPC models, just say they are clones. But how come the mayor outlaws happiness, but not the act that pretty much defies the laws of nature? Oh yeah, he's a clone, too. Your character is apart of, well, WILL be apart of a resistance movement to end the reign of The Great Admin. I'd say apart of, but you start off as a clone in a lab where your two best buds hold your hand for the tutorial. After that, you are free to do whatever you want, as long as what you want is in the first city, 'cos if you want to go somewhere else, you have to go do the story.
Turns out that the resistance is called the Gamers, and their HQ is located in the sewers, at the very top, which seems redundant cos' they have a DJ playing music pretty much forever. It's suprising how they haven't been caught yet.
Speaking of music, the soundtrack is quite good, it has two songs by Hideki Naganuma, who also worked on Jet Set's soundtrack. The music that plays is determined by where you are on the map(s). If you are in the sewers, Underground plays. If you are in the HQ or in a club/bar, Naganuma's pieces play.
In most of the maps, the main characters are strewn about the place, either delivering quips or tips when you talk to them or handing out missions, but when you get to the HQ, all of them are there doing something. The grammar in some of the text is a tad bad, and on some occasions, weird. I am one to forgive studios who's main language isn't English, as long it is fixed in a later update. But plot holes are everywhere in the game. If the sewers are supposed to be secure so noone could get into it without a keycard which unlocks a holo-door when you tackle it, then how does the rivaling resistance get in so easily and start stealing stuff? Or why does the other resistance hate the Gamers when they share similar ideals and both want to stop The Great Admin? Why does the guy who dislikes cloning when A: He is a clone himself, and B: He pretty much made a clone (the player) at the labs? Well, at least the gameplay good, some missions are near to impossible without other players or exploiting the AIs of the NPCs, but fun nevertheless. Run, jump, bounce, grind, do backflips, jump for a ledge and just barely miss it. But that's alright, because there is an interesting mechanic where you can press a button to "rewind" your movements. There is another thing I would point out very specifically, but I'd like to let people find it themselves. There are references to shows, notably cartoons, and they are fairly easy to recognize. Going back to you! The clone. You can customize your character on the basis of colours. Though, I don't see many people being creative since they just pick black clothing and white energy. For some of the palettes, there are more colours, but the game is a little bad at telling us about them. Also, before I forget, they have a detection system for pirates, it's just they don't use it to it's potential. As in, they can detect a pirate, but pirates can play online.
"But we solved the pirate issue! We made the pirates name in the user's player list RED!"
"Anything else besides that?"
"We put a sarcastic quip next to their name, emphasizing the fact that they are pirates."
When I saw the change log, I did have a chuckle when I saw that they put (yaaaaarrrr) next to the "feature."
You can name your character, but they changed it so when your name shows up in the player list, it shows your Steam name instead of your character name, still not using their features as well as intended. The character name only shows up  when someone joins a mission, and nowhere else.
You can upgrade your character with chips (as in microchips) to make your character better at jumping, running, etc. The game is also bad at telling you that in certain spots, you can put chips adjacent to each other to increase it's strength. It makes sense that having more of one chip would decrease in it's effectiveness to avoid the overpowered setup, it does not make sense when you remove a chip, the chip behind it (that was sealed by the chip that was moved) is still locked.
TL;DR
A fast paced parkour game that's missing polish in some areas, but not in the gameplay.

The short version- If you liked Jet Set Radio, buy this game, like, now.
Slightly longer version- Hover: Revolt of Gamers takes the formula everyone loved from Jet Set and spices it up a bit. You got the graffiti, you got the cartooney graphics, you got the evil anti-fun government, and most importantly, it's funky as hell. Biggest difference is instead of roller blades, you're free running, and have a host of new movement options and the extra mobility they bring. Also adds a level system with tokens similar to League of Legend's rune system, allowing you to make each of the five characters you can switch between at any time play exactly as you want them to.
Pros-
Biggest pro for me is the movement. Some of the most fun I've had with movement since Super Mario Sunshine. Although a bit slow at the start, it picks up quite quickly and once your character is all geared up you're regularly hitting lines that make you feel like a total badass. This is one area that I feel is done way better than Jet Set Radio Future, and that's pretty impressive in my book.
The character/gear system- you can have up to 5 characters on your team. You only start with the generic basic dude/dudette, but unlock different characters with unique bonuses and negatives. Each character can be leveled up 10 times, unlocking slots you put runes in to boost different stats. This allows you to have characters that specialize in different things so you never get stuck on a challenge your normal playstyle isn't tuned to.
Mu'frickin Gameball- I'll be honest, I hated this game type at first, mainly due to playing with computer AI teammates, but it really grew on me. It's basically 3 dimensional parkour basketball. Once you get the controls down it's pretty great. You wanna alley-oop to yourself, launch into the air, ride the wall around, and dunk on all your friends? Cuz you can and it's freakin' awesome.
Always some cons so here we go-
The Menus- The menus are not very controller friendly. If you're using a controller expect to be reaching for your mouse to do most menuing (and there's a decent amount you have to do, what with the rune system). Really frustrating getting sent to the slammer because you couldn't restart the mission fast enough.
Lack of explanations- Outside of a very, very basic tutorial, the game doesn't do super well explaining mechanics. Most of them are intuitive enough it isn't a huge problem, but it's a bit annoying how often you find yourself thinking "well♥♥♥♥♥♥I wish I knew that worked earlier"
If you fall behind on keeping all your characters leveled up and do too many quests, catching up your less  played characters can be a pain as all the good XP bonuses are used up already.
Lastly, the soundtrack isn't super diverse. Each area has it's general song, and then there's a handful depending on the type of mission you're doing. I don't mark this up as a big downside though, as all the songs are catchy enough that I didn't get tired of them. Your mileage may vary.
In summary, if you liked Jet Set Grind, Radio, and Future, you'll like this game. If you like bustin sick moves and spraypainting away an oppressive government because video game logic, you'll like this game. Full disclosure, I'm a bit of a Jet Set fanboy, but I cannot recommend this game enough. 10/10.

The best way to describe SquareLogic is... it is the game of which Sudoku could be one small mode.
Like Sudoku, it has a rule that a number shows up once in each row and once in each column.  But beyond that:
- Sudoku always subdivides the board into 9 equal squares.  SquareLogic subdivides the board in all sorts of crazy ways.  (And sometimes it doesn't even tell you where all the boundaries are.)
- In Sudoku, each subdivision contains one of each number.  In SquareLogic, a subdivision has some rule about its contents, but there are many possible rules.  The contents may add to some total, or all be odd numbers, or have some ordering...
This sounds brain-exploding, but a nifty thing about SquareLogic is that it provides in-game tools for figuring out the possibilities.  (You can disable these if you are super-hardcore.)  It also introduces the gameplay very gradually.  Just a well-done number puzzle game all around!

SquareLogic is like Kakuro on crack.  Kakuro is like Sudoku on crack.  So Kakuro is like Sudoku on meth.  If you like this sort of puzzle, there are tens of thousands of them included, so you'll never run out.  I fire it up every once in a while to work through a single puzzle to get my brain working.  It starts easy, but it ramps up.

This is the Nicolas Cage of puzzle games, because it:
a) entertains in even the smallest doses
b) makes you think in ways you never expected to
c) is a vampire
d) can become surprisingly addictive
e) takes the familiar (sudoku rules) and adds a clever twist
f) stole my drugs and made me watch as it ♥♥♥♥ed my girlfriend.
So basically it's well worth picking up, although god help you if you introduce a parent to the thing.

Lemme start off with the fact that I'm a fan of SAO, so this review is obviously going to have some bias parts to it. Come at me SAO haters. This is also my first review on this game, to let everyone know how amazing it is.
Review:
Fanservice: 10/10 Rain is best waifu, jus the kind of fan service you'd expect from SAO. And p.s don't lewd the loli
Gameplay: 8/10 Playing with a keyboard and mouse is inconvienient but it works. Combat is fast and enjoyable
Graphics: 7/10 Nothing outstanding, nice detail to character models, cutscenes are pretty and weapon + armor design are super cool (especially the legendary gear)
Customization: 9/10 Lots of different avatar options, even more battle options with the 9 different weapons and all their unique skills, buffs, and passives.
Stroy: 7/10 Kinda slow and a bit boring and confusing. It has its climaxes and stuff. But that's SAO for ya
Multiplayer: 6/10 No one really plays the multiplayer (I couldn't find any parties)
Content: 9/10 There is lots to do, especially after the main story. Lots of grinding and rewards.
Music: 8/10 A memorable soundtrack. I really enjoy how the track "Swordland" was altered to fit the mood
World: 7/10 It's large and seperated into a lot of sections, each with a mini boss. It takes longer than I want it to just to run to the next area
Difficulty: 5/10 After around lv20 you can start taking on monsters well over 30 levels above you and still beat them easy (until you finish the main story and start the DLC, that's a bit of a different story)
Pros:
- Fanservice
- A good SAO game on PC and doesn't run like♥♥♥♥♥br>- Cool animated cutscenes, makes you wish there was more of them because they're so beautiful
- Comes with all the DLC so that makes the life of this game much longer
- Great combat system, fast paced and not really button mashing, ultimate skills really feel like ultimate skills
- Multiplayer system where you can d-d-d-d-d-d-d-d-duel other players and participate in raids
- Lots of customization options, including the avatar, skill tree system, and party members including their class (you can make yourself look like any of the girls in Kirito's harem :D )
- Very satisfying when you pull off a long combo or kill a hard boss
- Tons of waifus to choose from, you can even take generic NPCs to dates
- You can remap the keys if you're playing with a keyboard making commands MUCH MUCH easier to manage
- Trading cards go for 50 cents, bro those are some expensive trading cards you can make a profit
Cons:
- You kinda have to watch the anime or read the manga AND  have some knowledge on the previous games (Hollow Fragment, Lost Song, etc)
- TONS of grinding if you want to be the very best. I spent the first 2h trying to get my level on par with the monsters in the area. DLC requries EVEN MORE grinding because of the sudden level spike
- If your level is on par with the monsters in the area you can almost always one shot them with a skill
- Board quests are nothing special at all. There are only two types of quests: Kill X amount of X type of monster, and collect X amount of a certain material. I'm serious, that is it
- Some fps issues here and there but it goes away after restarting the game
- Becomes a visual novel at some points. Some are good but some are just boring as hell
- Tutorial sucks at explaining romance system
- Story quests give you very vague locations on where you have to go and what you have to do, this especially comes true during the DLC
- Enigma orders are boring, feel impossible to complete, and requirements are just bs. It's a good thing it's not a requirement for the game to progress
- You can't just save the game out in the open world, you have to teleport then it auto saves (if there is a way to save anywhere please correct me)
- That one bug where you float in the air and can't move (to solve this just change equip.)
- Grinding after the main story so you can attempt the DLC
Verdict:
Combat and skill system remind me of Xenobalde X, fanservice is great, music is good, good graphics, ok story and lots of customization. It's worth $55 (CAD) because you get the base game + ALL the DLC (including all the costumes although movie costumes unlock after main story). It's addicting and fun, it's hard to put down once you know what you want to do, and there is always something to do whether it's continuing the story, doing character quests, or grinding. Also did I mention that there are tons of waifus?

Alright, so I'm keeping in mind that this thing is $15 and that it's meant for multiplayer. I prefer to write reviews based on a game's own merit, rather than comparing it to it's predecessors or other games.
Pros:
The game is fast paced and challenging in certain situations.
The elements in the game are relatively well balanced. There is oftentimes no catch-all spell that solves every problem.
The major boss fight is significantly difficult, but not punishing.
Magickas do not need to be memorized, although it is beneficial if you do so.
Lots of unlocks and 'artifacts' to diversify your game and lengthen play-time.
Everything is deadlier in it's base form, meaning that battles are quicker, and the game gets boring less quickly.
Boss battles to get awesome items. Good idea!
Cons
Universal Magick cooldown. Not a good idea. Players with quick fingers should be rewarded, not punished.
There aren't a lot of Magicks. More magicks would mean more diversity of spells in the game.
All summonable minions die in about 5 seconds. They're not worth summoning.
Some items make the Death element the catch-all spell for everything.
The most useful and complex spell is easily cast within 5 minutes of starting the game. It does not need to be discovered, and no experimentation is necessary. In other words, there's no learning curve.
The game feels 'dumb'. Everything is a cinch, and nothing is genuinely challenging until you get to the final boss.
Enemies have access to powers you can never hope to use.
The boss fight puzzle's solution is thrown at the player in big bold letters. It's easy to understand what needs to happen, but the Disruption spell has about a 2 second warmup phase, and by that time the beam to be blocked is empty. Easy solution, but difficult execution. I would rather there be multiple solutions.
The main story is far too short.
Elements don't combine. Steam and Ice are weaker than fire, cold, and water alone because they use less elements. Furthermore, why not other combinations? Fire+Earth= Lava, Life+Earth grows tanglevines, for examples. If you're not going to give us a lot of useful magicks, then increase the diversity of ordinary spells.
You have to re-do the 10 minute boss fight every time you die in the middle. It requires attempt after attempt after attempt after attempt just because you keep respawning at the beginning of the 4 stage fight.
Enemies summon insta-kill spells on top of player, no chance to save except through memorization of the fight.
Built for console. Really, this game was never meant to play on a console, and it shouldn't be dumbed down in order to be playable on a PS4.
Compared to the original title:
Faster pace
Runs better on most systems
Deadlier base forms of spells
No combining elements upon summoning
Fewer magicks
Click-and-hold healing makes for less spamming.
Fewer and less useful items and staves.
Easier bosses (except for the last one).
Honestly, the first game was a lot better. However, you get what you pay for, and this title is worth about $15. I reccomend this game for anyone looking for a cheap way to kill 3 hours, nothing more.

I will say this. This game is kind of based of the Wizard Wars engine wich isn't bad!
But.. pooh.. this game.. I am so mixed on it.
Do I recommend it.. sorta..
It's still a good sequal, but it falls in the tropes of being overshined then it's prequels.
So let me sum up the good and bad.
Good:
-Gameplay improved. Quick spells as well as manual cast is in the game. Element combining is nerfed but still great and the game feels overall more responsive. The fun thing to do is hit a death beam with a life beam to get a big boom.
- Visuals are improved.
-Humor is still there
-Good replayablity effort in the difficulty / custom difficulty settings
-Difficulty improved by mechanics. More control means harder enemies. Nothing wrong with that. You can't steam beam your way out of this game! Gotta be more creative!
The Bad:
-Game length. It felt shorter then the other one.
-The artifical difficulty. Though it is a hard game. They sometimes ramp it up too ludicrious levels by simply putting TOO MUCH ENEMIES into the screen. Especially of different variatiies.
-Game loves being wet. There are stage hazard but too many times are there puddles of water or rain or whatever to make you wet. This especially is annoying as enemies are immune to certain elements that combo with wet. While you are constantly wet! Wet immunity recommend or keep a water aura up.
-Bosses. Though Some bosses are well designed mechanic wise. Overall they fall flat over it's ancestor.
They don't feel epic enough from the last one or are just reskinned enemies.
Sometimes stages don't even give boss fights.
The worst offender is the final boss as it is gimmicky like hell and it's almost impossible to do!
It involves a mechanic you never could pratice + a mechanic that was flawed.
-Stage's
Stages weren't that interresting to me. The Final stage was a good idea. But other wise.. it felt a little blant.
Unconcluded:
-Story
The Story.. is.. well... nothing like the 1st game but interresting non the less.
I can say this with non spoiler ways.
"I have no idea how to feel of the ending of the game"
It is one of those types of stories. Tries to laugh, but.. I couldn't laugh.. something in this story made me feel differnet and think.
Overall:
I wouldn't rate this game but.. for a magicka expirence it only improves on a few aspects in favor of the others.
Bugs are glitches are sitll around some even from the 1st game.
But it's still a more polished game in it's mechanics.
For now.. I am still saying:
Buy the original!
This one needs some patching or some DLC to make it enjoyable.
As for the final boss..
It's ridiclously frustrating.. it's not even THAT HARD of a boss!
It's just draining you on frustration rather then trying to kill you.
