Below you'll find a written and video impression on the game
State of Decay was a fantastic open world zombie survival game when it was originally released on Xbox Live, but when it was ported to the PC it suffered from multiple problems. Bugs, and poor resolution were some of the most notable issues. Fortunately the core game was so good, many people including myself were willing to forgo any problems that it had, and enjoyed it any ways. What a great idea it is to "remaster" the original! The question though, is Year One remastered enough to justify a $30USD price tag?
If you've already played or own the original game is it worth $30? Short answer: NO.
Yes, the lighting have been improved significantly, and the texture quality is better, but other than that, there's not much new here. Sure, there are also some extra minor characters added, and now cars have decal (whoopie...), but every thing else about the game is exactly the same. The game advertises improved animations, and combat mechanics, yet I notice little changed about these 2 things. If there have been any changes, they're so tiny, it's barely noticeable. The two biggest improvements are the lighting and texture quality, both could of easily been added as a patch. There are no other notable additions, the model quality is exactly the same, there are no new modes to play, no new areas, no new quests, nothing for returning players.
If this was advertised as the definitive State of Decay collection, I would be fine with it. Lots of games like Boarderlands repackage old games into compilations for the benefit for new players, but this was advertised as a remastering. Even the description of the game mislead old fans to believe that there are a ton of new stuff here, when there aren't. Worst off, the most noticeable improvements, lighting, texture quality, and true 1080p, are things that should of been in place when they launched their original port! But instead they decided to charge it to us, as a lazy excuse of a remaster. If you're a returning player to the game, Year One is nothing more than a glorified update patch.
Luckily for us, the original is absolutely a stellar survival game, and since they changed nearly nothing about it, it remains a stellar survival game. If you are new to State of Decay, this might be a good time to get into the game, and perhaps Year One is suitable for the new comers. For old time fans who have already played, or own State of Decay, don't bother. It's not worth your money unless you have enough disposable income to justify it. But even then, the practice of selling what amounts to a patch for $30 and misleading old players to think that there are a ton of new stuff when there's not, is not a practice that I can condone.
Pros:
- Still the same, great State of Decay game
- Suitable for any one NEW to the game
Cons:
- For returning players, there isn't much new
- $30 for what amount to a patch is unconscionable
- Neither combat or animation have been improved enough to justify it being in the description
- The original was a lazy port, Year One is a lazy remastering

Rarely, I encounter a game so amazing and fun that I can't help but want to share it with my friends, for whom I buy copies.
I did this with Shovel Knight, easily the best platformer I've played to date.
I did this with Hyper Light Drifter.
I did it with Terraria.
And now? I will proudly do it with Hover.
Hover's one of those games that scratches an itch we all have as gamers: A craving for absolute freedom. Nowhere is that freedom more empowering and... COOL as it is in Hover: Revolt of Gamers. The Parkour system is absolutely the main draw and it's WONDERFUL.
You'll understand when you climb up to the top of the tallest building you can get to (and climb to the best of your ability), and look out over the huge, sprawling world that is Hover City, and realize: "This city, is mine. I can go anywhere. I can jump on this, grind on that, I can FLY."
... I mean, you can't literally fly. But you don't NEED TO. You can jump and climb and slide and run and bounce and grind and holy♥♥♥♥♥♥ man. The ground you can cover when you build up those skills. And I don't mean "level up abilities". There's that, too, but you won't get anywhere fast without actually learning to be good at parkour yourself! The AIR TIME you can get! I feel like I'm flying in a way that actual flying doesn't do as well. It's amazing!
Please. 20 bucks. If you have just a little over lunch money, get it. Please. Get it for friends who can't! Just get it!
Please for the love of god support this dev team.
EDIT: If I had to say this game had any flaws, it would probably just be the final two challenges of the story, which consist of a race, and then a GamerBall Game.
The race against the Great Admin goes through an obstacle course TEEMING with security that's REALLY annoying, because if you win you will still have to do the race over again if you get sent to jail during the dialogue (which they can and WILL do). And the final part just before the goal-line where you have to carefully jump between tall laser-fences can completely ruin your chances if you bump into just one, since they tend to pinball you around, making it impossible for you to escape, and forcing you to restart as you're inevitably captured by the police who sit there laughing at you while you bounce around.
The second challenge is a GamerBall game where YOUR goal is a mile up on the opposite side of a cylinder in the center of the room from where the ball spawns, and the Great Admin's are right on the ground a couple of yards away from where the ball drops down. One of those goals (He gets THREE), is right behind him after he grabs the ball and oftentimes nothing stops him from just turning around immediately after grabbing the ball and tossing it in.
These, however, I imagine are issues that will be cleaned up later on.
The only other flaw I can really think of with the game's design is the stats system.
For all of Hover I have only used and ever needed one character. And he is equally built for speed, grind, and jumping power, which makes him utterly dedicated to parkour. Some challenges have been difficult but I've been able to do absolutely everything with this character after just a few tries. There's really nothing he can't do. Which is sad because there are also Hacking and Strength stats that the game wants you to believe are important, but I ultimately wound up never requiring.
Hacking is only necessary when you come across a container that requires higher hacking capability than the base level (and these are rare, and also not necessary at all). Having trouble breaking holo propaganda? Turns out that hacking has nothing to do with it! You just have to plow through them while going really fast! Bounced off? You're not going fast enough! Mod up more speed!
Strength is the "gamerball" focused stat. It makes you more proficient at dealing with the ball. In GamerBall, you get a speed debuff while holding the ball. Strength mods will mitigate that debuff so you can move more easily while holding it. Strength mods will also let you throw the ball farther so you can potentially score goals from further away. And they also increase your resistance to being bumped by another player, and increase the force of your own bumps against enemy players.
... but if you have really high parkour skills like speed and grind, you can just grab the ball and keep it away from the enemy while you outrun everyone toward the goal. The GamerBall debuff really doesn't do enough to keep you down if your speed is high enough.
If the devs explored better ways to incentivize the use of these stats there might be better reason to have extra characters on your "team". As it stands, though, you can do everything as the one-man Parkour Master.
... which is appropriate, in a game about Parkour...

At first this was a pretty decent point and click noir detective game. While some of the puzzles were annoying and/or pedantic, the art design and story was just about good enough to make up for it. Then the plot went down the rabbit hole and things got... weird. I'm keen to play any potential sequel, but less supernatural voodoo and more gritty New York would be nice.

gets a lukewarm recommendation from me.  The story's not bad - a little bland at first, but it keeps getting more interesting and twisty as it progresses, making it worth finishing.  If a noir point-and-click casting you as a PI in the 1930's sounds like it'd be up your alley, go ahead, but be prepared for the flaws mentioned below.  I should note, though, that it ends with a lot of plot threads left dangling in anticipation of a sequel.
Voice acting's mostly decent, but some characters seem flat while others have exaggerated accents, and there are occasionally times when a character's voice noticeably changes from one sentence to the next (indicating that the dialog was probably pieced together from multiple recording sessions with inconsistent quality).  Despite having no support for widescreen, the graphics are overall excellent and work well to set the mood.  The quality of the graphics, does, however, make the terrible facial animation that much more obvious.
Compared to many other point-and-clicks, the puzzle solutions are logical and realistic, which works well with the story.  But that doesn't mean it compares well in terms of making the solutions fair and reasonable - in fact, it does just the opposite.  Some of the hotspots are tiny and barely visible, but that's a minor problem since F1 will highlight them.  A bigger problem is that at least a couple solutions depend on knowledge that the player cannot reasonably be expected to possess.  For example, you'll need to know what a certain country's flag looks like, which would be fine if said flag were clearly depicted in-game, but it isn't.  Worse, the game expects you to do things in a certain order that isn't always clear.  If you've missed inspecting the object that you need to inspect in order to open up the dialog option that you need to take before solving the next puzzle, you'll be stuck and you won't know why you're stuck until you've looked up a guide.  It may make sense, but only in retrospect.

I love me some detective games, and this one is... well, worth buying for very, very, very cheap on a Steam sale.
If you're as big a fan of detective games as I am, then maybe I added an extra "very" or two, just now.
CONS:
1) Voice acting: The voice acting is really bad. Sometimes the quality is, well... ugh. Enough said.
2) Animation: The animation is sub-par, today. I mostly speak of the mouth movements. Everything else is quite par.
3) Lockpicking: You can skip doing it altogether.
4) Issues: Now, this is an interesting con. I would have broken this one down into more than one part, but, the single word "issues" really sums it all up neatly. For instance, near the beginning of the game, it seemed quite impossible to be able to find a light switch in a blackened room, which prompted me to get frustrated and stop playing for months. And then, when I finally mustered up the jimmies (yes) to play it again, and use a walkthrough to figure out where the hell it was, I still couldn't find it with my cursor for quite some time.
Another instance was when trying to get around some NPCs to investigate; finnicky business, that, at times, but not awful. Just.... finnicky. You really have to play the game to know what I mean by  just saying "Issues". It's definitely not (it can't be) a big-budget game, by any means, though it does have it charms, and humour enough to keep me interested.
PROS:
1) Humour: The game has a good sense of humour, of which I won't spoil, because there's some fun quirkiness that you need to play into to appreciate.
2) Interactivity: The game is very interactive, for a point and click, and doesn't hold your hand too much with what you're doing. Though, as I said, Lockpicking was just... yes.
3) Story: The narrative is actually kind of interesting, once you... well, wrap your mind around it. Don't take this the wrong way; it's not complicated. It's just... a series of things happening, to the point of me not really remembering what sparked the narrative in the first place. But to be fair, I got frustrated and put this on hold for a few months. Maybe you would fare better..? All I remember is that I'm now framed for something I have to prove I didn't do, at this point. That's all I'll say, detail wise. That small tinge of con aside, it's amusing and not too shabby at keeping you engaged, so I take this as a positive thing.
4) Puzzles: The puzzle solving and clue finding is just what it should be; involved. You really need to think hard, search around, and try every angle you can to get the solutions your looking for. Some are easier than others, but none are 100% obvious.
FINAL THOUGHTS:
If you like detective games, point and click, and something that feels a little rough around the edges, this is the game for you. As long as you don't mind the awkward and sometimes questionable quality of the voice acting...
If you are looking for something to keep you on your toes, immersed, and delving into the shady underbelly of society, well... not so much.
Do I recommend?
Sure, why not.
But only if it's very, very, very cheap.

I'm normally not one to write a recommendation for a particular game in my library; my tastes are quite diverse and everyone else's tastes are different. However, Square Logic is a unique game with a unique place in my gaming heart. It is a puzzle game in its purest form: no animated characters, no falling objects, no globs of goo, no skeletons in the closet, and no laws of physics... but most definitely rules of math.  If you don't know how to add, subtract, multiply or divide, you will have trouble with this game. (If you can't count to 9, you'll have even more trouble, but for that you can watch Sesame Street.) Square Logic is a perfect game to give your brain a daily dose of exercise, a mental twice-around-the-block if you will. Some people will argue such a workout will help you think better in all aspects of your life. To me, it's just fun.
The game forum will provide more feedback from those who have already joined the Square Logic addiction. See you in the Beyond!

To start: I used to add a longer header to these reviews, but since it far too often (read as: more than once) made the review too long to submit, I've opted to leave it on my Backloggery page.
Gameplay: Star Wars: Republic Commando is a game that I had been meaning to play for quite a while now; ever since about 2007, in fact. I just never got around to buying it, though. Once I saw it go on sale through Steam, I figured now would be the time to get my hands on it. Did it live up to my expectations? Eh... kinda sorta. This game is pretty much a run of the mill squad-based tactical shooter with a little bit of actual tactics here and there. You do have to do some ordering of your own, as your squadmates are a little bit... dumb. I'm talking crouching right in front of a Super Battle Droid dumb (and man oh man do they love doing that). Now, when you die you do have a chance to be revived by your teammates, provided they don't end up doing what I mentioned in the previous sentence. Likewise, you can revive your teammates that have fallen, and they most definitely will fall throughout this game. Quite a lot.
Regarding the difficulty curve, there is one. It's too bad that this curve is a sine curve, though. In fact, the hardest enemy in the game is met in the first hour or so of gameplay; the Geonosian Elite. This guy will ruin your day, especially when they show up en masse later on. Why, you may ask? 'cuz he's got a death laser for an arm, which coupled with the sometimes turkey-in-the-rain level of intelligence of your AI, can often mean that your entire squad gets taken out by one enemy. I'd say that about 30% of my deaths in this game were due to Geonosian Elites, another 40% due to squadmate incompetence, and the last 30% due to my own incompetence. That does seem like quite the number for deaths on my hand, but hey, I never claimed to be a tactician.
As for the other enemies in the game, it's pretty standard fare. You've got Geonosians, Trandoshians, Droids, and that's for the most part your lot. Weapon variety isn't the greatest, but it's functional enough. You've got a pistol, assault rifle, sniper rifle, a grenade launcher, and one variety of "other weapon," which can be a shotgun, SMG, another rocket launcher, etc. Ammo can be pretty darn scarce, so if you have the opportunity to faceplant into enemies and end them with your  Knife of +9 Life Ending, that's a good idea. Yes, circle strafing around an SBD is a valid strategy. Yes, I've used it quite a bit. Yes, it's gotten me killed quite a bit as well. But hey, the knife is a very viable weapon, so I like to use it. There are, disappointingly, no boss fights in the game. I guess this is around the time when game designers thought bosses were SOOOO 90's or something i dunno.
Overall, though, I had a pretty good time with this game. It sure as hell ain't worth the 8.7 Gamespot gave it, considering Shadow Hearts: Covenant got an 8.7 and is one of my favorite RPGs of all time, but it's a pretty nice game nonetheless. I could see this being loads of fun with friends (especially since your friends will almost undoubtedly be smarter than the AI), but even with the singleplayer experience, I had a good enough time. 7/10.
Story: The actual story is pretty lackluster, I must admit. I'm not too huge of a Star Wars nerd, so there may be some parts of the Star Wars canon that this game apparently fills, but from what I could tell, it was either a fanservice-y plot or just a plot about four dudes going into places and shooting things. The game does try to add a bit of personality with squad banter, but it ends up being more groanworthy than anything else. Good effort, though. It also tries to be dramatic at the end, but I didn't find myself really caring all that much about what happened. 6/10.
Graphics: It's always tough talking about games from the past as far as their graphical capabilities go. Considering that this game came out in the early parts of 2005, I've gotta say; this game doesn't look half bad. Certainly pretty good for the time. Also, some of the visual effects such as when you go into low light mode look really cool. Some of the textures can be pretty ugly at times, but overall I'd say that the game is holding up, even if it's just barely doing so. It's not 90's shooter ugly yet, so there's that. As for the graphical capabilities of this game, they're honestly kinda disappointing. The game defaults to 4:3 resolutions, but since the game runs on the Unreal Engine, you can do a simple .ini tweak to make it run in fullscreen wide resolutions. I never did that, since I thought the game may not look the greatest, but after looking a bit on PCGamingWiki (a fantastic site), you can apparently change things like FOV to make the game look like it should. I didn't care enough to do that, so I just opted to run the game windowed at 1280x960. The game ran well, as one would expect, not really needing much of any resources from me. Overall, the game does look pretty nice, even though the game only runs at 4:3 resolutions without .ini tweaks. 3/5.
Sound: Well, they sure weren't subtle with the soundtrack. In fact, it gets kinda silly with how bombastic it gets at times. Apparently a lot of it is reused John Williams work, which is rather disappointing, I must say. I'd expect LucasArts to actually do a complete original score for this game. As for the voice acting... well, it's not bad. Nothing that'll knock your socks off, but it works well enough. Honestly, the game is kinda disappointing on the audio front. It either feels like a copy and paste effort or just a "not bad" effort. 2/5.
Overall scores are: 7/6/3/2; cumulative score of 6.0/10. Pretty much an above average game that doesn't reach too far beyond that mark.

Unfortunately, Magicka 2 feels like it LOST content compared to the original Magicka. For instance, you can no longer mix certain elements like steam and lightning. Physics on rocks are weird. Spells in general lack the punch they once had. The shield element is pretty useless, at least by itself (enemies can pass through them now and it doesn't last nearly long enough.) Melee attacks are super clumsy and sometimes don't even connect when they should. Even the act of just moving your wizard feels strange and clumsy.
And to top things off, they didn't add anything new, aside from artifacts and spell hotkeys (both admittedly good things). Magicka actually has more to it than Magicka 2. It's my feeling that cutting content without adding anything should preclude the right to put a "2" on a game. It feels like they tried to fix what wasn't broken,.. and broke it.
So I'm not being entirely negative, it would still be an ok game if the original hadn't existed. And there's still the same charming wackiness. The problem rests entirely in the actual mechanics.

I think Magicka 2 should have been released as early access game, with large amounts of openmindedness and willingness to listen from the developer's side. So first off, I'm not kibitzing about the YOSE - I have both the original and the remastered as it's kind of like the GoTY edition - those aren't given out to original purchasers either so I personally don't see the issue. I've played the hell out of this game and I love it even with its flaws.
The game looks nice. Maybe not 2015 Assassin's Creed, Witcher 3, Dragon Age Inquisition, etc. nice but it's not terrible. The effects are overall better and I enjoy the new look a lot. Unfortunately the textures break a lot and flatten out to look very low-res.
Cars handle better. Now that being said, they still handle really wonky at times. Car drives beautifully for a while and then you hit a small pebble or stick and car shoots into the air, slingshotting my character into a swan dive. Sometimes it does this for no reason at all. Textures on the cars break when my character is in them. Going from decent to low-res the second my character climbs in and sits down. There is no reason why a car sitting still should develop a case of the blurries. I do like the new vehicles UL added, they give the game a bit more variety and flavor.
Some pathing has improved. Some hasn't. I still get stuck on curbs and sandboxes and anything that is ankle height. I think my characters must all have weak ankles and thus have developed a fear of short objects.
Game difficulty seems cranked to 11. I started over instead of importing my save and opened up Breakdown lvl 1 (I prefer Breakdown to story TBH) and I was getting swarmed constantly. I lost one guy to a feral which is totally something that happens but a lot of survivors are getting mauled by packs of two and three zombies who glitch through doors and seem to hit like they migrated from a much higher difficulty. And OMG HORDES. Upon starting my game and moving into the Alamo, 6 hordes spawned. And each time there is a horde announcement, there are between 7 and 8 hordes. Half of these will almost instantly infest a house. It's kind of daffy.
Overall, I still love this game. It can go from mindlessly searching furniture to terrifying disaster in an instant and over-extending myself or being too reckless or even just getting unlucky can be the end of a survivor. While some people might not enjoy that, it is one of the defining features of SoD and it's done very well.

This is another one of those games I wish there was an "eh" option for. If you love JSRF  like I do and are really thirsty for a hopeful HD port, then I'd say Hover will probably scratch the itch. It's really fun to just move around in Hover with plenty of collectables to find and missions to complete. From what I can tell Hideki Naganuma only produced 2 songs for the game, but the rest of the soundtrack does well to call back to his style while also carrying it's own aesthetic. However the game is kinda easy to get lost and turned around in and really falls off on the later half, specifically the prison area and final area. There's also some bits and pieces here and there that make the game feel just a little unpolished, mostly text typos or missing scannable text but nothing too major.
The co-op is nice, but as someone who prefers to play solo the AI is kinda weak overall and is really terrible in the gameball missions. Most of the time I needed to grab the ball as soon as I could to prevent my teammates from taking it then flinging it wherever they want, usually away from the goal. In JSRF throwing the ball near a teammate would automatically pass it straight to you. Unless there was an obstacle in the way or an opponent to take it, it would home in onto you. In Hover however, throw means throw and usually amounts to the AI throwing the ball into a wall or passing it to the opposing team. This combined with a few design choices that I don't agree with makes for a really frustrating final level that left me wishing the ball mechanics were more akin to JSRF's or fixed in some way.
Unless you really like JSR or JSRF like I do, then I'd say to wait for a sale.

11/10 soundtrack ( when scuttle town was under construction why did the music change D: ) Dialogue in this game is actually hilarious at times and the pace of the game is fairly consistent. The gameplay was surprisingly more interactive then in riskys revenge. Going from transformations to pirate weapons in my opinion made the game feel more enjoyable. With transformations you have to sit there and wait to transform into a very specific creature to do a very specific job, and then u revert back to ur human form when the deed is done. With the pirate weapons you can do more then just hang on walls or swim in the sea. You have ur boots to speedrun through the level. Pistol for long range attacks. Hat for gliding across areas or avoiding grounded enemies. (Scimitar wasn't too interactive imo since I only used it to break blocks and that's it.) The difference between pirate weapons and transformations is that you are always using pirate weapons on the fly all the time, where as transformations were just there to get past a certain obstacle and that's it. You could even combo ur weapons like speeding up with the boots and using that momentum to fly across the level with ur hat while keeping ur self in the air by boosting urself with the cannon. With all this in mind it made the gameplay very creative and fun to mess around with.
There r times when the game makes huge jumps in difficulty without warning. For example, Tan Line Island was meh in difficulty only being the third island but the one right after is insane compared to Tan Line.
Overall I gave the game a 8.5/10 and would recommend this game to anyone looking to play a metroidvania style game.

Let me get to the skinny. I really, REALLY wanted to like Face Noir. A noir detective story wrapped around a point and click adventure? Yes please! But that said this game didn't work for me. The story was decent, the graphics were more than serviceable and level design was nice. But the game was, quite frankly, pretty boring. An excellent adventure game like Still Life pulls you in but Face Noir just didn't work for me. The puzzles were bland, voice acting was hit or miss and it just brought nothing new to the table. I think what I disliked most was the gameplay was so rigid. You HAD to do everything in a certain order or you were not going to proceed. I had to consult a walkthrough a couple times because I got frustrated by that. One last thing that ticked me off. The game ends up being set up for a sequel.  Welp. We'll see if that ever happens. I'd recommend Face Noir if you're really into old school style adventure games but be ready to have a walkthrough handy or you will be going back and forth over stuff you missed. 5/10 from me.
EDIT: I'd be remiss if I didn't give some props to the soundtrack, which was excellent.

I personally had a lot of fun while playing SE:NZA, and regardless of whether players want to be marksmen and take high-distance, high-risk shots, or instead run into hordes guns blazing with submachine guns and grenades, there is something for everyone. The game is fine in single player, but is best in multiplayer.
Another HUGE bonus: this is one of the few zombie games (yes, UNIQUE Nazi Zombies!) that has OCCULT-based zombies. It's been a while since I've seen non-infected, non-chemically-alterted zombies. The Occult themes allow for NZA to be a fun, yet creepy experience that's good to play with friends.
Some downsides however:
- The game has a tendency to play at Low Priority. I don't understand why this is, but those with high-end computers might find the game chugging more than usual. It resets as soon as you start playing again. I still don't know how to fix this.
- Enemies can get stuck on stairwells, and very rarely enemies will not spawn, forcing you to restart the level.
- There are many achievements requiring one to play co-op. While I'm not opposed to co-op achievements, getting 2000 kills in co-op is useless, as you can simply set up a private, 1-player co-op lobby and get the achievement there.
All and all, a good experience. Recommended.

For Starters: I've disliked SAO since the 2nd Arc during the First Season.
But this game, it's not bad at all. In fact, I can't believe how much I actually enjoyed it. lol
Key Warning though, it has a lot of Text. But you are given a Skip Text Speed Scroll Button.
So if you are worried about not playing the game due to it being a heavy Light Novel.
Fear not.
But boy do those Cut Scenes last forever sometimes.
A lot of the Text is also Voiced. I found that particually impressive.
-----------------------------------------------------------------------
Multiplayer:
You can't play Multiplayer until about 2-6 hours into the game. Depending on your pace.
This is because it only unlocks after you complete the first Area.
After that you can play the content that you've unlocked with other people.
This means that if you want to play this game with the sole intention of only using Multiplayer, well then, Tough Luck!
The game's multiplayer is like a cross between Monster Hunter and Phantasy Star Online with a little bit of Final Fantasy 14 for Hud displays and other various content.
DLC-1: Multiplayer Useful.
DLC-2: Multiplayer Useful.
DLC-3: Multiplayer NOT as Useful.
Raids in specific Dungeons are a requirement if you want Sacraments. Basically Gems to put inside of your weapons/Armor to make them Stronger. You will still need them in DLC-3 if you want to max out your stats. But not as necessary because I'm sure that you can easily Solo the Tier 3 dungeons.
I would suggest taking on the NMs (Notorious Monsters) Online to get better weapons that eventually lead to a Legendary item after you've completed the first few areas.
-----------------------------------------------------------------------
Gameplay:
Speaking of Raids, I didn't find them to be as particularly interesting as people had told me.
I found the first Raid boss to be the most interesting. But nothing else from that point on was done to make them more complex, interactive, or interesting.
So the first Raid boss is very similar to the rest of them.
The Skill play in this game is more interesting though. Probably the best part of the game hands down.
Phantasy Star Online should take a hint and implement something like this.
-----------------------------------------------------------------------
Quick Tips:
Make sure to go to your Option Settings and set the Chat log to appear on your Hud.
A must have in my opinion.
Learn the SSC (Sword Skill Chain) System as quickly as possible.
Basically tap a SS (Sword Skill) button and when you see a Blue Shining Cross near your character's head, tap a different SS button to perform a SSC.
Also, try to hit the enemies after they attack but before the attack ends completely. Enter Weak Stance = More Damage.
Press Select on your controller to force your Skill Bar to appear manually and to put it away.
I'd advise using the Controller. The Keyboard settings are trash in my opinion.
--------------------------------------------
Minor Gripes:
The Tutorial was meh~
Very Grindy at times.
Lots of backtracking in certain situations. (I'm looking at you DLC-2)
Do not be surprised if you have to look up guides to find stuff.
The above wouldn't be so annoying if I could just Progress through the game with friends. Would have been more fun.
Other than that, it's mostly a single player game.
AKA: Multiplayer is only useful to grind stuff in my opinion. Or to do things that you couldn't normally do due to having low level gear.
I give it a 4/5~

Aight, after playing a while I decided to write this one.
:
: A lot of variety here. Different weapons to choose from. Different skills and styles to master. I don’t agree with some of the people saying its purely button mashing. But hey sometimes we all tend to do the same things again and again in almost any game. The combat is fast and fluid.
: I really like the hidden skill system. Much like in the anime, you need to meet certain requirements before you are qualified to unlock them.  Wish more games had this lol. I imagine it gives you that unique and rewarding feeling when you manage to unlock a certain skill set (you’ll know if you look into it :P) since it’s not easy.
: I am not a fan of visual novel style by any means. The voice acting is done well and any fan of the series will enjoy it even if you aren’t a fan of text.
Throughout the story you will go through many cut scenes about the characters and you get to know more about them. The voice acting in those almost brings them to life. They can be hilarious, like the convo with Philia, Klein and Agil in the café lol.
: The game does a good job of simulating an mmo atmosphere. From what I’ve seen, you can’t get drops on a mob that has been attacked by another npc party first. Maps don’t feel dead with the npcs running around actually killing stuff. The story is decent, though not unpredictable. It makes you wonder about the future with the positives and negatives of VR. Will be playing through the dlcs now.
:
: Most of the side character stories get resolved in visual novel style. There were instances where I was ready to battle but all I got to see was text to end the battle. Some of those fights could have been actual action. It might have been more impactful.
: Each time I get an email I feel compelled to do the quest that follows it (that’s just me). I am ok with the quests since they don’t require extra effort. Just kill things on the way to get them done. It is just that I don’t get why this requires you to get the quest by going to that npc. I understand having to go to them while turning it in. The constant “wanna meet up” emails can get annoying tho but can be overlooked.
: Though it is decent, it feels half done. You get to see your character during some cut scenes but that’s it.  I hope (and read) that this will change for the better. Regardless, if the name and voice settings are untouched, you can still have fun by just altering your looks without breaking immersion since those two don’t take well to your choice.
: Didn’t want to go through guides for this. Just jumped in and tried to figure it out myself. I just feel that the intimate mood is a bit too randomish which makes it a bit frustrating, only if you are pursuing that particular dialogue subset. I should be able to direct what moods I want (without unseen factors) to set as was the intention of the system (I think).
:  If you are even slightly used to hearing Japanese, you’ll notice that some translations are a tiny bit exaggerated as a form of fan service. Regardless if you can’t notice it then it’s all good.
: There is this bug where you get stuck in place and can't move. It can be rectified by re-equipping gear. It seems to be common amongst players but I have come across some who have stated that they haven't experienced it. This is one bug that can annoy you if you are unlucky enough to encounter it. From my experience it has to do with the difference in plane elevation or so. There might be other causes.
Anyways, Overall, it’s a positive from my side. It is good a game. It needs some polishing. Hopefully, the series gets the support to make that happen in the future! The things that can be improved on prolly won’t bother many, especially the fans and they aren’t exactly negatives and more of a preferential thing. Thanks for reading!

Just finished the main story and the 3 DLC stories in 96 hours. That's fairly barebones besides having to stop for a day and just grind out levels. Overall I enjoyed the game I think it has really interesting mechanics however there are a few negatives.
Pros:
There is so much to do that if you have an itch just to do all of it you'll be busy for a really long time.
There is some complexity in the mechanics, Button mashing only works until about the first DLC pack then you have to actually learn how to play with tactics and plan each button press.
The game is sorta like the alter ego of SWTOR, where swtor was an MMO that played like and single player game and this game is a single player game that plays like an MMO.
Cons:
The port has some memory leak issues in later DLC areas and using a controller sometimes requires a work around and if you do buy the game make sure your mouse cursor is off the screen when using a controller or else it'll mess up commands and targeting.
Buffs are really strong, too strong, if you get the right buffs and a good weapon you can kill something several levels higher than you.
*SPOILER* While you can make your own avatar, you are still technically Kirito. Your cutscene voice is Kirito, if your avatars name is Kirito the other characters will say Kirito, if it isn't Kirito they won't say name in the cutscene, if you play a girl avatar you still hear Kirito's voice which is kinda weird. There is an option to turn it off but I feel like it messes with the flow of the cutscenes.
for 50$ this is actually a great game if you are looking for a sorta MMO itch without playing with other people. there is multiplayer but it's entirely optional.
If you need something to do while waiting for Fatal Bullet to come out I'd suggest this, if you play 8 hours a day every day until Fatal Bullet comes out you might be finished with the game 100% by the time Fatal Bullet comes out.

I love this game and have barely stopped playing it since I got it.
Positives:
The community is fantastic. Most servers you end up on, if you ask for help then someone will answer. Of course there's always the odd place where no one talks, but just wait until later in the day or try to switch servers, and you'll find some people who will help you as much or as little as you need. It's also pretty easy to re-connect with people you met previously - I've made loads of great friends and usually see at least one of them every time I open the game!
Gameplay is fun, there's a huge variety of missions, it's pretty addictive, and just overall I can't put this game down.
Online mode is the best part of this; I never thought I'd prefer it to solo mode, but nearly all the missions can be completed with other people if you're struggling. The game gets hard in places, but you need never struggle when Online mode is just a click away! (Except the grind race in the sewers. That one is bull, and no one can save you from that.)
Negatives:
The 'main ending' is a bit disappointing. However, for those who really want a better ending... there is a way to get it ;) The final mission is also complete bull, and the best way to beat it is either cheese the AI, or gather together about 5 people online to brute force it. Some of the other missions seem equally impossible to get medals on, without an online army.
There are bugs. It's fun when you fall through the world after collecting a gamegirl in some hidden corner of the map. The final area was so laggy that it crashed me the first time, and the second time I had to face backwards until I got deeper into the map. But, the glitchy areas are actually useful for finding cool arenas to play custom gameball or races, and the devs are always putting out updates to fix the major bugs. Several things were broken when I started playing, and two weeks later they were working perfectly. You just might need to play on very low quality if you have a computer that wasn't really built for gaming, like mine.
A lot of people pirate the game. This is nothing the devs can fix, but it gets sadder every day seeing the number of people with their name in red text increase (something the devs put in to show off & shame the pirates). Please buy this game - the 50+ hours of fun it's already given me are well worth the cost (though a sale discount never hurts).

It seems the Shantae series have been going for quite a while. Actually, this series began on the Gameboy Color but I have only heard of it recently. Well, not that recently as in the Nintendo DS days I heard about a game called Shantae being released on the DSi Shop but as I didn’t own a Nintendo DS DSi, only the Lite model I kind of forgot about it.
A few years forward and many more games of this franchise have been released on pretty much all platforms and after seeing some charming graphics and pretty artwork I, being a sucker for a good 2D platformer, decided to give it a go.
Honestly, I did hear this game was good but I couldn’t possibly imagine it would be this good! I played Shantae and the Pirate’s Curse on PC and I have to straight out say it, this is certainly one of the best, if not the best 2D platform game I have played on PC.
You start your adventure just chilling in your home when your arch nemesis knocks on your door and you are set for a new adventure. While Shantae and the Pirate’s Curse is a 2D sidescroller it is more than it seems at first glance. At start you have Scuttle Town which is the main hub part of the game. There is where you can talk to most NPCs, always with great and funny dialogue. Here also you can buy items and upgrades but you may come back to the town for more than that as the game has different but welcome way to make you progress. Many times you’ll have to deliver items to NPC to help them with their troubles which in turn helps you move forward on your adventure. The best thing about it is that it is very organic and refreshing.
Aside from the main town you have islands you get to explore, find secrets but also in most of them there are dungeons which come in varied forms and each with new mechanics so the game always feels fresh. It is also good because as you gain new abilities they aren’t just used in the current dungeon and then forgotten, quite the contrary, they are all required in the subsequent dungeons and many are important to help you find secretes scattered around the islands.
The combat is not on the hard side but it is always fun. The platforming on the other hand, there are some pretty easy parts but when the game decides it’s going to be hard, it’s lovely. Such a good challenge but never frustrating as it is pretty lenient with checkpoints.
Gameplay wise, this game is a blast from beginning to end. I do love some Metroidvania games but on top of the already great aspects of the genre there is also some great characters and dialogue.
Another things worth mentioning is the graphics which look lovely. The game has a charming pixelated graphics but always full of color and details. Also, we have the music which is fantastic. The music is in fact so good I’ve been humming the theme for the town for a while now.
Overall this game is a must play. I can’t recommend it enough. If you are in any way intrigued by this game, be it the graphics, the 2D gameplay or the adventure aspects, please give this game a go because I doubt you will regret it.

There is simply no questioning the artistic integrity of this dated action exploration roleplaying game. Graphically the fidelity has not held up well over the years, but taking in the voracity of its design, here is a piece of art that will leave a lasting impression in the hearts and minds of players for generations. There's no question that the purity of vision afforded by the influence of the incomprable David Bowie is a driving force in the emotional tangibility of this world.
Bowie provides several songs which serve as set pieces for the digital stage, and also cameos as a guiding character with the peculiarity and vision we expect from the creative visionary. Always a leader in many frontiers, the digital in particular, one might easily forgive the less than fluid manner in which different game styles are meshed in ways later perfected, but rarely with such passion.
A screenshot has the presense of a painted work of art, a feat rare when this game was released. It is unflinchingly challenging, with themes sexual and moral that will bring the jaded player pause. What are you doing and why? For whom? A question this game seeks to explore, where only you can provide the answer.
A rare game that suits its most notable collaborator. The daring and adventurous would be remiss in passing this game by. Do yourself a favor and study this piece, as it is of the time and timeless in its presentation.
Rest in peace David Bowie, I'm still speechless...

With David Bowie's recent passing, I'd imagine a lot of people will be learning about this game that were unaware of it before Omikron is a game I've tried to complete several times now, but I doubt I ever will. It's really a shame, because on top of it having both Quantic Dream and David Bowie attached to it, it has some pretty interesting ideas, like being an open-world adventure game that combines multiple combat genres and a neat resurrection mechanic where during certain parts of the game your death will result in your soul (described in the game as being your own, real-world soul, transferred into the game as a trap) moving into a different character with new stats.
Unfortunately, the game was just too ahead of its time, and as such almost every aspect of the game is flawed in some way. The standard adventure mode plays out like an extremely clunky version of Quantic Dream's later games (like Fahrenheit and Heavy Rain), but the cities are terribly designed and the signs are written in a font that I can only assume was designed to be incomprehensible until you stare at it for several minutes, and as such the only way to reliably travel is by taxi, which essentially defeats the purpose of a open world, let alone the issues I had later on where addresses I had read wouldn't show up as destinations at all. The FPS segments are arguably the only part of the game that works the way you'd expect, but they still feel sluggish and the controls aren't that great. The fighting game portions are the real nightmare, since those are usually the parts where you can be truly "killed"; they play out as if the developers got completely trash-face wasted and then played tekken until they passed out and used that as their inspirational focus, and while there does seem to be some form of a combo system in the game, it doesn't tell you how to use it, and the controls are slow enough that I probably couldn't manage them anyways, so every fight is really just a test to see how quickly you can successfully do a downward leg sweep to known the enemy off their feet and then keep doing it over and over in a stunlock until they die.
I would love to finish this game, because even though he barely seems to appear in the game outside of concerts I would love to listen to more of David Bowie's acting, and the story seems legitimately interesting, but the game is just practically unplayable, and even though I make it a little bit further each time I pick it back up I doubt I'll ever manage to finish it without giving up. This is the sort of game that I would love to see remade by Quantic Dream now that they have the tech, but I doubt they ever will. Ultimately, if you want to remember David Bowie, you're better off rewatching Labyrinth instead of playing this game.
R.I.P David Bowie.

Hey!.. Yeah you!
Are you one of those people who watched Sword Art Online and afterwards thought: "Damn if only Kirito ended up with Lizbeth instead of Asuna, or maybe Sinon or Yukki.... hell maybe even Leafa or Silica, because hey why not that's not weird at all"
Well do I have the game for you.. Where literally everyone, and I mean EVERYONE, around you can be your next Waifu.
-A more serious review-
If you have not watched the anime I highly recommend you do so before even considering buying a game about it. I say this because there is a LOT of talking in this game between the main characters, typical of games in this genre, and if you know nothing, you will quickly grow bored of it. Just an FYI...
There is a lot to like in this game. It successfully captures the SAO feel perfectly, even going as far as to have roaming parties of AI battling out in the wilderness, a nice touch that makes the game feel more alive. The story, so far for me, is solid with plently of cutscenes and chatter between characters. I have no problem with this personally and see it as a positive rather than a negative, although I will say the translation could of done with some improvement. The art style and graphics are nice, it is a port so I didn't expect anything amazing although a remaster would of been appreciated.
Combat is satisfying and diverse, choose any weapon you like and any role you like. Wanna be a healer or tank, no problem! Chaining skills and attacks with your companions is vital as it allows massive damage gains for quick slaying of harder mobs and bosses.
As I hinted in the beginning there is an affection mechanic. This is used to prioritize what your companions do while in the field, as in either focus on healing, buffing, attacking etc by rewarding them with a 'Good Job' when they do something you approve of while out in the field. But this is also used to get closer to characters, and I mean WAY close, to the point you can literally take them to bed... for some pillow talk. I have never seen this in a game before now and I find it a real positive point. I actually care about my companions, something games fail nowadays. You can take them for walks and do some casual dating, as well as gifting them presents which normally consists of new gear. If there is more than that, I don't know about it yet...
There is a LOT of content here to enjoy and I can see myself putting in 100s of hours to do and see everything. There is plenty to do, although I will point out there is a lot of the same thing to do. Expect to be doing the same things over and over...
The game runs fine. I have maxed out settings at 4k and the game runs perfectly, it's a nice change to see a decent port from consoles. There is a small issue with getting your controller to work that can be easily resolved through the Steam controller settings.
I will mention a few negatives here, as the game is far from perfect.
The AI can be kinda stupid... and in some cases really stupid. This makes most fights, outside of bosses, a little easy as they provide no challenge whatsoever. This is a big problem, but one I can ignore. I will note this also applies to your teammates, I have seen my partners just standing around doing nothing while a boss is kicking my♥♥♥♥♥♥.
While the game feels openworld, it's very tunneled. I would of prefered one huge open map rather than several small corridor style areas.
Repetitive. While I can deal with this, I am used to it from other games I play, but I feel I should mention it for everyone else. There is a lot of fetch quests which makes you go back and forth. I can put up with that.. You may not be able to, consider that before purchase.
It can be more of a visual novel than a videogame. As I said earlier there is a lot of talking and cutscenes. I have no problem with this, but for some it may be a bit of a chore.
Well that will about do it. Im sure there are other points I have not touched apon, and I will update as I progress through the game if I find something that must be noted on. I recommend the game to anyone who likes SAO and JRPG's, like plently of dialogue and enjoy a more relaxed gaming experience.
Edit 1: Well I never thought I would forget to mention there is a character creator at the beginning, oops my bad. This allows you to create your own ID in the world of SwordArt and while I found this to be a neat add-on I still found myself playing as Kirito, the default character you are set too. There is a huge reason for this, no matter how you make your character, including gender, you are seen as Kirito in everyones eyes while playing through the game. This can break immersion as you will see Kirito in the cutscenes, and hear his voice in the dialogue, regardless if you made your own character or not. Yes even if you make a female you will have his voice, luckily there is an option to turn his voice off if you wish.
Edit 2: The game does a terrible job sometimes of explaining just where the hell your meant to go, or what your meant to be doing. This has resulted in me needing to look up guides on the internet to get me through some areas.... that should not be needed. I have fought through it, but it's been frustrating to say the least.
That's a couple of edits for now. The Pro's still outweigh the Con's by a large margin and as a result im still loving the game. I still have so much to do (140hrs in). The story is still great and interesting, there is still plently of chatter and cutscenes. Ah hell there are even familiar faces I was not expecting to see in the game now! :)

This game is very unstable. Servers crash often. System is easily exploited, and it is P2W. Trion games are usually pay to win, so no surprise there. End game is really slow. Grinding is tedious and repitive. Not a lot of options after you max level cap. Bosses are predictable, no versatility or challenges.
If you are a limited account, meaning you have not purchased anything on Trion games, beware of this game. You must spend a minimum of $5 or else you will be restricted from lots of resources and vendors within the game.
I have played 431 hours so far, have 4 characters, our of 5 classes. The 5th class is only available through purchase. Again, money.
Customization is very limited. Don't expect to make your character have various tattoos or hair styles. There's about 5 you can pick from. Classes are gender locked. Only 2/5 classes are male.

To put it simply, the pros are really straightforward : The gameplay, and the freedom.
Running freely throught Haven District is a real pleasure. Some races are challenging, some missions are fun. This is really nice to play.
Then the bad side of this game comes to hit you behind the neck : The police system. But in Jet Set Radio, policemen were rather stupid and kinda easy to bypass. Here, it really just ruin missions. I mean, when I'm racing or playing gameball, I don't want any security police to ♥♥♥♥ with me, I just wanna play the mission I'm playing. The fact is I'm writing this review out of frustration :

This game really feels like it was made by people who didn't care what they were doing. This is a mystery game with basic contradictions in the facts of the case. For example, there's a police report that claims a character was found 'not guilty' on Dec 1932, for a crime they were originally arrested for in either March or May 1933 (another inconsistency). The dialogue is incredibly disjoined (half-clinical, half written-by-someone-not-quite-fluent-in-English), and their idea of making it "noir" is to repeatedly use the same two or three Depression-era or Italian-immigrant words (e.g., "joint", "Dannazione"). Also, when they talk, their models just chomp robotically for about two minutes longer than it would have someone to actually say what's being said. Textures on important characters are misaligned and then repeatedly shown close up (GOOD GOD PLEASE FIX THE LITTLE GIRL'S FEET, she looks like a cripple). Some of the puzzles are so contrived it's ridiculous. At one point you need to cheer someone up by finding some music on the radio, but there's like five frequencies with music and no hint as to which one she would prefer. At another point you need to get through a door with a barrel in the way, and the only way to do so is to pull a nail (one of 5, the only one you can pull out) from a pile of disused boats, then drive the nail into the barrel with your bare hands to drain the barrel of fluid so you can move it. Yup.

The game is a quite good technical job: nice graphics, nice voice work, interesting story... It had everything to be perfect, but things were implemented just all wrong.
The "puzzles" are simply a matter of finding something well hidden in the scenario and, once you find it, you basically need to move your mouse in the right directions and there goes the "solution".
The path you have to take to follow up with the story is made way too explicit by the thoughts of the character. His monologues always tell you what to do next, as hints you didn't ask for.
But the worst is that this game just kills the basic principle of point-and-clicking: exploration. Most objects only become available for use when the character already realized that he needs it. So the first time you explore the ambient he will say something like "I don't need it" for almost everything you try to interact with, but then after some stupid event that makes the character think "Hey, I need a
for accomplishing that" then suddenly the
can be picked up(or turned on, closed, open, or any other interaction that was previously unavailable).
It's a big challenge killer, you never really get the opportunity to think things through. As soon as the problem is presented, the character's consciousness gets to the answer for it, inevitably preventing you to draw any conclusion by yourself. What keeps you playing is just the hope that at some point all that seemingly pretentious work will actually turn into something fun. But I guess this is just an illusion...

THIS IS NOT THE MAGICKA I FOUGHT DAEMONS FOR
Here's a trillion reasons why this game sucks.
THE SPELLS
The spell system has been lobotomized - there are now no efficient ways of killing anything and the skill cap is barely half an inch off the ground. The whole point of getting good in Magicka was knowing good spells, improvisation and casting fast enough to heat the keyboard to thermonuclear levels. There is no fast casting now, everything is charged or channeled, even the damned mines have to lie there for a while before they are of any use. There are no good spells because every spell is equally pathetically weak now. There is no flexibility because no matter what you cast it just works the same, that is barely even works.
Projectiles suck because you have to charge them for eternity to actually hurt anything.
Charging mines suck because nobody ever used them as actual mines anyway.
Fire sucks because everything regenerates and anything but focused fire does jack sh*t.
Freezing sucks because frozen things are now stupidly hard to kill. Especially in singleplayer it's just unusable.
Steam sucks because its only purpose was to boost lightning.
Not being able to extinguish oneself while having water immunity sucks.
Lightning sucks because it can't be added to beams. Arcanized lightnings have no sense, it's just adding plain, boring damage to a spell which already is all about damage. The whole point of adding arcane to lightning was increasing the range.
THE ENEMIES
The enemies suck too. They shifted from crowds of cannon fodder to being the freaking Terminator. The goblins in Magicka 1 were not there to be a threat, but to be bombarded with fireballs and run around screaming in a kinaesthetically pleasing way. The trolls, orcs, beholders, mages and all the rest - they were the real enemy. Now not only the trolls, but also the regular soldiers, the goblins and even the damned peasants are made of kevlar. You're no longer a powerful wizard, you're an idiot in a bathrobe throwing colorful lights at things.
The enemies are also really boring, you fight the same generic dudes in pointlessly fancy armor and glowing weapons 90% of the time. The other 10% is bugs. Magicka 1 had orcs, daemons, dwarves, bugs, undead and several tricky monsters too. There are no cool bosses either. Where is the Reaper, the Fafnir, the Jormungandr of this game? Only the final boss is actually interesting.
Everybody has elemental attacks too. I get this was supposed to make the game more challenging, but instead it's just annoying because it DECREASES THE CONTROL THE PLAYER HAS OVER THEIR WIZARD. 90% of the time you're trying not to be burning, wet, chilled, on the ground or in the air just for a freaking second instead of ACTUALLY FIGHTING. There is no way to defend from the bombardment of annoying crowd control attacks, because the shields and armors barely block anything now, the walls are weak and the auras only really protect from one element.
Except from the disruptor magick, which blocks casting, in a game built entirely around casting, and so just pointlessly stretches the fight.
Enemies have way too much health too, killing them is just slow and tedious, especially and lower difficulties. Adding a weakness to one element fixes nothing because it rewards using the same one or two spells over and over again.
THE GEAR
The eqipment sucks. Magicka 1 had a helload of weapons which were mainly here just for sh*ts and giggles. Most of them were useless and that's why obtaining a strong weapon felt like an achievement. Now every weapon is close to useless because of the balance this game never needed.
The robes suck as well. Magicka 1 had robes for everyone - some were there just for the looks (if you wanted to look sleek without any side effects), others could change the game completely. Magicka 2 robes just shuffle around some resistances and that's it. They're also not as varied and crazy as Magicka 1 robes.
The magicks suck. They can't be cast in quick succession anymore, further reducing the reward from memorizing and learning to cast quickly while also slowing the game down. There's too few of them too. Magicka 1 allowed to completely change the playstyle just by using some magicks one normally doesn't.
THE CONTROLS
The "click to go" movement sucks, it feels unresponsive and more like Diablo than the top down shooter Magicka is supposed to be. It's also annoying when you automatically send your wizard into a crowd of enemies just because you put the cursor on them to aim better.
The menu sucks, it's not ergonomic at all on PC.
NON-GAMEPLAY THINGS
The humor sucks because there barely is any in the latter half of the game.
Even the world sucks. Gicka 1's Midgard was a simple and full of cliches old enough not to be annoying anymore. It had barbaric orcs, sneaky goblins, evil warlocks and ugly demons. It was simultaneously a parody and a pastiche of classical fantasy from before WoW.
Gicka 2's Midgard is made of modern cliches, with all of its generic not-scifi-at-all magitek, overdesigned scenery and characters (which were there since TOSotC, also by the new developer) and the SUPER RAD ORIGINAL fantasy race in the form of Vanir. The Vanir suck especially hard, the game is just busy pretending they are really cool. I bet someone in the plot department likes them waaaaaaay too much.
Arcane being called death sucks. Everybody now uses death magic, the good guys, the bad guys, the morally ambiguous guys. Death also seems to act as the generic magical energy for some reason. The new death spells are supposed to sound ghastly, which is way less satisfying than the PEW PEW PEW of arcane. And there is no more artificial vs natural contrast of arcane vs life, which was way more interesting than just life and death.
And why do all the soldiers have female voices? Is this some kind of a logic defying matriarchy?
And why is Khan a freaking woman? It's not even a joke. It's just a huge, buff, fat orc who gets called warlady because f*ck this game i quit.
I probably forgot about some things.

If this is your first entrance into the franchise then I doubt you will be as disapointed as myself and many other fans of the series are of this addition. It is not a bad game by any means, but it is certainly not a sequel which does justice to the original. It has taken everything great about the original and just made it a little bit worse in almost all areas, which as a whole makes the game just seem like a bland cash in.
So youre probably asking what made the original so special? Magicka was a combination of a very innovative spellcasting system mixed with a very funny referential adventure spanning a mystical world. The combat can be broken into two systems; Spells and Magicks. Spells are what you get by combining up to 5 of 8 different elements; for example Fire and Water makes steam, while Fire Water and Arcane makes a beam imbued with steam. Earth and Fire creates a flaming rock projectile that explodes in a raging inferno. Perhaps you need a patch up? Drop an Earth and Life boulder on your head to heal yourself. Magicks are what we would traditionally think of as spells, they are things you unlock in the game to cast incredibly powerful spells with unique effects. Arcane Lightning and Fire will allow you to run incredibly quickly. Cold and Shield allows you to slow down time to a crawl, giving you the ability to weave around incoming projectiles. The fun comes from how many combinations of Magicks and Spells there are. The original had over 20 unique magicks, ranging from creating a wall of fire to summoning death himself to kill your enemies. Spells could technically hold up to 10 elements when you factored in Fire and Water combining to fill a single slot out of your 5. This allowed for amazing spell combinations such as the fabled Steam-Steam-Arcane-Lightning-Lightning spell. It was incredibly powerful because you could shoot someone with steam thereby wetting them and making them more vulnerable to lightning all in one spell. Normally you would need to cast water, and then cast a lightning spell afterwards. It was overpowered in the base game, but DLC addons created enemies which were literally immune to this spell and created the need for ever adjusting to the resistances of new enemies. Magicka 2 removed all of the fun from both of these systems. There are something like 10 magicks in the entire game, only one of which is very exciting; a spelled called dragons breath which you get in the second level and is so strong you will use it for the entire game. The rest of the spells are bland; a stone that heals in an aoe, a speed spell from original, the ability to summon a few enemies, and a few others which i never used besides the first time i tried them because they were so uninteresting. The original game gave you ability to go invisible and then charm enemies to fight for you. This game also removed the ability for elements to combine, an attempt to remove some of the clunkyness from the original. So yes, you no longer get the overpowered beams of before, but they were only overpowered because of poor balancing in the base game. The DLC's proved that proper balancing made overpower spells impossible.
Somebody else below stated it perfectly, Magicka 1 would have made a fantastic sequel to this game, but instead we are left with something which feels like a large step backwards in the franchise. I could go on for ages about how much worse this game is than the original, but if you haven't played Magicka 1 then none of these points will matter. Just play the first game, it is a cheaper and better experience. Then if you want more Magicka play the DLC as they are all fantastic experiences. Only after that should you play this game, and even then I wouldn't recommend purchasing it unless it is on sale for $5-$10.

Its unfortunate that software with a very small, very dedicated, and very hard working team come up with a solid beautiful product, but ultimately shoot themselves in the foot with lofty ambitions and an inability to prioritise.
It is a difficult product to review, as just with plenty of other games and various software or sim packages in the past, there is the demonstration product (which isnt what im reviewing here) and then there is the 'finished' product. Laminar have fallen into a newly created catch all (trap from a consumers perspective) of having a fantastically immersive and pretty demonstration product showing how well their ideas work, but then trip themselves up by releasing a 'commercial' product at a lofty $80 with a long list of features, the fully working parts of this sim, are fantastic, but are all of the same stock standard functions of any other flight simulator.
Laminar work very very hard on getting THEIR standard features of their flight sim working, and fastidiously update them as they work futher on the product... BUT......
The problem comes when you look at the list of features that are meant to be unique to X-Plane, and thats when you run into a long slew of inherently broken, unworked on, promised, or somewhat-working-low-priority-to-fix issues, that on enquiry are met with a slew of 'Well it IS just a pre-release beta version, of course there are going to be issues'
What you get for your $80 - is the Demonstration area which has been spit polished up the wazoo to make sure you get a feel for what the X-Plane world is meant to be, and a handful of beautifully detailed aircraft with 3d cockpits. However, its not just a plug in the joystick and go type sim. In this regard, its supposedly meant to be a little fiddly working out how to start this and switch on that, including working nav and com (debateable - ATC was an original 'selling point' feature from day one, that has remained inherently broken since day one) systems which add to wonderful immersion.
What its not meant to refer to, is having to fiddle around with background simulator options just to make an aircraft flyable in the first place (it took about an hour of googling various unrelated things to find a fix for utterly uncontrollable pitch flutter for instance) and often requires fiddling about when loading another aircraft. Thereby breaking the previously aforementioned immersion again.
There is a decent sized community providing plenty of aircraft, but these are fairly badly organised, and doing a general search for specific aircraft generally brings up masses of repaints of aircraft, and you WILL download plenty, but it will take a few error indications trying to open the aircraft in the game before you figure out that most of the files youve downloaded are only repaints of a stock aircraft you dont have, and is no longer available. One particular person has worked wonderfully hard on some fantastically detailed F-14s and F/A-18s for instance, but theyre all based off an airframe made in the in game tool, with little internal detail, and the external detail it does have, doesnt really mean much when the AI flying it lands by lining up a beautiful approach, shutting down engines about 50ft above the runway, then nosediving straight into the ground. (According to most of what i can find, this is either - completely normal/user fault for not creating routes for an aircraft theyre not going to fly/non existant (always followed by a video showing one of the demonstrator aircraft on a demonstrator airfield)/it IS beta you have to expect problems/your computer is too slow/youve got a third party mod not compatible with your ai) - Occhams Razor would say - games broke.
Easier to review the scenery outside of the demo areas or the hideously overpriced payware available - Its basically crap. The huge downloads for regional scenery are little more than big bump maps overlaid with ICAO points, overlaid with generic objects. Melbourne, for instance, has a 1.5km tall 'Eureka Tower' somewhere in the middle of hawthorn. (Thanks be to the crew behind VOZ  for fixing that, yet more third party freeware modders that work harder than the original developer - Melbourne actually has its bridges and biggest buildings in the right place)
Ultimately, unless Laminar want to drop the price to something far far far more reasonable, and make all base software for it part of the price. and ensure anyone that actually has paid the current price for this gets all updates and payware in future either free or a drastically reduced price, this really is not software that is close to being worth the price tag.
Excellent sim, but the price, the broken promised features, and the perpetual 'Beta status' excuse for anything outside of standard flight sim fare being broken combine to me absolutely regretting biting the bullet and paying for this.
I would highly advise downloading it first and seeing if what you intend to use it for is broken or not then go from there, but this certainly isnt worth a casual purchase with cheap hardware.

It's going to be a tough act finding another kinetic novel to read that measures up to this one. Couldn't have asked for a better induction into the genre and form.
There were moments about two-thirds of the way in when I was getting a little bored, but good things come to those who wait. The ending is (for lack of a better phrase) explosively kinetic. Even when nothing much was happening, however, I felt compelled to continue by some inexpressible quality in the narrative. One Thousand Lies has the distinction of being the only game in my library to have incited me to whack the F12 key multiple times. Some of Ciaran or Claire's deep ruminative statements are just that memorable.
I also don't usually pay attention to sound or music, but One Thousand Lies has one of the nicest, least-annoying-to-hear-on-loop soundtracks that I have ever encountered. This is one reading experience that will remain with me for a long while - plot, characters, music and all.
Best of all, it's free! There's literally no reason to not try One Thousand Lies out if you're a fan of good storytelling in general.

This was a beautiful and inspirational story that left me crying after seeing the friendship and closeness between Chiran and the people surrounding him. The use of the Wolf's story temporarily was percieved as a tale of the struggle in the life of Chiran. The impossible goal of protecting everyone, that he so desperately wants but will never achieve. In the end, it appears to have a better and easier solution when all seems lost. The Wolf without companions or memories  represents Chiran, the man who wanted to forget his own memories because of the suffering he bought to all around him, the Sun represents his unfulfilled and uncompleteable promises that he so desperately wants to fulfill, and the Moon represents Luce, the one thing that filled him with the strength to continue another day and eventually his salvation. It was said that the story had no relevance by Ciaran and the author but I think that it is still a perception that the author intentionally left there. 'For one door to be entered, all others must be closed' defines that once a decision is made, no matter how hard you try, cannot be undone. Claire teaches him that this is false, and that you can always go back, that you can make mistakes and learn from them. I was not expecting much from 'One Thousand Lies' but there is so much self-reflecting that I have done thanks to this novel. It is the most touching piece I have ever read and I will continue to remember this novel throughout my life. The novel that made me question myself and reflect on how I affect other peoples lives. I would like to thank the development team for the time, energy and spirit they put into this project and the happiness that the answers bought me.

First of all, I'm a fan of the SAO stories (Read the books and watched the anime), however, this is the first game I've played of the series (Mostly because I don't own any consoles atm). The story is similar but it does goes on a tangent and follows it's own series of events.
The story in the books/anime has many faults in terms of game mechanics, being a gamer myself it annoys me once I get out of the 'let's enjoy this story' and into 'game mode'.
This game has some really good things, and some really bad ones. Just like the story in the books, it leads me to believe that whoever designed it is not a gamer themselves.
Good Aspects
1. The world. They made a very believable MMO setting with NPCs acting like players would in the field and in town.
2. Unique NPCs. You'll see them in town and in the field. You can befriend them and eventually take them with you to the field or date them, etc.
3. Quest Board. A good way of making Col (Currency) and getting some extra XP. Hunting quests, boss quests, mob drops quests (which come mostly from the Unique NPCs and help towards befriending them).
3. The Sword Art system. The active abilities are fun to combine in combat to use your combos and enhance your own playstyle. Use a weapon (sword, dagger, axe, etc.) to raise your skill level with it, which will give you access to new arts and buffs that you can learn by spending skill points.
4. Multiplayer. Is very simplistic. Play with friends or strangers to grind for gear or levels.
Grivances
1. NPC quests. They are monotonous once you start getting a lot of them. You pick them and then have to confirm every single one of them, even if they are 150+. Is very annoying. QoL (Quality of Life) would be to have a way to pick them and turn them in in-bulk.
2. Buffs/Debuff Skills. I rather have smaller buffs or debuffs turned into passive skills or reactive skills. Than having to buff myself every 30 seconds. And also they become completely useless towards end game. As passives/reactives they wouldn't become as useless.
3. Controls. Gamepads don't work well at the moment. At least I couldn't get mine to work. It took me a few hours, but I got used to using mouse + keyboard. I don't think I'll use a gamepad even if they fix the issues at this point. Another thing, with so many keys, there is no need for toggle keys. It should be Optional, not enforced.
4. Difficulty. It starts good and challenging, but it doesn't scale well. I got to a point around lvl 20+ when I could one shot trash that should be my level, world bosses (the lvl95 and above) were beaten with ease, and Zone Boses were done in under a minute. I went into the multiplayer at around lvl 30+ on Nightmare difficulty... they should rename it 'Stroll through the Park' difficulty. Bosses do decent damage, they just need to be more spongey.
Overall is a fun game, even with the grivances I have with it. However, it also is a niche game. Is not for everyone.
I'm not done with it, I'll continue until I finish it.
