This game is such a great classic game!
I bought it when it was on sale and since then I didn't really find time to play it, but when I was younger I used to play the sh*t out of it!
This game is one of the few FPS where one can actually care for the characters in the game, not like in CoD where everyone is a generic constellation of polygons...
And that's kind of odd, clones being more different from one another than those "realistic" soldiers in recent games..
In the following text I'll state some of the most important things and I hope, that one day you will like this game as much as I do!
Graphics and atmosphere:
The graphics are old, but what does one expect from a nearly 10 years old game?
Nevertheless it's still perfectly playable, the sceneries are filled with atmosphere, the levels change from desert like design to a more futuristic design and then jump back into a even more primal design. (I don't want to spoil anything, so I won't mention the actual places.)
_______________________________________
Characters:
You are the Boss. Like for real, his nickname is Boss. You are the commander of a squad of specially trained clone troopers, called Republic Commandos (roll credits). The rest of your squad are clones aswell, who could've figuered... and they also got special personalities;
Scorch, your buddy when it comes to set up some explosives! But don't be fooled by his profession, he is the calmest one and has a joke ready for almost every situation.
Sev, his long ranged abilites are only matched by his cold personality. He is your team's sniper, a rather quite guy but nevertheless still an awesome character. To say it in other words: "Sev is a pretty cool guy, he kills aliens and doesn't afraid of anything." (Got the refefrence?)
Fixer, fixing stuff that wasn't even damaged in the first place. Fixer is your computer hacking professional and has traits of both other team mates, focused on the mission, but still in for a good old joke!
_______________________________________
Soundtrack:
This. Theme. Is. Dope. Period.
Seriously, the Song "Vode An" is a song written in the old language of a fictional warrior cult, called "Mandalorians". This catchy tune was performed by a choir and goose bumps are guaranteed!
And that was only the main menu!
In the rest of the game you're able to enjoy different songs and resamples of the music from Episode 1-3 (Some people may dislike those movies, but the music was great though!)
_______________________________________
Controls:
The controls are normal FPS controls and even a new player only needs a few minutes to understand the controls.
It may not feel as fluent as in more recent games, for example the fact, that weapons have a fixed accuracy, that doesn't change when you fire more bullets, might look a bit clunky compared to our New-Era-Games.
_______________________________________
Gameplay:
You are the commander of a elite troop of soldiers, so you are suited to be able to withstand even the greatest problems, against all odds. Well, aslong as you are using cover and you're able to aim!
Speaking of cover, you can order your 3 different squadmates to do things like:
Slice that console, commando!
We could nee some explosives here!
Assign sniper position!
Mount that turret!
Those are just some of the commands, during a playthrough you are able to encounter various more.
_______________________________________
Storytelling:
Like I mentioned before, you will encounter different level designs, depending on your progress.
Every mission has various levels and when you completed your mission, you are deployed somewhere else, just like a real Clone-Trooper!
The game follows a chronological path and takes place in the time between Episode 2 and 3.
Most of the places you visit are part of the new trilogy viewers of these films will recognize them.
_______________________________________
TL;DR
Graphics+Atmosphere: 8/10
(Old but gold)
Characters: 8/10
(A shooter with actual CHARACTERS!)
Soundtrack: 9/10
(The music is simply stunning, just couldn't get myself to give a Halo-like 10, because Halo still owns the rank 1 most iconic music in my heart.)
Controls: 7/10
(Meanwhile a bit outdated, but still fine)
Gameplay: 7/10
(We could have needed some more crucial commands, if you're good, you can get through without ordering most of the time)
Storytelling: 7/10
(Sadly just a seven from me this time, but the story is a great stand-alone story, but at the beginning of every chapter one has to understand the situation, but you get your basic intel through loading screen and an intro from your mission adviser in a cutscene like start)

Playing this again, in a generation where the gaming technology has vastly improved, I can say proudly that Star Wars Republic Commando still holds up absolutely. This game utterly succeeds at immersing you into the spot of a Republic Commando, and all the squad management mechanics are fantastic in their design. Despite the fact that you play as the leader of a squad of elite death-dealing supersoldiers, this game is by no means an easy one. The opponents and environments you are put in are made to overpower you, and it's only through cold, hard strategy will you perservere. The story revolves around your Squad, and is grounded quite firmly there, in that everything in the game is seen from the visor of your player-character. All in all, if you're looking for a challenging, immersive, strategic FPS, and are a fan of Star Wars, you need this game.

I should probably point out that the original state of decay was the first ever open world zombie apocalypse game that I played. Long before DayZ, H1z1, etc. I put 46 hours into the original version of this game. I bought this version hoping for more, but basically just got the exact same game with updated graphics and sound and some general improvements to gameplay. If you've never played the original state of decay, I would suggest you play this... but I think the price of $30 is too much. Buy this game while it is on sale.
PROS:
-You are in an open, zombie infested world and can essentially go wherever you want and do basically whatever you want as long as you live. You have to rest though and the bigger your group is, the better off you are, as long as you keep supplies stocked. There is a story and you have to follow it if you want to beat the game, but technically you can just survive and explore as often as you prefer.
-You can grow a garden, build a medical center and can craft sniper towers in your base. There is some customization of bases in this game and it is interesting.
-You must maintain supplies such as food and medical. You can raid houses, factories, schools and collect weapons and loot.
-You can recruit other AI players that you meet, or you can deny them. You can let them into your group and if they start acting crazy you can send them packing or help them. You can control several different characters in the game and can decide who you want to play as, as you go.
-You can establish a base where you can build a small community of survivors.
-There are vehicles throughout the world you can take and drive. You can use the trunk to stash extra supplies to transport to your base. Driving around in this game feels a lot like the open AI world of Grand Theft Auto
-Different types of zombies provide various levels of challenge to kill. Sometimes hoardes come upon you while you are raiding a house for loot and you end up having to barricade yourself inside "Night of the Living Dead" style.
-The story, acting and soundtrack are all excellent. They keep you interested and engaged in the game.
CONS:
-There is no online mode. You cannot play co-op or with anyone online. This is a single player game only. This is a massive strike for some people, but understand that this is still a great game without online.
-You have to play this game in 3rd person. There is no option for 1st person.
-There is no way to customize your characters. You have to play as the survivors on the game. Lack of customization. You can techincally mod the game unofficially, but it can cause crash problems.
-The map lacks very large structures to loot inside of, such as a large hospital or large schoolhouse. You spend most of your time looting houses and small shacks or warehouses.
-There are no real destructable environments. Sure houses burn down and cars explode... but that's about it. You can't pull a fire axe out and chop a hole into a wooden house.

The music works so well in this game I have to call it out first. It's fun and upbeat and exotic, and sets the tone, pace, and rhythm of the entire game.
The platforming is great. It flies by quickly, matching the beat of the background music. Not quite as challenging as other platformers out there, but there are plenty of very satisfying moments, especially when discovering upgrades. The final stage does introduce a decent amount of challenge.
Varied and satisfying boss battles. Still not too difficult compared to other games. The Steam achievements surrounding boss battles sound insanely difficult, for anyone seeking more.
Likable characters and fan service abound. The dialog feels fresh, jokes not overdone.
The length of the game is just right. 8-10 hours for experienced gamers. Again, it flew by, and I was left wanting more, yet satisfied with the experience- if that makes sense.
Downsides:
- The beginning of the game (first 30-60 minutes) feels easy and boring. It picks up after that.
- A couple of the collectibles are obscure if you don't clear a room the way the developers intended. This makes backtracking/exploration tedious in a couple areas. The majority of collectibles make sense though.
Overall a fantastic and highly satisfying game. Pick it up!

Sword Art Online: Hollow Relaization (SAOHR for short) was a game that I've been wanting to play ever since it first released for the PS4 as an exclusive. Now that they have it ported over to the PC community, I can say in my honest opinion that the wait was well worth it and here are my reasons:
SAOHR is as it says, a unique story. I was not even 1 hour in, and just got past the myriad of tutorials when I got hooked onto the game. I wont say much, as to avoid spoilers, but from what I've seen so far it is well worth your time.
Now this is coming from someone who's been on a game like World of Warcraft for most of their life. SAOHR nails it pretty well when it's trying to make the world feel alive in the Singleplayer side of things. (I have yet to touch the Multiplayer side...) There are NPCs litterally EVERYWHERE! They are walking around the town, just going on with their day. Outside of town in the fields, you will come across parties of these NPCs just aimlessly killing mobs. You can join them with your own party, or as a solo, and help them kill even bosses that spawn in the world. This is a massive thumbs up from me.
YOU DON'T HAVE TO PLAY AS JESUS-KUN KIRITO! Change the name, hair, eye-color, skin-color, gender, and hair color. Even the voice you can change!
The combat, with all the sword skills and the number of weapon types to choose from gives you a lot of options as to how you want to play and what suits your tastes better. Want a Katana? Done. 2-Handed Sword? Go for it. Stick to the 1-Handed Sword? All completely up to you.
Now yes, at the time of writing this, I've only gotten around 6.5 hours into the game. Take what I say as my opinion, as you there, yes you who are reading this right now, can have a very different look on the game than me. I personally was not a die hard fan of the anime, but I didn't hate it either.
Yes. I personally think it is worth your time and worth the price since you get all the DLC that was released on the PS4 post-launch.

A single-player game with limited co-op play and dueling set in the SAO universe.
I'm recommending this game somewhat reservedly. This is a pretty niche game, but there aren't many in this niche, and it is well-done. About the most similar game I can point to is probably Kingdom of Amalur, but it's less Diablo and more Lineage 2 than that game was.
The basic qualifications of whether you'll like this game are two points:
1. Are you a fan of the SAO anime series?
2. Do you like single-player ARPG/Faux-MMOs?
While I have about ten hours in the game, there's a lot to do and explore. The questing is mostly main storyline and kill quests or collect quests.
With all the simplicity for the basic goals in the game, however, there is a depth to the systems I rarely see outside of detailed MMOs.
Combat can be as complex or simple as you care to play it. The game can be won by button mashing, but it's not the most efficient way of fighting. Good interplay between your party members and your fighting, allowing for support, switch for more damage, amazing combos, and multiple defense and offense moves which all rely on good timing to get the most out of the system. Facing and other positional moves are at play.
Frankly, the combat is some of the best single-player combat I've played recently. Choosing skills and their use, involved and intriguing combat that rewards you for playing well, and overall a general sense of interaction in the fight which doesn't make it "hit A, repeat until dead" make for a great game.
While I haven't gotten that far in this, there is a lot of VO from what I've played so far. The quest discussions/interactions usually happen in a 2D anime style with characters talking to you and not much input from you other than reading how it plays out. The storyline seems pretty linear so far. If you're a fan of the SAO anime series, you won't be disappointed - but if you're looking for story like TW3, this won't be a strong point for this game.
The game's mechancis are set up to be an early 2000's MMO. Which means most of the skills are unexplained, things are nested in menus inside of menus and not much is clearly presented. Many things show statistics you will never neally discover how they affect the game, or items which seem better but you honestly have no idea whether they are or not, because it's just a mess of stats without any idea of how they work.
Basically, a terrible MMO.
Which mechanics-wise, fits the SAO setting. While SAO was an interesting series, the base game mechanics themselves were cool ideas poorly implemented from a game design standpoint. This is part of the charm of the game, if you're looking for complexity and depth.
Well done textures, good layout of areas, detail to the NPC groups you run into in each of the areas, the other adventurers "playing" - all seem intricate and well thought out. Being able to recruit other adventurers was a nice touch as well. However, you cannoit customize these joined adventurers beyond prioritizing which skills they should focus on, and aside from group composition, this doesn't seem to make a big difference in actual play.
Keyboard and mouse support - well, what there is of it - is pretty poorly implemented. WASD to move and IJKL to position the camera is unwieldy and awkward, and the default mappings are terrible (for example, pulling up the character screen is SPACE and jump is O by default). You'll want to re-map every button from default.
Controller scheme is a little better, and it definitely plays better on controller. Getting an XBONE controller or Steam controller working just required some tinkering and enabling controller functionality though the Steam Big Picture mode.
Ultrawide is not supported, and by default the game is set to run at 720P and 30 FPS in borderless mode. The graphics settings are pretty exansive, though, so it's easy enough to fix. Even playing in 16:9 I get "squished" visuals during certain cutscenes showing the environment, so something is wonky there for sure.
I'm going to cut short the review here, because there are a lot of Let's Plays on this game out there for the PS4 version, and it's basically a decent port with some flaws. I would recommend this game to those who are looking for an SAO game or an "offline" MMO with decent combat, who don't mind using a controller.
For me, the game was filling a hole and thus, despite the technical points, I am enjoying it immensely. I don't believe the title would be worth the asking price to most people, so I'd have to say for most people, this would be "wait for a deep, deep discount" unless you fit the two criteria at the beginning of this review.

This game is positively fantastic.
Pros:
Exceedingly snappy and responsive controls.
Colorful graphics with just enough feeling to be taken seriously.
Multiple characters.
RPG elements (gear/exp levelups).
Extremely satisfying sound effects.
Addictive mini-games.
Competitive without being overbearing.
Very forgiving (ie; You were an inch or two from that rail, but the game lets you grind anyway).
The AI isn't entirely stupid...kind of.
Easy to get your adrenaline pumping.
There's a story to it all.
You can repeat almost all of the missions, and even beat your previous scores.
Truly seamless multiplayer (no load screens, only a ten second wait time to change to an online mode if you're unlucky).
Everything you do is client-side.
The developers are actually taking a huge interest in their community and feedback.
In multiplayer, anyone and everyone can participate in all content.
Amazing musical scores.
Truly made it as Jet Set Radio's spiritual successor.
There's a way to skip the tutorial...and how it is implemented is absolutely pure genius.
Smol game is smol (2 gigs).
Runs on lower end computers without looking like trash on higher end rigs.
Tutorial is simple but also interesting enough to keep attention.
Player character's existence is easily explained without seeming like utter bullcrap.
You are not forced to play by yourself or with others.
Cons:
Depending on the zone, you might get a little maddened by the constant loop of up to four tracks.
Though many mechanics are forgiving, the difficulty gets a bit much if you don't practice enough.
There's a few minor typos in NPC dialogue (not that big of a problem tbh but still listed here for now).
The AI sometimes decides to go jack off in a corner or completely vanish in missions (other times it works almost flawlessly and feels like a real player alongside you).
There are a few mechanics that are never talked about that I accidentally discovered using my tried and true method of randomly pressing buttons (unless this was addressed far later in the game...for whatever reason).
The Sewers
There is no party/find friend mechanic, so when you're playing with someone you want to find, you have to talk to each other in the chat (or in my case, Discord) in order to find each other unless you have a map in that zone.
Found a couple surfaces that didn't appear to be properly finished in a zone (you could stare into the void outside the level).
There is a way to Skyrim your way up flat walls without a hitch.
Default keyboard options are set to French (not quite a con I suppose, but it confused myself and my Australian friend right off the bat).
Time flies when you're having fun (it will make you late for work >.>).
All in all, the pros outweigh the cons. This is very much worth the money. Twenty dollars for this is nothing compared to the other titles that ask forty dollars so they can only do half of what Hover does. To be very honest, I dislike games like this, and I had the time of my life playing it. I even bought a few more copies for friends just so they could try it. You can really tell the developers put their heart and soul into this, and that's something very rare in this trying time of half♥♥♥♥♥♥♥indie companies.
Buy it. Play it. And above all, have fun with it!

I'm borderline about whether I recommend this game or not.  Do I deduct marks for falling short of something truly great, or reward them for getting close?  It stayed with me enough to write this review, but not enough to go through it a second time to pick out the nuances (maybe some day in the future. Maybe).
On the plus side: The backstory is brilliantly crafted, the characters have moments of genuine humanity and funniness, as well as a surprisingly emotional conclusion. The music is effective, too - setting the scene without distracting. The visuals are nice, the backgrounds giving a real sense of place rather than the generic 'school/home/cafe' scenes.
On the minus side: There's some dense and uninteresting dialogue, a lot of it concentrated in the first third of the story - I actually stopped after the second meeting with Claire, bored with the endless verbose verbiage that didn't seem to be going anywhere (as enjoyable as the moments in class with Ziva and Ausse were, they didn't point to an ending that I felt compelled to follow through to).
To me, the actual story begins at the birthday party, when the abstract philosophising and slightly improbable character introductions give way to actual things happening.  And from this point on, there is a solid and quite powerful narrative; the reveal of Ciaran's backstory feels real, and there's plenty of moments that felt like actual teenagers interacting that are quite engaging.
Ausse is excellent comic relief - a hard role to do well, and his interactions with Ciaran are genuinely fun. Ziva's sniping with Ciaran also has a nicely realistic feel. Diniz is a little underdeveloped, especially given his importance as revealed in the end.  Claire felt unrealistic; didn't quite fit with the rest of the characters, and not in an intentional way.  Luce had interesting depth. And Ciaran himself, rather than the usual two-dimensional narrator, has a compelling backstory that puts everything into perspective.
Which makes the unrealistic parts that much more jarring - when the cop pulled over the car, it was amusing; when the bartender broke the glass, it felt a little forced; when the waiter went over the top, it was a sort of mix of the two, I smiled but felt it breaking the suspension of disbelief just a little.
It's a mashup of things that work and things that don't - if I'd paid money for it, I would have been genuinely annoyed at the point where I first stopped playing, and I would have missed out on the very good bits after that point. Given that it's free, and taking all the very-good parts into consideration, I would recommend this; I just wish the story as a whole could have been the shining gem that's half-buried amidst the so-so ore.

It's been a few months already since I played this, before it was greenlit. But today I stumbled upon the notes I took while reading and, oh man, I owe it some words.
The plot and themes are deceptively simple and grounded, light hearted even, which is why I would recommend this to anyone wanting to have their first go at the genre. And there's no way to screw yourself over and getting an anticlimactic pooey end midway through the game by clicking the wrong box once either, so there's that. The flipside to this is that, well, you can't screw yourself over. That is what a kinetic novel entails, though: you have one fixed narrative, and you click wherever to continue reading and looking at pretty pictures. Also it's free. That's three reasons, and you should only need one to go and try it out.
For everyone else out there, here's three reasons for you, too:
1) The way the plot is layered makes it so that it can be enjoyed on multiple levels, depending on whether you're having a giant cup of black coffee while staring at Ziva's breasts and clicking furiously or not. I recommend you do. There's a great amount of detail put into the game and you will miss a lot of it. Your second playthrough will consist entirely in hunting the little rascals, be it references to other stuff, foreshadowing or hints as to what in the name of hell is actually going on. If you're like me, you'll end up with several pages of notes, quotes, and silly comments. And you will love it. But if you're a functional member of society you can just read it once, feel a warm fuzzy feeling in your stomach that resembles happiness and go home. Or stay there, or whatever. The prose itself might be a bit iffy at times (although it's generally decent), but the overall narrative is extremely well thought out and solidly constructed.
2) It takes full advantage of its medium in a way that reminds me of, say, Metal Gear Solid 2. Kind of. Not that they've got anything in common, but yeah. Alright, forget that. What I meant is that it would never work as a book, or a movie, or an RPG, or even a visual novel with multiple routes and branching decisions (oh,
not as one of those). It's nice to see an amateur work that's not just some badly written anime without, well, any animation. Each and every element is crucial and you should pay attention to them all, including the UI.
3) The music is pretty good, but the way it is used is even more worthy of praise. OK, maybe not, making music is quite hard. But it's true that it's very well utilized. Every track matches perfectly with the situation it's supposed to enhance, and it's never used just because it's cool or whatever. This, of course, is a given when talking about games with professional sound directors in the credits, but this is not the case, so it's surprising. Effects are very well placed too, even if some of them sound like crap.
Also it's free. That's 4).
On the minus side, they could really use an editor to polish some of the writing, and a dozen artists willing to work for free too. Or an actual budget, whatever.

The art was pretty okay, at least for the charcter sprites. The background was the classic "blurred photos" trick, but it fit quite well.

This is a nice and surprisingly versatile light strategy on a grave subject. Your playground: the whole world depicted as a classic Risk-like map divided into different socio-economical-political regions or territories, so to speak. Your mission: wipe out (or enslave in some more fantastical cases) the entire human race with a plague of your design. Get infectious, get evolved, get mean. Bubonic fun for evryone! Flashy graphics or hectic action not included, which suits me fine. The UI may be quite plain, but it's also very functional and easy to read and navigate.
The mechanics are simple to grab: enhance your disease with the DNA you gather by infecting (and eventually killing) people with your plague. More dangerous the plague gets, more humanity puts efforts to fight against it. Eventually it can be pretty hair raising race against time, when you try to find a decent infection and kill ratio to get all the 7+ billion of buggers on Earth and get them squished before the sicience does its trick on you.  With every win you unlock new disease types and optional properties for them. Difficulty levels may be ramped up from a walk in the park to boggling. And if meddling with bacteria, viruses, fungi etc. gets boring, how about a run with mind controlling parasite, revolution of the apes or good ole vampirism? These change the playing field a ot and let you think outside the box, which I found invigorating.
I'm always a sucker for all kinds of "easy to learn, hard to master" designs, and this is no exception. This is a kill'em all simulation of my taste, having lots of replayability and possibilities to design different kind of "what if" scenarios.

I do not play many casual games but I found Plague Inc: Evolved to be a fantastic distraction for me, having thrown much more time into it than I initially expected. I really enjoyed the medical science perspective of this game as it would lead to me often researching some of the horrible symptoms of these diseases and as a result improve my understanding of pathology. The geographic effects of the disease spread are well depicted and give good feedback to the player, aiding the understanding of the impact of their contagion. The game has also recieved a lot of updates and content to keep the gameplay fresh and challenging.
Some qualms I would have is that some of the art and music is a bit too heavily used and could do with some more variety. Additionally, some scenarios feel a bit too linear in their approach and could do with some rebalancing to allow more creative approaches.
Otherwise I would recommend this game to people who are looking for a game that can distract them from 15-45 minutes at a time, they can put down easily if they are busy but has some long term appeal through many scenarios and community content.

I rather enjoyed the first Magicka game and when I heard that a Magicka 2 was in the works, I was pretty excited!
Upon release, I was both satisfied and disappointed by the game:
Pros:
+ Many more Easter eggs
+ Updated visual effects*
+ Artifact system allows for customizable gameplay
+ Can still kill fellow wizards
+ Balanced around multi-player - no longer ridiculously easy with more than one player
* while the particles effects on the spells are updated, there are only minute differences in character models
Cons:
- Focus system takes away some of the gimmick in knowing and applying spell combinations to cast Magicks
- Unbelievably short story-mode
- Inability to merge elements (e.g. fire and water into steam) into a single element
- Balanced around multi-player - difficult to play alone
- Player control feels clunky
- Conjuring spells are not very responsive, although it is more responsive than it was in the first Magicka
Overall, while I enjoyed the game, I wouldn't recommend this game over its elder brother. While future DLC may help this skeleton of a game, I had hoped that the game itself would have had a little more flesh to it.

This game does a decent job, on an extremely basic level, at showing how plants function. The goal is to grow the plant to its complete size and harvest all of the seeds before the growing season is over.
Overall, the plants are very similar in that they have predefined growth points. Sometimes you get the option to grow a flower instead of a node, but not often. The only thing that really differs between the plants other than the looks, seed production, and some other basic things is that each one generates and requires varying amount of resources to create more roots, notes, leaves, flowers, and fruit.
What is not very obvious at first is that this is less about learning about the plants and more of a resource-harvesting clicker game. In order to gain any of the resources to keep growing your plants, you have to click on each part that glows. If you don't click as soon as the glow appears, the amount you can gather goes down and will eventually be lost. As your plant gets larger, the clicking turns into a frenzy. Meanwhile, you're also trying to grow more by clicking on the growth points.
Once you have a flower, not only do you have to tell the flower to create pollen, but you have to manually drag a bee to the flower. This wastes valuable time that can be used to click for more resources. Before the garden is fully upgraded, you also have to worry about clicking on pests, pulling off blighted leaves, and warming up frost-bitten leaves.
Even with all of the clicking requirements, I was able to obtain all of the achievements and fully grow the prickly pear within 2 hours. I haven't played it in Strategy mode, but the growth model is the same. I can't really see any replay value. There is plenty of room for improvement, such as more types of plants, freeform growth instead of pre-defined points, sandbox mode (no season timer, etc), and more realism.
I'm recommending it because it was a pleasant little game that is a bit different from the few in its class. Due to the lack of replay and the really short playtime, my recommendation is only if it's on sale. I bought this as part of a weeklong deal at 75% off ($1.24). My general rule for no-replay casual games is $1/hr. The sale puts it in that realm.

Gameplay - You "play as" a plant aiming to reproduce, and while this does sound interesting, it can devolve into a bit of a clickfest, especially with classic mode. That being said, classic mode was by far the more exciting of the two and I found myself concentrating and getting quite hurried, especially towards the end of the growing season! Visuals - Fairlly pretty! But for the simplicity, they need a pretty beefed up computer to run smoothly, and I didnt notice much difference between low and ultra, apart from the speed. The flowers look lovely, almost as a painting, but you dont really see them growing as such, just parts such as stems suddenly extend from a node.
Sound - AMAZING. Really lovely relaxing music that I felt was almost taking me away to a meadow - compliments the game perfectly and is great to relax with.
Replay value - UMMMMMM... I beat the game yesterday for the second time - this was the second time I played the game since I bought it about a year ago. It's a decent game to come back to now and again when you're in the mood, but for £4, it does seem a little much for such little replayability.
VERDICT: If you want a relaxing game that won't task you too much, this is probably a fairly good game for you. This game got off to a rocky start for some which is why the reviews look so poor here. Even now, I hear there are struggles with certain controllers. However, as someone who played it on keyboard on a low(ish) end laptop, I had a decent experience with this.
I was in love with this game back when it was originally released. I lost the disc copy I had back in '06/'07 and was longing for a long time for a way to play it again and my wish came true at the end of the summer last year.
The only technical issues I ran into when playing this was EARLY ON when there was a bug with the game crashing after completing simulator disc missions from the kiosk in hub areas. This has been FIXED now though and I haven't had any issues since.
The graphics didn't receive very much of a boost from the Gold edition of the game which seems weird for an alleged remaster, but a more accurate description would be a port. The game design is a bit outdated with limited backtracking availability for certain missed collectibles and the inconsistent behavior of parts of the already-completed game resetting itself with enemies and bosses.
However, all of that aside, this game is the bees knees. It's so addicting to try out different combos of characters and even making mini "builds" RPG style by matching up the right equipment to the right stat boosts on certain costumes to make your characters the most viable. Combat is simple but really fun. A handful of different playstyles can be achieved with the right setup. The Marvel universe is brough to life for casual fans and hardcore ones alike. The soundtrack is actually pretty catchy and will stick around in your head unexpectedly often.
The price is the biggest thing holding me back from calling this a must buy right now. I still recommend it due to the great fun I've gotten out of it, but if you aren't a humongous Marvel fan or don't have disposable income, I'd wait for a price drop. Even if you ARE those things, a price drop or a sale is probably your best bet. But definitely get it at some point!

I will start with the most important aspect of the game to me, which is also the only one I dislike : the difficulty.
Easy to learn, hard to master. Very hard to master.
I do timed challenges at least 10 times because the tiniest mistake can make you lose. Imagine if I was actually trying to get gold medals.
The path to success is painful and frustrating. Sometimes your character do things that would be good in certain situations, but are annoying when they slow you down or makes you miss an optimal trajectory : like, when you fall down a wall accidentally, your character grabs on an edge to not make you fall further (this is where the Rewind ability is useful). When you need to go down on purpose, it's annoying.
I wouldn't mind about those if the time allowed to make challenges/missions was longer and less pusnishing.
After short-timed challenges, let's talk about the difficulty of finding your path.
The city is built both horizontally and vertically, which I appreciate. Jumping from roofs to balconies to windows to plazas makes you feel free of movements. But also free of choosing your own path. This wouldnt be a problem if the way wasn't that hard to find in some challenges. But when you have to start from point A to get to point B, then back to A, then to C, then A...until you get to F (thinking about that 3rd mission of boxes delivery for Watabax), when there are no clear path to follow, it takes dozens of trying and failing to finish the mission with only 5 seconds left on the timer (imagine again if I was trying to get gold medals).
The city is big and a-maze-ing, literally.
Those were the negative points I had.
A neutral point here, about the chips.
The chips system used to upgrade your character may be a bit complex. Too many tiers of chips. Using too many of the same type of chips lower their effect, I don't really understand this, as there aren't numerous types, so you're kinda forced to use some types several times.
Being able to trade a few chips to get a better one is good, but not guaranteed.
I noticed there was, in previous versions of the game, a system of points you could spend on each category, like strengh, speed, jump... This seems easier to understand in my opinion. Surely the developpers had their reasons to change to a system with fancy chips.
Now, everything positive.
The game is visually very pleasant. Lots of colors (maybe a tad too many). While I cannot graphically run this game at the maximum (playing at medium and 30fps), I appreciate navigating in this living futuristic city, filled with many people of different races.
The music is simply eargasmic. Both Cédric Menendez and Hideki Naganuma are great. As a big fan of the Jet Set Radio games, I can't keep my head nor my feet from not moving to the beats.
Concerning the story, nothing exceptionnal but it's good (I haven't finished the game yet. I reached the Administration District). Your teammates all have their own distinctive personality and somehow go well with each other, often teasing and being teased.
About the controls, it's satisfying to just run and jump around the city. Grinding takes practice and sometimes you may miss a railing, forcing you to rewind a few times to get it right. Particularly annoying during timed challenges.
Overall : I really like this game and the atmosphere of its universe. But sometimes I just give up on missions, or skip optional ones, because of the difficulty. I come back to them later, knowing it will take many many tries to beat them.
Take away the tight controls of Mirror's Edge, misunderstand Jet Set Radio's color design, remove all polish, then throw in some poor map design and you've got Hover: Worst Subtitle of the Decade.

This game is extremely fun! While the controls take some getting used to, they really aren't as bad as a lot of people say they are. The missions are fun, and the open world is fun to explore! Plus, it can be EXHILIRATING to go fast and parkour your way through the map! It's easy to learn and hard to master, but it is worth mastering.

I really wish I didn't buy this on Humble so I could get a refund.
I wanted to enjoy Hover so badly. I've played through Jet Set Radio numerous times, both on Dreamcast and Steam, and I really wanted to play something similar, as no game has matched the aesthetic, gameplay, or soundtrack of it. Of those three things, Hover got only a single one right: the soundtrack. The aesthetic is filled with colors either far too dull or far too bright, clashing with each other in an extremely unpleasing way. As well as that, the gameplay is nothing to write home about. Awkward controls that try to use the mouse buttons for *every single function* and uninteresting game modes. It advertises as being online, and has the setup of an MMO, but to my knowledge there are no dedicated servers and no party-finding mechanics.
As well as the issues plaguing the core game, system requirements are through the roof for a game that really doesn't look very pretty. Everything is jagged and fuzzy, and despite meeting the minimum system requirements, I could not play the game on the lowest settings possible at my native resolution, and decreasing the resolution seemed to have no improvement.
To make a long story short, a spiritual successor to Jet Set Radio was a far too ambitious undertaking for amateur developers. I'm positive that, if they had more experience and focused on a more linear game like Jet Set Radio was, rather than trying to force in multiplayer and a bland upgrade system and any other mechanic they saw in popular AAA games, Hover: Revolt of gamers may have been a game I wasn't upset that I couldn't refund.

Starting off I would like to say that if you are someone like me who desperately wanted a sequel to jsr I would most certainly recommend this game. It even has Hideki Naganuma working on the soundtrack.
To give comparisons to this game I would say it is a mix of jet set radio, mirrors edge, and crackdown (not listed much). Even subtler influence in my personal opinion would be the collectathon genre as there is plenty of that here as well.
Your goal here is to revolt against a police force that hates fun and games. You explore a well crafted and sizeable cell shaded cyber punk city collecting items, upgrades, and spray painting over "anti fun" propaganda while also talking to npc's to do missions. Story is present and not the heaviest aspect of the game, but that doesn't take anything away from the experience. The main goal here is to explore and do as you please. Seeing how this game's main focus is parkour you traverse by wall hopping, ledge climbing, bouncing, and grinding on lines. The more smoothly you move across the environment the more your "hover heat" bar charges which allows you to move much faster and jump higher. Also collecting and applying upgrades to your character increases stats.
Multiplayer is seamless and has a very clean drop in drop out mentality whereas players in the city can run over and join missions without any loading screens. You can free roam and explore with anyone in the server and the best comparison I can give is to an mmo. If you do not prefer multiplayer there are private and offline options as well.
There are a few bugs and glitches but never have they ruined the experience. Some things may require more polish but overall the game is smooth and really nice to look at overall. Certainly needs more music from the legendary Hideki Naganuma.
Overall this game is suprisingly innovative in many aspects and you can tell it was made by real fans just like us. Nothing here has the offensive corporate ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥t like microtransactions or game breaking bugs because the devs rushed it. I believe this was genuinely made by people who are driven and inspired by their childhood games, I hope this game does well so that we can see more updates and content constantly added. There is still so much I didn't mention.

Well, to be honest, there is not much GAME in it. Even for a walking simulator, its gaming element is still scarce. What you do is basically walking around, investigating objects (with virtually no puzzle solving or whatsoever), and talking with a lady. The game is mostly linear, although you are free to wander off where you are told to go and explore the entire map.
The story is decent and engaging for the most part, but I have to say it kind of fell apart toward the end. The story builds up a very good atmosphere from the beginning and makes me genuinely curious about what has happened, but it ends up very disappointing and simply uninteresting.
The graphics is good and it runs well. I was told the audio was great; well, I'd say it's okay but not too impressive. The world is gorgeous and detailed, and I quite like its depiction of the wild national forest. Overall, I'd say it's been a very immersive experience.
Do I recommend it? Yes, if you like story-driven games/walking simulator with nice atmosphere and a beautiful map. If you are looking a GAME in a more traditional sense, then no, you will be absolutely diappointed.
Also worth mentioning is the price. I think 20 bucks is a bit too much for this game (considering you can finish it in about five hours and it has very little replay value), and I would not suggest buying it at full price. It's worth it probably for 10 bucks or below.

I'd like to vote "meh", but Steam still doesn't offer this option, so it's a negative vote mostly because the game description is misleading.
Offering the experience of wiping humanity from the surface of Earth using an always mutating pathogen agent (virus, bacteria and whatnot), Plague Inc fails at making it anything more than a very casual game, with basically only 1 strategy, and with unrealistic game rules.
If you're really curious to see how the game turns out, I'd personally recommend to pick it at less than US$5, as after a couple of hours in the game, there's almost nothing new to do nor see.
However, it's a very good mobile game, and I'd recommend it on mobile if you have 15 minutes to kill.
- original setting
- neat interface & visuals, although very limited quantitatively
- funny
diseases, although plagued by the same limitation of the game rules
- might encourage you to wash your hands ;-)
- You can wipe the humanity from Earth ; personally, I felt that a bit unsettling without being worthwhile, at least the first couples of times ; afterwards it was meaningless ; your mileage may vary
- the only strategy of the game is that you have to make your pathogen agent
to kill everybody before a cure is found ; there are slight variations, but it never diverges significantly from that
- causes & consequences are kinda hard to apprehend, so you play with tries & errors, and it takes 15-30min to see if your new mutation path is effective enough or not
- serious lack of depth to call this game a strategy game, especially when compared to the tenors of the genre
- UI represents infected humans by red dots on the world map ; very often, no red dot takes a plane or a boat from a country with the whole population already infected (and thus a red dot doesn't come back his country after a travel) ; it doesn't make any sense whatsoever with real life and other game rules ; it just means the red dots are fake and just funny things to show for the math formulas working in the background ; this is an immersion breaker for me
- the
mode requires to almost do nothing for 30 minutes to be beaten
- human gets infected and their immune system never clears the infectious agents
- so no human is immune to them
- pathogen agents mutate in a similar way in all hosts on player command ; IRL, the new mutation would form a new strain in 1 host (or a few ones if "lucky") and should propagate again
- The more money into the research, the faster it is (likely in a proportional way) ; AIDS research struggle shown it's not true

Have you ever fallen in love with a movie or a book only to be horrendously disappointed by its low quality sequel? Well if that concept were not already introduced to gaming, Magicka 2 more than fulfills the stereotype. I was looking forward to seeing what new and exciting improvements to one of my favorite games was released only to find an extremely dumbed down cash-grab sequel. Everything I loved about the original game was♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥all over or completely removed. Lets name a few of those things:
1.	No more combos- The experimentations and discovery of different combinations of magics is what got me hooked on this game in the first place. I couldn’t wait to see what new spell combinations awaited to be uncovered in Magicka 2. What were they? NOTHING! In fact, worse than nothing! The most devastatingly powerful spell combos of the previous game were not only rendered completely useless in this pathetic imitation of Magicka but the elimination of the ICE and STEAM elements cut in half the number of combinations available in the first game.  Ultimately you are stuck using the same 1 or 2 spells over and over and over and over.
2.	Spell Duration: Sofar the longest spell duration I have seen (haste, armor/immunity, spell walls, etc) only lasts a few seconds. You are constantly having to recast which makes you vulnerable to attacks which totally defeats the purpose of buffing up in the first place. Not even an aoe rock barrier is useful anymore.
3.	Protection:  Physical  armor (rock/ice armor) can be cut through like butter by even the weakest enemies, not to mention there is no weight value anymore (even though it slows you down a lot). You will find yourself constantly being hurled through the air or knocked on your♥♥♥♥♥by every bit of damage that comes your way.
4.	Weak offence: Status changing effects such as cold, burn and stun may as well have been completely removed from the game. No more lighting fires and running, no more cold spells to protect yourself, no more defensive barriers, no more fun in general.
5.	AOE spells have been reduced to almost melee range. Boulder takes 10 times as long to cast. Lightning doesn’t bounce worth crap anymore. Shield walls don’t do damage. Lets face it, you are stuck using beam attacks almost exclusively now, something I hated using before.
6.	Shield spell: OMG, just take the damn thing completely out of the game! Enemies walk through it like it isn’t even there. Shield have 1 purpose in Magicka 2 – to deflect beam attacks. Wow, that’s like, 1 enemy that you will ever use it against, and it isn’t even useful then since the cast size is super tiny and it only lasts 3 freakin seconds!

7.	Mouse controls have been completely scrambled! This wouldn’t be so bad if there were some interface options that allowed you to customize which buttons did what- which there isn’t. If this were a stand-alone game, that would be ok but since it is a sequel  you cant jump back and forth between each game without having to re-learn the controls.
8.	Dumbed-down big magicks: Hot keys? Really? REALLY? What differentiated the pros from the newbs of Magicka 1 is their ability to remember and speedily cast difficult big magick combos. Now just assign them to buttons 1-4 and press once. No skill required.

(There may be some spoilers ahead)
Pro's:
- It's free.
- It's quite long, for a VN (4hrs or so)
- Art is beautiful.
- Created by one very talented guy, whose work I would definitely consider picking up in future.
- Plot twists.
Cons:
- Apparently, there were a lot of references to things which I completely missed. Partly my fault, but I can't help but feel I'd have enjoyed the story more if I had.
- Story is, for the most part, a bit convoluted and has big gaps - especially at the end... the main one being the question as to where the hell did Claire go? How come everyone could see her, and talk to her, but then she just became a figment of his imagination?
- On that note, Claire looked about 5 years old. The artwork here was a bit disturbing.
- Characters were missing (Luce's father, the substitute teacher, Ciaran's family, and so on) which made it feel incomplete.
- I didn't like the main character. Personal opinion, but he was very, very irritating at times and at points I felt like turning it off, simply because of how much of an idiot he was.
- Some of the things that happen are completely unbelievable, and break the fourth wall.
- Some of these events were not just strange, but ridiculous. (Air gun fights, the policeman showing up 4 times, and so on)
- In line with the above, there's no way some of these things would have just randomly been allowed to happen.
Overall:
A good effort, and well worth the read (especially considering the price), but it is flawed - but I'm still recommending it, because it's interesting and, on the whole, very well written.
But, be warned. It's weird, and at times annoying, and the whole Claire situation is disturbing.

You're stuck with running in windowed mode.  Amusingly, and with a fertiliser truck worth of hubris, the developer describes the game as being "graphically intense".     This is particular relevant for Igob, the time travelling caveman from 12,832BC.   Should he travel forward in time with his trusty 486DX with onboard graphics, he may well pay attention to this warning, if he could read.   Igob will consult tree and stone.
I will say that despite the technical issues and limitations of the game, it's an original and educational premise which pleasantly draws the individual into the science of plant biology. Marvel Ultimate Alliance has had a rocky history on Steam. It was pulled a while back because of licensing only to recently reappear. Its relaunch alongside Ultimate Alliance 2 was not without its problems. These were documented by the likes of Jim Sterling and Totalbiscuit which included issues like unfunctioning menus that did nothing, audio issues, and controller issues.
Now I am pleased to say that it appears these issues have been resolved. During my time with the game I have not encountered any of these issues. The menus work and there are a number of resolution options as well as keybinding options for keyboards. I do recommend playing it with a controller. I use my WiiU controller and it works pretty well with a WiiU controller adapter set to Xinput.
The game itself is a bit like Diablo in that you assemble a group of heroes and traverse a variety of environments and locales pulled from the Marvel universe. Along the way you will earn currency and points that can be used to upgrade skills and abilities. In addition you can unlock a variety of costumes each with their own bonuses that can also be further augmented with points. There are also characters, comics and concept art to unlock as well. The game boasts a pretty extensive roster of heroes ranging from Spiderman, Cap, Wolverine, Deadpool, Dr. Doom, Thing, Spider Woman, Iron Man and more.
The story is a bit too silly for my tastes as you will deal with one threat only to have another crop up almost immediately. It suffers from a lot of plot contrivances but at the end of the day the game is still fun to play.
The voice acting is a bit of a mixed bag. Certain characters definitely sound better than others. Wolverine and a few characters definitely sound on point while others are a bit indistinguishable from others. Marvel Heroes 2016 certainly has the edge in terms of voice acting with the likes of David Hayter playing Winter Soldier, Nolan North voicing Deadpool and so on.
The elephant in the room is the price. I don't know if I can quite recommend this game at full price considering that Marvel Heroes 2016 is similar to this game and can be played for free. I would recommend this game to anyone who is a Marvel fan and has a bit of nostalgia for the game. The game is certainly in a better state now than what it was. I would advise waiting for a sale though and getting both this and Ultimate Alliance 2 for $30 as opposed to paying $40 each or $60 for both regularly.

TLDR:  I've put a lot of time and effort into this game (300+ hours); Also a good bit of cash, which I am now regretting.  I'm getting fed up with games that promise to deliver content and expand upon it in a timely manner only to have the companies renege and disappoint entire communities. When dealing with the support for this game, it feels like an after thought;  Like they aren't taking it seriously and have no communication with one another.  The web page itself feels like a slapped together wordpress blog with a free forum board strapped to it with ductape;  It's insulting. ((I'm a web desinger/developer.  I notice that stuff.)) There isn't enough content to keep most hard core players interested.  Wide spread bans, lagging, exploits and bot issues are another huge turn off.  What the game promised through game play in the begining, it failed miserably to deliver at the end.
-------------------------------------
I can't justify continuing to play.  I'm not even as geared as I could be but I honestly can't bring myself to follow through grinding out runes from AD and dust for talismans as there is no content to aim for coming out in the immediate future.  So what am I supposed to do?  Spend the next month grinding the same dungeons over and over again for gear and stats I'll replace when the new content arrives?  Am I supposed to enjoy the ever shrinking population of pvpers?  I feel like the new daily gifts are a 'please stick around' consolation prize for all the banning, lagging, exploits and bots.
The lag issues that effected the entire NA Asperon server where horrendous.  When support was contacted, despite this being a SERVER WIDE ISSUE, the players were blamed.  *sarcasm*  Of course!  Thousands of players all having lag issues --all at the same time-- must be a software issue; something in our startup.  Obvious.
And then there was the exploit that they released with the game that they KNEW was there since alpha essentially allowing players the opportunity to screw up the leveling curve, the economy and the community when the exploiters where finally banned... after two weeks.  I know two weeks doesn't sound like an awful lot to some, but to others that first two weeks in the game is when you set your pace.  The first two weeks is when you find your companions/friends.  Those first two weeks after release, pretty damn important to someone who wants to push content.
I love the community in this game; Amazing people - I've made some great friends that I really hope to cary on gaming with.  And the game play itself is amazing -- There's just not enough of it to keep hard core MMO players occupied.  Overwhelming at the beginning, but you can knock it all out with effort and time.  Maybe I chew up content too quickly, but I don't feel like there is enough.  When the new stuff comes out, will I devour it just as quickly and be bored again?  I feel like that will definitely be the case.

Is over 70 hours enough to give an opinion on this game? Well I have a lot of problems with this game and it's mostly just the class diversification.
Let's just say it up straight right here. If this review isn't convincing enough for you to avoid this game then please for the love of god just play the Evokers and/or Cannoneer class. There is little reason to play the other classes, whatever they may be at the time you read this review. Reason being is that right now not only are they dominating in both pve and pvp, they are the most dominant (in numbers) class in this game. Everywhere you go there will be evokers and cannoneers. Very RARELY will you see a berserker or shadowhunter... because those classes are just complete @SS.
Here's just a small example as to what I'm talking about:
That is an example of a pvp game. The pvp matchup is random but how can it be this bad? In fact this happens more often than you think. So what's wrong with that? First, level 52 is the max level in this game, but how can there be more 52s on the other side than my side. Second, the other side is FILLED with evokers and cannoneers while my side is a bit diversed, but not saying much.
To top it off with tbagging the berserker, the pvp game is almost ending, our side trailing behind by almost 1000 points; that list of players is sorted by players with the most points at the top and lowest at the bottom. Surprise surprise, the berserker on the other side is at the bottom... ANNDDDD he's level 52, the max level. Seven assists means he tried his best in battle but couldn't quite get the kill.
So what's the point of berserkers? Nothing, they are useless and so are shadowhunters.
All in all, just stick with evokers and cannonners. Why is this happening? Because every class is pretty much the same, just that ranged characters get the HUGE upper hand of dealing the SAME EXACT damage as a melee character but has more crowd control and range. If their ranged ulimate skill has the same exact cooldown and skill damage as a melee character then what is a point of a melee character? Tank? Surely nope because as you play harder dungeons, going melee is absolutely NOT RECOMMENDED because you die in one or two hits.

For those of you that are just starting for flight simulators this is not nesseciarily a plug-and-play game. It's hard, very hard. But it is the most rewarding simulator that I've played to date. I personally am not a pilot but have flown VFR on small planes in real life before and this game really does bring back those memories of me being in the air!
If you are looking for something that you have to really buckle down and learn about, this is the software for you!

First, this is not a game it is a simulator.  Compared to FSX it has better flight dynamics.  I have over 10,000 hours in several multi-engine jet aircraft and it has the feel and reaction of the real thing.  FSX feels like driving a bus  compared to x-plane.  ATC is better in FSX and is okay for a simulator.  X-plane ATC is so bad I never use it.  I plan my routes to include descent and setting myself up for an approach without ATC because it is just unusable and doesn't even come close to the real thing.
Scenery in x-plane is better for atmospheric conditions and the out of the box terrain is comparable to FSX out of the box.  FSX does have better add-on scenery available.  X-plane surpasses FSX on the actual runway.   X-plane runways follow the terrain and are very realistic.  FSX has better stock aircraft than x-plane so plan on adding a payware aircraft unless general aviation is your thing.
If checklist are your thing, FSX add-on aircraft like PMDG 737NGX are probably better than many x-plane add-on aircraft from a switchology standpoint.  I have the PMDG 737NGX for FSX and the FJS 737-200 for x-plane.  Systems functionality is more realistic with the high end FSX add-ons, but x-plane add-ons are comparable and generally cheaper.  Cockpit graphics are better in FSX, but x-plane is catching up.  Weather conditions more accurately affect the aircraft in x-plane.  Try a 30 knot crosswing landing in FSX and x-plane and there is a noticable difference with x-plane being very realistic.
It all depends on the desires of each simer.  If you are really into checklist procedures and in depth systems operations then get FSX and pay for a high end add-on like a PMDG aircraft.  If flight dynamics and a very realistic feel to the aircraft  that is close to the real deal then get x-plane.  I prefer x-plane and if it had a decent ATC I would probably uninstall FSX and exclusively go with x-plane.  I split time between the 2 right now.  Hope this helps anyone trying to make a decision.

Bad Company 2 is a first person shooter game created by DICE and published by EA in 2010. The game features both a team-based multiplayer mode and a singleplayer campaign. The singleplayer campaign has you playing as Marlowe, a member of an elite American special ops team. You start the game,however playing as Thomas Wyatt, coincidentally also a member of a U.S special ops team,though this time you play back in the WWII era instead of in the future. You start out going on a secret mission to meet up with a Japanese Scientist who wants to defect and claims to have valuable information on a new super weapon. Things quickly go to hell and your entire team is wiped out after the Japanese discover you and proceed to make you bear witness to the test firing of the weapon,killing you and your team.

You begin the real campaign after that and you start playing as Marlowe,though the campaign is in a futuristic setting now instead of the bleak hell of WWII. The campaign features 13 full levels with each one ranging from 10-20ish minutes to complete,with some more long or difficult missions being around 30-40 minutes at most. For the most part the missions are all quite linear,although they give you open fighting grounds to fill with corpses as you make your way to the objectives.If you came to Bad Co. 2 for a story that would blow your socks off you will be suprisingly (or maybe not suprisingly,depending on how you feel about Battlefield) dissappointed. The story isn't poorly made nor is it poorly done at all really. Problems arise when you have a story that is incredibly average and is only being held up by the unparalleled gunplay. When you get into the thick of fighting it's easy to get lost in the heavy smoke of the fresh gunpowder and the whump of your rifle as you mow down entire squads in your quest to save America from Soviet invasion.

The campaign may not be anything special but i'll be damned if this isn't one of the most fun MP modes I have played in quite a while. The destructibility is astoundingly fun to play with and actually has some serious strategic value. Enemy sniper hiding behind a window? 40MM Grenade launcher solves that real quick. Enemy soldiers crossing a bridge into your base? Blow that bridge to hell and back! Being able to just destroy pretty much anything at anytime you want is an incredible idea in both the campaign and the multiplayer. The multiplayer itself consists of 5 different game modes each with varying degrees of difficulty. The first one is Conquest,a mode where each team has a set amount of tickets,dying will of course drop this ticket total by 1 per death,and the goal is to drain the other teams tickets before they drain yours. There are also multiple flags you can hold that will give you a constant ticket drain if you hold the majority. Other than that you just need to kill them faster than they can kill you.The next mode is Rush,a gamemode where you have two teams,attackers and defenders each trying to attack or defend multiple M-COM stations respectively. Attackers are tasked with setting C4 charges on the stations then defending them until they explode. Defenders,of course are charged with defending the stations until they finally bring the attackers' ticket count to zero.After that you have Team Deathmatch which,if you have ever played a multiplayer FPS before, just consists two teams each trying to end the game with the most kills. Next you have squad rush which is just normal rush but with no vehicles,smaller maps,and a max of eight players.Finally there's onslaught,a co-op DLC mode where you try to play against AI and capture flags. Vehicles spawn at certain points and there are multiple levels of difficulty to fight against. Generally all the MP modes seem fairly balanced and there were no glaring problems with the mode that I noticed during regular play. The matchmaking system is completely broken and will either not find you a match,even though plenty are available,or it will put you in a match with just yourself; so make sure you just use server browser.The Multiplayer is what you really would be buying this game for as the campaign was pretty much overlooked due to more people wanting MP than SP.
An excellent game for the price. Astoundingly well done MP component with an overwhelmingly average SP campaign. Solid gunplay and unparalled destructability make this a game you wont want to miss.

Three native french people made this game and the writing is very naive euro-engrish (franglais?), but this only adds to the game's weird, graffiti-plastered charm. The story is the typical anti-establishment allegory; a plucky gangy of expressive urban youths vs. the fascist anti-fun regime, and this is written with about as much subtlety as you'd expect.
It's still quite charming though, largely due to the cartoonish, comedic nature of the character interactions and expositional codex entries, which help keep things feeling irreverent and laidback, and suit the game's oddly slapstick hip-hop/rave aesthetic. Sort of like Jet Set Radio meets The Fifth Element.
Some missions may involve grabbing a box with a city-dweller's pet inside and taking it on a high-velocity walk, whilst another had me carrying expired boxes of sushi to nearby waste bins dotted around the neon highrises. The variety is good, and they get a lot of mileage out of the base mechanics of running, jumping and grinding (in addition to carrying and throwing objects, such as in the sports-influenced GameBall matches).
These are all playable in multiplayer, although currently the missions are all advesarial, with only the first player to finish being awarded a medal/completion credit, progressing cooperatively is apparently still something being worked on by the devs.
Exploring together while searching for the multitude of hidden collectibles or completing open-world tasks (such as breaking through signs at high speed or covering propaganda posters with graffiti) is still a lot of fun in a group, but completing the mainline story, for now at least, seems to be more of a singleplayer affair.
I definitely recommend Hover, especially if you're a fan of the various influences that it wears on its neon pink fishnet sleeve. It's also just a great fit for anyone that enjoys bright colours and the thrill of jumping around amidst them.

If you like parkour and open world game, this is a pretty good mix.  There's collectables around the map to well collect, and there are also missions of various types. If this sounds appealing, it's great value for money.

TL;DR This game is very bare bones and needs a lot of work, and I don't recommend it.
First, I would like to note that the developer seems to be working to improve the game. The last update/improvement announcement was 3 months prior to this review. I want to commend the developer for putting the effort into making and keeping up with their game.
Into the issues I faced playing this game:
1) The first thing I noticed was the load times and loading screens. The first load entering the game was several minutes long. Not much of a problem in itself, however, the loading screen is mostly blank with little design to it. Without something to look at while it performed its extended load, I was about ready to go do something else while it finished.
2) When the game had loaded, I began to move over to the slingshot and ammo table when I got a notification in the game: "Low FPS Detected. Would you like to improve performance?" I wasn't expecting any graphical options in a game of this scale, so I agreed to improve performance. Which would have been nice if it hadn't made the performance worse. Going through the pause menu and setting the graphics to low alleviated some of the fps issues to a more tolerable level(my PC isn't magnificient, but it should be able to run this game with no problem).
3) I'm going to lump combat and gameplay together for this point. Your heartbeat meter is out of 100, but I was able to get it over 600 by avoiding as much damage as possible and grabbing every health item I saw. I'm not sure if this is an intended mechanic or not. The AI is quite lacking. The enemies stay outside the buildings and shoot you through the windows whenever they have visual. I noticed that when I would move the enemies would square dance back and forth outside the window until they decided they wanted to shoot me, or I got too close to a wall where they would literally kick my♥♥♥♥♥through said wall. Your fire rate is much slower than the enemies' fire rate. Even their shotguns fire like rifles. I timed 2 shots from the sling, and it was about 4 seconds from the first click to the time the second shot left the sling. In that 4 seconds, I could be shot 6+ times from a single enemy which is about 20 damage per hit. A headshot to most enemies was a kill, but the aiming and delay of your shot(plus the urge to avoid incoming shots and the enemies' affinity to squre dance outside the windows) makes it hard to line up a headshot. I found the best course of action was to shoot the enemy body parts that clipped through the wall as they waited on either side of a window for you to poke your head out. Getting too close to spiders on the walls will damage you. The game overs don't seem to make sense unless I was missing something. Sometimes when I died, it would just restart me back at the original spawn location, and I would resume like nothing happened except that any of the items I collected were gone and the enemies I had killed were still dead. Then other times I would die, get sent back to the main menu, and have to restart at the same spawn location, but this time everything had reset.
4) This is the final point I wil make. The overall cohesion of the game is strange. If you speak to the women in the levels, it seems no one really knows why you're there and why the military has KoS order on you. The start building seems to be a basic fps setup. However, the second building had two jumpscares. One being a monster reminiscent of a Resident Evil type of monster. The second simply being a doctor who appears when you open a certain door and just stands there menacingy. The real scary part about the doctor was that I didn't kill him immediately and entered the room to collect the items and when I started getting shot, he was blocing the exit, and I ended up dying.
stfu and take my money .

Although i wanted to wait for the new patch that got announced by the devs to write this review, I might aswell just do that now. So let´s break this game down into pros & cons.
PROS:
- Let´s start with the obvious. Devilian is F2P so initially you dont have to buy anything.
- You can buy an item called "Dex" for ingame currency and use it to buy things on the real money shop.
- Performance is suprisingly good. I don´t have any problems running the game with my old pc.
- You can get pretty quick to max level. Quests are pretty straight forward.
- MANY different dungeons that´ll enhance your leveling experience.
- There´s a paragon system. Just like the one in diablo 3.
- Devilian Mode(= special transformation with new abilities). Also able to level your devilian form.
- Up to 15 daily quests and you can select those you prefer.
- Guild bonuses can be unlocked. Such as salvage, Resurrection and merchant discount.
- Adding friends offers daily bonuses aswell. (e. g. health potions, gems)
- Current Endcontent boss is decent (difficulty wise).
- You can either enter the looking for group tool or manually get one together. (Dungeon/Raid/PVP)
- You can socket your gear with so called artifacts and upgrade them separately.
- There´s a Challenge tower in which you have to progress through waves of monsters and try to get as high as possible. Probably compareable to greater rifts (diablo 3)  in some way.
- Your character is customizable with wings, costumes etc.
CONS:
- Well to get a verified account you have to spend 5$ in any Trion game. Without a verified account you´re not able to sell items on the auction house, whisper to people that are not on your friendslist, use the global chat, initiate trades with other players, send letters and request marketplace items from strangers. Considering in any other game you can get verified via e-mail validation, this is just an obvious way for Trion to make money.
- Only 4 playable classes at the moment.
- Classes are gender locked.
- Balance is simply non-existent. E. g. the berserker class is pretty decent in dungeons and raids, but if you want to play pvp you´re just getting destroyed.
- Ranged classes can shoot through walls in the pvp arena.
- If you can crowd control your enemy first, you´re most likely to win the fight. They need to reduce cc time.
- PVP queues for 20v20 can take up to 30 min. or longer.
- Even 3v3 queues can take up to 10min.
- No open world pvp.
- Limited bag space. Only extendable with real money or DEX.
- 10 sec. + loading screens.
- Server lags are happening multiple times a day.
- There´s some kind of pay to win. For example getting an artifact above +7 without spending real money is kinda impossible.
- You HAVE TO play pve/pvp and do quests to complete daily challenges.
- Large guilds that invested some money into the game can take over areas and control the boss spawns. So it may happen that you´re not even able to get those rewards. There should be separate boss spawns outside of those areas.
- Lack of End-Game content
- To complete your first endgame set could take very long time. The 2nd one didn´t take that long.
- At the moment it is hard to get started and find groups outside of your guild. Because everyone is just selling boosts for ingame currency.
To say the least, i would recommend the game. But would I really recommend investing tons of hours into the game ?
No, not at the moment.

Nazi Zombie Army is a fun game. You team up with 3 people and you start shooting Nazi zombie soldiers throughout the 5 chapters the game offers. As opposed to "regular" zombie games this one explains zombies by the good-old occultism background that gives the game a more creepy atmosphere: zombies have glowing eyes and the demonic laughter they occasionally produce can give everybody the creeps.
Eliminating these otherworldly creatures with precision aiming is very exciting - wind is not taken into account as was in the original Sniper Elite games; this is as casual as it can get. Also, I liked how the developers tried to make this game authentic - objects and places feel realistic and you can really feel being part of an apocalyptic WW II era.
And here comes the bad part: Finding players online is extremely difficult. I read many forums and I know there is a relatively big community and really wants to keep playing this game. I also had the chance of playing with 3 people several times only to find myself disconnected once a chapter ended. Some of these were friends on Steam and while chatting with them they confirmed having being disconnected. Playing the game alone is simply too difficult and boring - also, some achievements can only be attained in cooperative gameplay.
If you want to play this game badly I suggest not only to wait for a big discount but also to gather at least 3 friends who want to desperately play it. With the 4 of you playing it together you can manage to have fun throughout but even with friends you'll experience disconnection several times.
In addition to this the game also has a handful of bugs and glitches. I find it difficult to recommend a game that is marred by so many issues.
