Shantae and the Pirate's Curse is a very good game with lots of interesting elements.
Shantae and the Pirate's Curse is basiclly an action platformer that somehow feel like a fusion betwen megaman and metroid (more megaman than metroid). I'll start with, an odd point : the controls. The first time I have controlled shantae, something was odd, I felt like I couldn't control the caracter properly and I always took hits that I would have normally dodged. I felt this for, like 1 hour then the controls were perfect for me. So that's why I first thought that the controls were bad and I almost gave up, but in the end, it's just that you really need your time to adapt yourself I think (or maybe I was just stup). So the controls aren't bad. After that let's talk about the difficulty and the levels : It's very well done. In the middle of each island, you will obtain a new equipment item which grant you a new movement skill that will help you to move forward, and the level disign is perfectly done to use these item and make each equipments usefull. I have made a first impression with visuals on my channel:
-The game suffers from its mobile version.
Its UI is barely improved upon and still has redundant buttons for the mobile version.
Tooltips are not present anywhere in the game and leaves the player clueless as to what certain upgrades or attacks do.
-The player is given little time in battles.
The time bar makes sense for the drawing of spells because the quicker you draw, the more damage you do, but keeps running the entirety of the battle.
In short the game pushes players in making hasty decisions which prevents players from applying strategy in battle.
-Unit placement is almost completely useless as you will always be limited to 3 moveable characters per at the very most.
Recruiting more units of a single type stacks them, but it would make a lot more sense if units were placed seperately so you could actually block off attacks aimed at ranged units with melee units for instance.
-There's a serious lack of combat modifiers and/or lack of visibility. As far as I can tell all units have the same effectiveness against each other unit. Enemy units that are stationed near fences appear to get a bonus against ranged attacks regardless of their position towards the archer. Let's say an enemy's flanks are exposed and you were to use your archers, you would still do little damage as they're considered protected by adjacent fences.
TL;DR
The game suffers from Mobile platform's limitations and is barely suited to PC.
Again the game is fun and I quite like the magic system even though it could use more depth. It would be great if you could practice spells whilst not in battle. The game has its merits but as long as these issues are not addressed I couldn't in good conscience recommend this game. An added option of saving the game and having save games wouldn't be to shavy either.

Please note this is an early access game and I bought it heavily discounted, neither I've looked at the dev page to see which features will be available in future, so this is just my first impression after finishing the first scenario.
- There is no map, no introduction to the story and the basic tutorial gives too few hints
- The game so far is really linear, but could improve later. Basically is like an HOMM game where you buy units, explore, collect gold, kill enemies and repeat the cycle. But at the moment there is no loot system, so you always find only gold. Also it seems you are stuck with a certain type of units (3) and can't recruit / find different units, but this could be just at the beginning and heroes could change later in the game.
- The camera is fixed, I don't really see the purpose. In certain situations will move in a completely different angle while you are walking making you lose where you were going (add on top of this that there is no map)
The good sides:
- The spell system is the thing that distinguishes this game from the others. You have to draw the lines on your screen and then select the enemies. Faster you are, stronger is the spell. If you don't remember a spell sign, you can always select it from the spellbook but this will make it less powerful. I did not really notice so much difference, but probably with stronger spells and more balanced game in future this will be more noticeable.
- It's really simple and for this price the final edition of the game can fill the void while waiting for your next favourite AAA game

This game succeds at what it does. It combines 2 fan favorites over the years, and mashes it up into a wonderful mix of Parkour and cyberpunk.
This game takes elements from Mirror's Edge and Jet Set Radio and puts it all together in one game. The basic premise of this game is that video games are banned in the city, and you and a rag-tag group of people are working together to bring video games back, and overpower the law. The story isn't really a big part of the game, the biggest part is finding different ways to complete the misssions you are given. The main mechanic of the game is being able to parkour and rewind. You are able to climb on buildings, do super jumps if timed right, and more. If you mess up while doing these actions, you can hold your rewind key and go back to the point you want to restart at.
The missions in the game as of now are pretty basic. Some examples;
-Get from point A to point B in a certain time frame.
-Run past security cameras while holding something
Etc Etc
I've attempted 3 missions so far (all I could find) and I've completed 3 of them.
You can customize your own player and take it online or offline. You then proceed to level up to a max level of 10. At random intervals, you gain skill points in which you can put towards your skill tree. In your skill tree, you can level up Jump, Speed, Acceleration, and more.
The online play is pretty solid. So far, i've seen 1 official server. Online is the same thing as offline. You can still complete missions and all, just doing it being online. The biggest server i've seen is 64 slots. The only problem that online has is that it drops your FPS a bit during play.
Keep in mind that this game is still in very early alpha.
The performance of the game could be better, but devs have acknowledged this and are working to get it better.
*Verdict*
I love the main premise and idea of this game. The game is in very early alpha, so there isnt much content. But running around and smoothly finding ways to keep your streak going is fun in itself. The little missions that are already in the game are cool because it shows what potential it has to be implemented into different missions or even online races. I like this game for what it is. 20 bucks to me is a bit overpriced at the moment, I think 10-15 would've been a suitable price.
8/10
-1 for overpricing
-1 for unoptimization.
I do recommend this game.

I'd say this game is quite underrated and even underpriced. It's a pretty standard formula of action adventure games akin to the likes of Darksiders, God of War, and Devil May Cry, and it might do everything that's been done before, but it does so very well and manages to stay fun throughout.
The gameplay is nicely balanced between combat sections, platforming, puzzles, and mini-games. You're never doing the same thing for too long, which keeps the experience fresh and entertaining. As you progress through the game, your weapon acquires different forms (scythe, twin daggers, whip, and hammer), which are useful in different situations and you can switch between them at any time. In addition you also learn some very powerful spells which are good at clearing out large crowds of enemies.
Overall the difficulty I felt was balanced perfectly. There were no unexpected difficulty spikes and most of it was a smooth ride. In the last quarter of the game it gets a bit challenging, but it does so gradually and reasonably. Only one section involving a certain collapsing underground bridge felt a bit cheap since it gave me a lot of insta-deaths, but that section was pretty short.
I really enjoyed most of the mini-games, such as the first-person shooting sections where you have to mount a turret and shoot down helicopters, or even flying one yourself, or sliding down the cliffs and dodging obstacles. No overcomplicated mechanics. Just simple and fun mini-games to give you a small break from fighting and platforming.
The plot is somewhat cheesy and lighthearted, but the main character is quite likeable, and his frequent dialogue exchanges with his sidekick, the Mask of Death, are all very funny. The length was also quite spot on for a game like this. Took me about 10 hours to beat it on Normal.
My only serious critique for this game would be the occasional crashes to desktop that I got (and it seems there are some other people who get them too). It wasn't too bad, since the game has very frequent checkpoints, so you don't lose a lot of progress, but it's still a bug.
I'd say if you enjoy action adventure games and seek something to give you heaps of entertainment, then I'd highly recommend this game. I got it for merely £4 (~$6), which is its full price on Steam and enjoyed it way more than some games which I bought for a higher price.

I like to call it. . . Cracktorio . . .
[Early Access Review Nov. 11 / 17]
I highly suggest this game to those with OCD tendancies, those that don't mind simple math, enjoy puzzles, and not looking for an in-depth storyline.  This game is as the name and description states; you build factories in order to achieve the end-game goal, which is quite simply:
Launch a rocket into space.
Sounds easy right? WELL YOU MIGHT WANT TO RETHINK THAT! In my first experience the fun really began when I wanted red circuits; well to do that, you need oil.  Build pump jacks to pump out crude oil. Then you need to refine that oil; well now hook up the basic oil refinement process to acheive a 3:3:4 Light, Heavy, and Petroleum output, which will then need to be fed into a chemical plant that can refine the petroleum gases into meldable plastics.  Finally that plastic can now be combined in an assembler with green circuits, copper wire, and said plastic.  Then the first problem occurs, in order to keep pumping petroleum you need to find a use for the light and heavy oil by-products. Otherwise your storage containers will be unable to pump in more petro because there is no where for the oils to go.  Thats plastic for ya. Which overall wasn't that bad. . . especially compared to the nuclear option.
The beauty of this game is the fact that it always gives you something to do.  Theres never a time where you're waiting for something to finish because there is always a problem to solve, minerals to refine, resources to move, and factories to build.  In my first 3 days after purchase I managed to rack up 44 hours of gameplay time.
PROS:
- Highly Optimized, with low recommended specs. And a puny file size. (Less than a Gb)
- Never encountered any major bugs or glitches.
- Active and openly discussive developers
- Intuitive & powerful GUI; simple, elegant, and very useful.
- Brilliantly executed hotkeys, and multikey functions.  I can run, move inventory, and craft items virtually all simultaneously.
CONS:
- VERY ADDICTING; I highly advise lining up the purchase of this game with a weekend as it can easily consume your mind into solving the infinite amount of puzzles the game provides.
- Math-Oriented. Especially with Ratios, learn your ratios!
- No Train Horn (in Vanilla anyways).
- Fluid Wagon attachment (to pumps) is very finicky.
Bottom Line:
I highly recommend this game if you have the patience, time, and motivaton to work with puzzles in a Real-Time sense.  If you enjoyed playing any RTS or Sandbox game then this game will likely appeal to you.
If you want an in-depth story, cut-scenes, and current gen graphics, fast-paced shooter, or RPG.  I would not recommend this game.
Similar Games:
(please note these might be pretty vague similarities, but overall there is some feature or style that is similar)
Minecraft - (circuits, logic gates, & mechanical engineering)
Space Engineers - (creative freedom, sandbox-style building mechanics w/ mining, refinement, and production)
Age of Empires - (mostly graphically.  Although resource management is quite similar)
Cities: Skylines - (power, fluids, pollution, and math-involved)

If you haven’t played anything in the Sniper Elite series, what sets them apart from other run-and-gun shooters is the emphasis on over-the-top sniper shots with x-ray cams. The kills feel incredibly satisfying and the reliance on accuracy pushes one to enhance their skill and experiment with the weaponry to find the best player method. What is NOT here is the stealth element of the previous games, nor is it missed.
If you’ve played other zombie games, like Killing Floor or Left 4 Dead, this series emphasizes limited weapon selection, each with different strengths and weaknesses. It also emphasizes slow shambling zombies over fast-moving ones. The mood is set very well in this game, as it does a good job of providing a feel of a destroyed hellish zombie-infested landscape. It is sufficiently creepy, particularly because you know that survival depends on seeing them first and getting a good distance between you and them. As they shamble closer, accuracy matters more making it harder to pull off shots when it matters most, complimenting the major strengths of this game.
No doubt, you’ve read some criticism of this game. Some of the most prominent criticisms are condensed as follows:
Cheap and unambitious.
Monotonous and repetitive gameplay.
Cashgrab.
Unoriginal.
No plot.
While some of these are accurate to a degree, the reality is that even if they *are* true, it shouldn’t scare you away from this title. It is very fun with four people. I could go by each and refute them point by point, but most of these concerns can be alleviated by two counterpoints.
First, this game *is* cheap. The game is $15.00. The average movie ticket is between $7.84 and $8.38 (as of November 2013). At 1 Hour and 30 minutes as the average length of a film, if you get even three hours of enjoyment out of the game, you’ve already gotten more out of it than your average movie (and you can bring your own snacks and be as loud as you like.) It’s not meant to be some gaming magnum opus, and many Triple A releases try too hard to do this, and fail miserably. This is what you might call a “niche market” game… its aimed at a small segment of the gaming community for a modest profit. This is not a bad thing nor is it any more a cashgrab than any other game produced. While it is not for everyone (nor is it meant to be), it is worth the price of admission.
Second, as far as repetitive gameplay, yes it does have this. Every game is repetitive within certain respects, and the lack of a compelling plot or original gameplay elements makes this title’s repetitive nature relatively obvious. You *can* turn off the x-ray mode if it becomes overwhelming (or reduce its frequency) and the repetitive aspects are alleviated if you play with friends. The solo game mode is best enjoyed in small chunks. The shotguns function as shotguns, the sniper rifles function as sniper rifles, and pistols function as pistols. If you get tired of mowing down zombies with these methods, there are relatively few shooter games that will overcome this limitation. However, one should not expect too much innovation from a shooter game. There are precious few shooters that are innovative with regard to combat mechanics, or they’re successful at dressing up this shortcoming by using non-shooter elements. Much like the title implies, what you see is what you get… and what you get is pretty reasonable and fun in the right mindset.

What a GREAT game!  This is a fantastic Co-op game for 4 players (3rd person top down view).
AND IT'S FREE!!!
There are 4 different classes, each with 2 variations of specialists to choose from.   Each soldier can carry 3 items.  Guns galore: flame throwers, machine guns with grenade launchers, tesla turrets, damage boosts and a TON of other items and weapons are at your disposal.
Each specialist has their own jobs to do: Medic, Tech, Weapon Specalist, and Officer.  You NEED to work as a team to pass through the missions alive.  The swarm is relentles...
The one and only problem with the game is the lack of levels.  You only get one campaign with the game, and it's 5 missions long (I believe) and can probably be finished in a few hours with a good team..   BUT...  Look around online and you will find user created map packs to continue the fun!  This game is not so much about story as it is about teamwork.  All you need are more maps to run.  My team has found 54 campaings (and many more are out there) most with multiple maps per campaign.
Many small details make this game a pleasure to play.  Easy to understand, variety of equipment that unlocks as you level up, being able to draw on the mission map to plan out things (and laugh hard as we draw rude things...), ability to reconnect while mission is running if dc'd, laser sights so you know where your teammates are covering, easy multiplay connection, etc.
Probably not a single player game, though you can run the missions yourself (and die horribly) for practice.  But if you have a few players that want to do something co-op, it's free and fun.

A fire burns in the distance. With the sun having long since disappeared below the horizon and endless acres of forest warding off the artificial light of civilization, its flames flood the night sky with incandescent hues. It's a natural brush fire, unlikely to do much harm, so for now I rest my elbows on the railing that surrounds my lookout tower and admire the view. A nearby transceiver crackles to life. It's Delilah, radioing from her own tower several miles away. She comments on the fire, how beautiful it looks, how it's all smoke and ash during the day but utterly resplendent under the cover of darkness. And it is. But over time, the fire spreads, and as its intensity escalates, so too does the tension of the narrative.

It used to be only Madagascar that would be the problem country, the one that would close down shipping and borders if anyone so much as had an eyebrow twitch.  Now, it's a world of hurt for you or humanity depending on what difficulty you've chosen to test fate.  The prototype for this game was called "Epidemic 2" and I played it on
and
long ago.  It was a lot more primitive back then and to have it brought up to modern standards with better soundtrack was certainly a treat.  I also loved all the scenarios and what ifs that were built-in by the creator.  This game is great for the inner sadist in you.  Ever wanted to destroy humanity?  Well, here you go!  You can wipe them out with various disease types, or go for the throat with your very own zombie apocalypse that YOU unleash on the world.  They've even got the Planet of the Apes option where you can turn an experimental treatment into a world of simians who destroy labs and bases while humanity dies from whatever symptoms you've chosen.
I like using dysentary, myself.  Dysentary with sneezing, diarrhea, and total organ failure is probably the most brutal way to die if you're a human.
It's well worth the price and you'll find yourself playing it again and again just to win or try other ideas.  One of the most interesting is the Worm infection wherein you don't even have to kill humanity.  You can make them into slaves and win the game by infected everyone to become a worshipper.  Pretty neat spin there and the Christmas scenario has you save humanity with the Worm, bringing everyone back to having emotions after being oppressed and suppressed to drone-like states by the world governments.
Very fun, very worthwhile, check it out.  You won't be disappointed if you like viral apocalypse scenarios.  With tons of achievements and hidden challenges, it's very worth the price and the time you spend playing it.

Oh and 10/10 would name my plague "Tumblr" or "yo mama" again.

Before you write it off though, the second game (and it's special edition) has choices out the butt, so I still say you should buy this as more of an appetizer to enjoy before the main dish of the second game.
One other-other thing. They explain why their boobs get big. Yeah, I was not expecting that at all, but it's actually fascinating as f*ck that they didn't just write it off as "Time stuff", they brought up actual, real-life biology and body chemistry and scientific junk. Props to the writers.
I'm going to be honest with you. I'm not so prudent or ashamed that I won't say the reason I originally bought this game was because, y'know, boobs. I'm a guy, so sue me. What I didn't expect, and what i'm sure you wouldn't have expected either, was the fact that this game actually had a LOT, and I mean a LOT of thought put into it. Sure the first thing that drew me in was the sex appeal, but what made me stick around was the fact that the characters had a certain degree of depth, they may have served as a visual selling point, but they proved to be well-written enough that they became characters that you grow attached to and feel the same concern for that the protagonist does.

I like to call it. . . Cracktorio . . .
[Early Access Review Nov. 11 / 17]
I highly suggest this game to those with OCD tendancies, those that don't mind simple math, enjoy puzzles, and not looking for an in-depth storyline.  This game is as the name and description states; you build factories in order to achieve the end-game goal, which is quite simply:
Launch a rocket into space.
Sounds easy right? WELL YOU MIGHT WANT TO RETHINK THAT! In my first experience the fun really began when I wanted red circuits; well to do that, you need oil.  Build pump jacks to pump out crude oil. Then you need to refine that oil; well now hook up the basic oil refinement process to acheive a 3:3:4 Light, Heavy, and Petroleum output, which will then need to be fed into a chemical plant that can refine the petroleum gases into meldable plastics.  Finally that plastic can now be combined in an assembler with green circuits, copper wire, and said plastic.  Then the first problem occurs, in order to keep pumping petroleum you need to find a use for the light and heavy oil by-products. Otherwise your storage containers will be unable to pump in more petro because there is no where for the oils to go.  Thats plastic for ya. Which overall wasn't that bad. . . especially compared to the nuclear option.
The beauty of this game is the fact that it always gives you something to do.  Theres never a time where you're waiting for something to finish because there is always a problem to solve, minerals to refine, resources to move, and factories to build.  In my first 3 days after purchase I managed to rack up 44 hours of gameplay time.
PROS:
- Highly Optimized, with low recommended specs. And a puny file size. (Less than a Gb)
- Never encountered any major bugs or glitches.
- Active and openly discussive developers
- Intuitive & powerful GUI; simple, elegant, and very useful.
- Brilliantly executed hotkeys, and multikey functions.  I can run, move inventory, and craft items virtually all simultaneously.
CONS:
- VERY ADDICTING; I highly advise lining up the purchase of this game with a weekend as it can easily consume your mind into solving the infinite amount of puzzles the game provides.
- Math-Oriented. Especially with Ratios, learn your ratios!
- No Train Horn (in Vanilla anyways).
- Fluid Wagon attachment (to pumps) is very finicky.
Bottom Line:
I highly recommend this game if you have the patience, time, and motivaton to work with puzzles in a Real-Time sense.  If you enjoyed playing any RTS or Sandbox game then this game will likely appeal to you.
If you want an in-depth story, cut-scenes, and current gen graphics, fast-paced shooter, or RPG.  I would not recommend this game.
Similar Games:
(please note these might be pretty vague similarities, but overall there is some feature or style that is similar)
Minecraft - (circuits, logic gates, & mechanical engineering)
Space Engineers - (creative freedom, sandbox-style building mechanics w/ mining, refinement, and production)
Age of Empires - (mostly graphically.  Although resource management is quite similar)
Cities: Skylines - (power, fluids, pollution, and math-involved)

"Sniper Elite: Nazi Zombie Army was everything I loved about Sniper Elite V2, with an amazingly well-crafted zombie atmosphere. No other zombie game has managed to replicate the dread and imminent doom of the Romero-style zombie"
I've never been good at stealth games. I've also never been good at driving games - blame it on my Asian heritage.
When I played the original Sniper Elite V2, I loved the World War 2 setting, as well as the simulated realism of Sniper Physics -- distance to target, bullet drop, wind, holding your breath to steady your shots. I detested the stealthing segments, throwing rocks and scurrying about. I would try the stealth approach 3-4 times, give up in frustration, and go very loud and turn the game into a shooting gallery as enemies attempt to find me, with my back against a wall and all approaches covered. Ultimately,  the original Sniper Elite V2 wasn't for me -- that's not a knock on my game, simply just a mismatch between my playstyle and game preferences.
Sniper Elite: Nazi Zombie Army was everything I loved about Sniper Elite V2, with an amazingly well-crafted zombie atmosphere. No other zombie game has managed to replicate the dread and imminent doom of the Romero-style zombie -- Left for Dead's rage zombies scamper towards you in waves but drop like paper mâché; Dead Island's zombies are sparse and require a lot of physical damage; Dead Rising zombies ignore you most of the time.  SE:NZA sticks you with the great conundrum of taking the time to properly aim for a headshot, at the risk of the other 10+ zombies getting closer. No other game has induced the same sense of panic when you realize just how badly surround you are -- they're just shambling slowly, how could I possible be surrounded?
The stages themselves are very linear, albeit with extremely large areas for each major wave of attacks. There is room to kite, until the special zombies begin to appear. The suicide explosive zombies felt very unfair -- they're very difficult to deal with if playing single player, given the damage they deliver.  The resurrected skeletons are also a nuisance, but I suppose they force you to reprioritize your plan and backpeddle while shooting.
The fifth area "fetch quest" in the subways was a chore, needlessly extending the game. I did enjoy the fact that these stages are all created from the base Sniper Elite V2 stages, but with much more fog and blood splatter.
Picking up this game at $15 for a 4-pack was a steal, and kept my group of co-op friends occupied for a good two weeks, running one or two stages a night.  There is a lack of replayability -- in fact, I've yet to finish the game, due to the difficulty spike of dealing with the last boss -- which tends to play much better with three players than two.
I can recommend this game for people who are not looking for a hardcore challenge, but rather, a "beatable challenge" with their friends. ~$4 is the right price for this game, but definitely do it with similar-minded friends.

Sniper Elite: Nazi Zombie Army can be an enjoyable game. But it comes with a long list of pretences. First of all, you NEED to have friends who are willing to play this with you. Preferably friends who are fans of Army of Darkness and similar campy zombie movies. Second, you need to know what you're getting into. NZA isn't a smart game, nor is it an original game. It isn't all that much of a good game either. It's just a little something you and your friends can jump into together for a few hours on a boring, rainy Sunday afternoon. For the cheap price you pay, Nazi Zombie Army is not at all a bad purchase in its own right. It is its own, stand-alone game for the price of a Call of Duty map pack. It looks good, has about the same length as Medal of Honor, and it has four-player Co-Op. The problem is just that, in this day and age, when you can get a retail game for the same price during a Steam daily deal, NZA simply does not hold a candle to the competitors. The game isn't great, some will argue that it isn't even good. I had fun with it, but I purchased it knowing what I was getting into. If you're desperate for more Co-operative zombie action, then you might want to try it out. But if you're new to the genre, you might as well pick up Left 4 Dead 2 instead.

Bearing in mind that this is not at all my genre, I found Firewatch to be a welcome change to the hectic rampages of games like Killing Floor 2 and Primal Carnage. Here there was suspense. There was an air of danger, mystery. An adventure. This is not about the skilled gameplay or sharp decision making, it's just a story. You go, you choose, you live. It's more of an interactive film than anything, but it really is a good one. There aren't many games or movies that keep me guessing, but this one had me thinking and wondering even in the end.
The gameplay is purposefully slow to give you time to fester about what is happening and build tension. It's a great game if your mind goes at a million miles per minute and you get worked up easily about misunderstandings. The graphics weren't cutting edge, but the art was beautiful. The world was immersive as long as I stayed on the path, but not being able to climb freely was a downside.
This is the first game I have stayed up this late playing in several years.
10/10 would play again. Contemplating doing some free roam later.

HP Weapon Shop is visually appealing, has a decent sense of humor, and it pulls you in with an interesting premise. I like the idea of being on the other side of the bench and having to make the choices as to what's best for the hero. The jokes are your expected video game pop culture references and they are good for a laugh or two without feeling excessively forced. The game loop of sell weapons, unlock areas, explore area, research weapon & repeat gives a good feeling of progress until it becomes exceedingly repetitive.
The major issues for the game all come about from its lack of depth. Each NPC adventurer requires a weapon with a main stat and a second stat and gives you a few choices of weapons they like. So you just pick the weapon with the highest potential stat for the primary and assign your people to prioritize that stat. It's that simple, every time. There's no strategic choice about your smiths, just assign the highest level ones with the best  stats to the primary. There's no strategic choice about weapons, just pick the one with the highest potential, weapon type has no effect as long as it's one they like. It's so annoyingly simple that you try to mix up weapon types just to be creative but the game doesn't reward you for it, it just wants the highest stats.
Then there are minor frustrations such as the game's interface. The game could really use some means to flag or favorite which NPCs you intend to make weapons for, as I spent a lot of time flipping through the menus to try to remember who exactly wanted what. Research in the late game is frustrating as old research materials stay on top the menu resulting in having to click through (no scroll available) a lengthy list to get to items you can actually use for research. Lastly the awards ceremony just felt broken, being impossible to win in the early game and laughably easy in the late game.
Started the game with a happy vibe, finished it out of determination and left feeling bitter and disappointed.

It used to be only Madagascar that would be the problem country, the one that would close down shipping and borders if anyone so much as had an eyebrow twitch.  Now, it's a world of hurt for you or humanity depending on what difficulty you've chosen to test fate.  The prototype for this game was called "Epidemic 2" and I played it on
and
long ago.  It was a lot more primitive back then and to have it brought up to modern standards with better soundtrack was certainly a treat.  I also loved all the scenarios and what ifs that were built-in by the creator.  This game is great for the inner sadist in you.  Ever wanted to destroy humanity?  Well, here you go!  You can wipe them out with various disease types, or go for the throat with your very own zombie apocalypse that YOU unleash on the world.  They've even got the Planet of the Apes option where you can turn an experimental treatment into a world of simians who destroy labs and bases while humanity dies from whatever symptoms you've chosen.
I like using dysentary, myself.  Dysentary with sneezing, diarrhea, and total organ failure is probably the most brutal way to die if you're a human.
It's well worth the price and you'll find yourself playing it again and again just to win or try other ideas.  One of the most interesting is the Worm infection wherein you don't even have to kill humanity.  You can make them into slaves and win the game by infected everyone to become a worshipper.  Pretty neat spin there and the Christmas scenario has you save humanity with the Worm, bringing everyone back to having emotions after being oppressed and suppressed to drone-like states by the world governments.
Very fun, very worthwhile, check it out.  You won't be disappointed if you like viral apocalypse scenarios.  With tons of achievements and hidden challenges, it's very worth the price and the time you spend playing it.

I'm a little disappointed in the performance. It is an alpha though so, it is to be expected. I have right around the minimum spec as of right now and it is a tad unplayable. I get about 25 fps on average with my laptop overclocked (because it actually requires a decent amount of CPU power). I'll test on my desktop when I actually go home (I'm at my girlfriend's place). Specs are: AMD A8 (quad) overclocked to 2.6 GHz, 8 GB of DDR3, and an 6750m (which is pretty close to the 4800 series in raw performance). If you are having performance problems do not play in first person as it will be disorienting due to the low frame rate! I could definitely play the game chugging along at about 25 fps in third person, but I'll probably just see how my desktop holds up or hold off until the performance is improved.
As for the game itself. The game looks solid thus far. It feels pretty fluid. The scale of the alpha seems to be a bit small but that is also to be expected. There isn't much music yet, still waiting on Naganuma music. The minigames are a bit basic from what I've seen, just races and throwing "gamerballs" into boxes. Haven't taken it online yet, but I assume the game will be more fun with human competitors.
Though I was slightly disappointed with performance, the game is coming along nicely and I'm looking forward to each update! I would still recommend this game but with caution that they might have to wait a while until the game is super playable. I'm still excited for the game and will probably try to play more soon.

If you enjoyed the first game, or sniping games in general, DO NOT GET THIS GAME.
I am so disapointed in this. Sniper Elite V2 is a great game and a blast to play, but this doesn't use anything that made its base game great.
Why they took a game about carefully planning your sniping targets, getting into position, and hiting pinpoint targets and then turned it into a game where you almost never get a chance to snipe anything, I have no idea.
They even taunt you with interesting sniping targets (like skeletons with still beating hearts), except they spawn those in groups of 4 or more, 30 feet away, and they immedatly start running at you.
I paid only $5 for this game and I'm still feeling a bit ripped off.

So far this is the most satisfying co-op Third Person Shooter I have played on PC yet.
I'll go further and say this is my favorite 'co-op shooter' on PC at the moment.
The ballistics showcased on sniping are as fun as they were before (in Sniper Elite V2), with satisfying hits being able to go through 4 zombies or more in 1 shot sometimes. And you feel rewarded for killing multiple enemies at once, as "8-for-1 grenade kill" will pop up with how many points you earned from it.
I could go on, but I'll leave it at that for now. I recommend you buy this game NOW --OR if you're cheap, then wait for it to go on sale (again) for $5.08 or less (like I did). Now, I haven't beat all the levels yet (and there are only 5), BUT seriously, this game is great, you just need to play it with people (even strangers will do!) & I can only imagine the 2nd one will be SLIGHTLY better, lol. Either way, check out Nazi Zombie Army sometime.

Short list... only one thing that was a bit "off" to me:
- Really nicely done little Match 3 puzzle game, with a pretty look and sound to it, a decent story for this type of game, and relaxing play. 2 modes make this enjoyable for "hardcore" players looking for challenge, and "casual" players looking for a light, easy to play, relaxing game. I've played this game A LOT, as you can see from my recorded playtime. I started on it in early access, and did several restarts during the years it's been out. Weirdly enough I never actually finished it, but now that there aren't that many new interesting games coming out, I decided to return to it.

Still it's a flawed gem, and if you like turn-based RPGs with survival elements, you'll probably enjoy it regardless of those flaws.

It's got a few rough around the edges moments, but honestly I think this is the most relaxing game I play. And I play a LOT of similar games (
).
From the best tree-chopping mechanics I've ever seen in a game to just tending my farm or pulling around my cart, even designing a new lift system to pull stuff up a mountainside, it's really really enjoyable.
If you're looking for a fight, DO NOT buy this game. if you're looking for a game that will let you build a complex machine to harvest your crops and then till and plant for you while you turn a crank, just buy it... NOW. Seriously.

After sitting down and looking up some guides on the building mechanics to the game, I can say it's pretty in-depth on that side. It's confusing at first, and your walls/floors won't always snap the way you want them, but bear with it and you learn how to manipulate the snapping pretty well.
At first glance I saw a dead broken game that wasn't worth a cent. This was until I started playing with friends and other folks online, which is where the game truly blooms. It's not the best crafting/survival game out there, but far from the worst.
I would recommend the game on a sale. Not worth $20, but nonetheless a good game if your main focus is creativity with some light survival. Building towns with multiple people is a blast, especially when there's the threat of other players attacking your village or keep.
